We're going to cover basic principal-agents models and take a look at such basic applications of mechanism design as auction theory. Some formal instruments will be introduces: how to work with uncertainty, reminder of nash equilibrium in static simultaneous games.

title: Mathematics and Statistics
description: Mathematics and Statistics is an introduction to mathematics, probability and statistics for graduate studies in economics. It prepares students for graduate economics and econometrics courses. The covered topics include calculus, descriptive statistics, probability, random variables, moments, special probability distributions, distributions of sampling statistics, parameter estimation, hypothesis testing, goodness of fit tests, simulation, and bootstrap. Students apply the data analysis methods with statistical software.

title: Microeconomic Theory II
description: Advanced Microeconomics covers more advanced topics in macro economics. In the first part it covers the decision theory of the consumers, choice rules, the weak axiom of revealed preferences, the compensated law of demand, the substitution and income effects, the Slutsky matrix, rational preferences, utility representations, Sheppard’s Lemma, Roy’s identity, preferences over loteries, the Independence Axiom, the expected utility theorem, risk attitudes, general equilibrium existence and welfare theorems, economies with an infinite horizon and overlapping generation economies. The second part explores advanced topics in auctions, mechanism design, and strategic communication under incomplete information. It begins with auction theory, first-price and second-price auctions, revenue equivalence, and optimal mechanism design. It then examines dynamic games of incomplete information, introducing Perfect Bayesian Equilibrium and its applications to signaling games. Other applications include job market signaling (Spence), adverse selection (Akerlof’s Market for Lemons), strategic information disclosure, and cheap talk models. Finally, the course explores herd behavior, Bayesian persuasion, and advanced monopoly pricing strategies, including price discrimination and its limitations.
prerequisite: ECON 501 Microeconomics (2187) (C- and above) AND ECON 512 Mathematical Economics (2154) (C- and above)

title: Advanced Macroeconomics
description: The course aims to provide students with a comprehensive theoretical and empirical foundation in modern dynamic macroeconomic analysis, progressing systematically from the representative agent RBC framework to the sophisticated HANK models. The curriculum synthesizes rigorous analytical formalization with computational implementation, enabling students to master the theory of dynamic stochastic general equilibrium modeling while developing practical proficiency in model solution techniques, calibration methodologies, and computational tools such as Dynare. The course equips students with the analytical and computational tools necessary to analyze macroeconomic models and contemporary debates in monetary and fiscal policies.

The course will focus on both the theoretical and empirical aspects of econometric methods.

prerequisite: ECON 531 Econometrics (2505) (C- and above)

title: Programming for Economists
description: This course introduces students to Python programming, with an emphasis on its economic and econometric applications. It will focus on numerical programming, data manipulation, data visualization, and relevant applications in economics such as web scraping, geospatial data, and standard econometric methods.
prerequisite: ECON 531 Econometrics (2505) (C- and above)

title: Empirical Finance
description: This course provides a rigorous study of capital markets, integrating theoretical models with empirical observations to analyze financial market structures and functions. Designed for graduate students, it explores financial instruments, portfolio choice theory, and asset pricing models, including CAPM, APT, and market efficiency. Students will develop analytical tools for asset pricing, portfolio management, and investment strategies, gaining essential quantitative and conceptual skills for careers in academia, financial research, and investment management.
prerequisite: ECON 531 Econometrics (2505) (C- and above)

title: Economic Simulation Modeling
description: This course will teach the principles of computable general equilibrium (CGE) modeling and introduce some applications in trade, environmental and energy economics. The course will teach how to build a CGE model using the GAMS software. CGE models are widely applied in international organizations (World Bank, IMF) and research institutions.
prerequisite: ECON 501 Microeconomics (2187) (C- and above)

title: Topics in Applied Economics 1
description: The aim of this course is to present detailed analyses of the main areas in applied economics. The topics covered may vary from year to year and from instructor to another. Such topics may include, but are not limited to, labor economics, industrial organization, development economics, energy economics, health economics, monetary economics, education economics, and public economics. The ultimate objective being to equip students with a solid foundation for undertaking original research in applied economics.
prerequisite: ECON 501 Microeconomics (2187) (C- and above) AND ECON 511 Mathematics and Statistics (2188) (C- and above)

title: Topics in Macroeconomic Theory
description: Topics in Macroeconomic Theory focuses on detailed study of selected topics in macroeconomics.
prerequisite: ECON 502 Macroeconomics (2186) (C- and above)

title: Public Finance
description: This course will familiarize the students with the most important papers in the field of public finance on the topics of government expenditure and taxation.
prerequisite: ECON 501 Microeconomics (2187) (C- and above) OR ECON 413 Econometrics II Time Series (1037) (C- and above) OR ECON 531 Econometrics (2505) (C- and above)

title: Advanced Game Theory: Mechanism Design
description: This course is an advanced course in Game Theory, with a particular focus on the theory of Mechanism Design. Mechanism Design is a subfield of economics dedicated to the construction of economic mechanisms, including rules, environments, and institutions, with desirable properties. While traditional microeconomic analysis seeks to understand how agents behave within established frameworks, Mechanism Design aims to design 'suitable' rules that lead to 'desirable' outcomes.
prerequisite: ECON 501 Microeconomics (2187) (B and above) AND ECON 512 Mathematical Economics (2154) (B and above) AND ECON 521 Microeconomic Theory II (2506) (B and above)

title: Structural Methods in Market Design
description: This course covers many empirical methods used in research in market design and empirical industrial organization. We will use recent published papers to guide our study of these methods. We will cover five main topics (listed below). For each of these topics, students will learn models employed by economists and estimate those models using real economic data and the econometric techniques covered in class.
prerequisite: ECON 501 Microeconomics (2187) (B and above) AND ECON 512 Mathematical Economics (2154) (B and above) AND ECON 531 Econometrics (2505) (B and above)

title: Quantitative Macroeconomics
description: This course has a dual aim. First, it provides an overview of workhorse modern dynamic equilibrium macroeconomic models that are relevant for actual empirical and quantitative policy analysis. Usually, these theoretical models do not have an analytical solution, and drawing their practical quantitative implications requires resorting to computational techniques. As the second aim, this course thus introduces computational methods for solving and simulating macroeconomic models.
prerequisite: ECON 502 Macroeconomics (2186) (C- and above) AND ECON 532 Applied Econometrics (2977) (C- and above)

title: Mathematical Finance
description: The course aims to cover knowledge of basic financial actuarial models with applications and to prepare students pass the actuarial financial economics (MFE) exam.

The aim of the course is to introduce the students to nonlinear circuits in application to newer computing architectures, and brain like processing circuits. The course expects the students to prepare the students for graduate studies in the area of circuit design.

title: Special Topics in Signal Processing

Topics of study include characteristics of the mobile radio environment, propagation phenomena, cellular concept and channel allocation, dynamic channel allocation and power control, multiple access techniques

description: This course aims at making the students thorough about different varieties of power generation technologies, and the relevant economic analysis to make them directly fit into the power industry requirements in Kazakhstan.

title: Photonics for Engineering
description: This course is designed to provide students with a complete overview of photonics, which represents an essential prerequisite for advanced courses like Optical Communication and Optical Sensors. During this course the fundamental laws of optics will be explained. A particular attention will be spent to describe the formalism of ray and wave optics. A deep explanation of guided optics will be delivered, focusing on guiding structures like dielectric slabs and optical fibers. Passive and active photonic components including: couplers, circulators, interferometers, gratings, modulators, LEDs, lasers and photodetectors will be presented and fully described. Furthermore, for each of the previous topics, the attention will be focus both on theory and on applications. A CAD numerical laboratory will be included in the course.

description: This elective course will introduce artificial intelligence based algorithms to students vis-a-vis their applications to power system analysis. The intelligent algorithms to be included are Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) based algorithms, Fuzzy Logic and Genetic Algorithms. Analysis of power systems shall include load flow analysis, load forecasting, and power system stabilizers.

description: This is an undergraduate-level course manly designed to introduce various optimization techniques that can serve as efficient tools in solving unconstrained and constrained problems in engineering domain. The course will include implementation assignments to help students nurture their understanding of the concepts taught and prepare them to identify and model problems that can be optimized in real-world scenarios.

title: Analog Circuit Design
description: This course focuses on the schematic and physical design of analog integrated circuits. The specific focus is on the circuits such as current mirrors, amplifiers, operational amplifiers, PLLs and mixers.

title: Introduction to Big Data
description: The course will provide an introduction to various machine learning techniques for analyzing big data.

title: Internet of Things
description: This course introduces different aspects of IoT development such as sensor data collection, edge computing, cloud computing, different communication protocols used in IoT etc. It is a project based course and high emphasis is given to hands-on training. Students will start with sensor data processing using Arduino, edge computing with Raspberry pi and use cloud services such as Amazon AWS for connecting to the cloud and data processing in the cloud.

title: Deep Learning Machines
description: This elective course will introduce deep learning algorithms and its hardware implementations in digital and analog hardware, and develop the understanding through a practical IoT application.

title: Industry 4.0
description: This elective course will introduce industry 4.0 which is the current trend of automation and data exchange in manufacturing technologies through Cyber Physical System (CPS). Cyber Physical System (CPS) is the enabling technologies that make multiple innovative application processes a reality where the boundaries between the real and virtual worlds disappear.

title: Modern Characterizations for Semiconductor Industry
description: This is a new elective course for students who are interested in semiconductor materials and devices. Students will gain the fundamental knowledge and practical hands-on experience for characterizing semiconductor materials and devices. This course will also equip students with important scientific skills for their future research and career in semiconductor industry.

title: Fundamentals of Biomedical Engineering and Biophysics
description: This elective course will introduce fundamentals and insights on the relevant biological and engineering related issues including complex cell culture and structure, extracellular matrix biochemistry and tissue organization, muscle and bone regeneration, scaffold fabrication and nanoscopic optical and topographical characterization. Course is open to upper level undergraduate students enrolled in Bachelor programs in Engineering, Physics and Biology.

title: Signal Processing for Communications
description: The students will acquire knowledge on the signal processing techniques and approaches in the field of wireless communication networks. In addition to the knowledge on the concept of cellular networks and MIMO systems, the students will be able to apply various signal processing methods based on the typical features and bottlenecks of different communication techniques and their combinations. Also, the students will be trained on how to implement signal processing techniques in the communication systems in a computer.

description: The fundamentals and practice of computer networks, with emphasis on the Internet. The structure and components of computer networks, packet switching, layered architectures, TCP/IP, physical layer, error control, window flow control, local area networks (Ethernet, Token Ring, Token Bus, DQDB and FDDI), network layer, congestion control, and quality of service.

Next Generation Substation Automation Systems
description: Substation data communication system plays a critical role in the real time mission critical operation of substation automation systems. All secondary equipment within a substation is interlinked with communication buses. In conventional substation, legacy communication devices typically rely on one-way communication. Serial communication buses or proprietary communication media with associated protocols are used for local HMI, as well as for remote SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) communication. Modern communication substations are data transmitted between station, bay and process levels. The data information includes control, report, log GOOSE, SV, etc. Communication between these three levels is called vertical communication and connected by high-speed Ethernet station bus and process bus. Station bus facilitates communication between station level and bay level. Process bus is used for time critical messages between process level and bay level. Most of the substation functions will rely on the performance of the process bus. Communication within one level is horizontal communication. In station levels, the time based data from multiple bays or substation level database will be analyzed and processed. The control commands for the primary equipment will be submitted and data like voltage, current and power factor will be collected. In bay level, units collect data from bays and perform actions on the primary (e.g. power circuit) equipment. In process level, performance and condition information are read from essential station equipment. Control commands from bay level will be received and executed in the equipment at the process level. Currently, there are over 50 communication protocols for legacy substation automation systems. These include Modbus, TCP, ProfiNet, Ethernet IP, OPC-DA, and LON. Many of these topologies are vendor specified and have serial interface, low bandwidth, limited network devices, serial interfaces and inflexible data, etc. Their communication architecture does not fit to the corporate communication technology and are not able to expend the network. Most representative protocols are DNP3 and IEC 60870-5-104. Both of them are master/slave based fieldbus communication and can only be implemented till station level and bay level. Nowadays many substation vendors are moving away from serial to Ethernet based IEC 61850 which is a client/server communication standard. It fully supports the interoperability among IEDs supplied by different vendors in the substation and can be applied also in the process level of substation automation.

title: Industrial Power System Protection & Relaying
description: The function of industrial protective relaying is to cause the prompt removal from service of any element of a power system when it suffers a short circuit, or when it starts to operate in any abnormal manner that might cause damage or otherwise interfere with the effective operation of the rest of the system. The relaying equipment is aided in this task by circuit breakers that are capable of disconnecting the faulty element when they are called upon to do so by the relaying equipment. Circuit breakers are generally located so that each generator, transformer, bus, transmission line, etc., can be completely disconnected from the rest of the system. These circuit breakers must have sufficient capacity so that they can carry momentarily the maximum short-circuit current that can flow through them, and then interrupt this current; they must also withstand closing in on such a short circuit and then interrupting it according to certain prescribed standards. Fusing is employed where protective relays and circuit breakers are not economically justifiable. A secondary function of protective relaying is to provide indication of the location and type of failure. Such data not only assist in expediting repair but also, by comparison with human observation and automatic oscillograph records, they provide means for analyzing the effectiveness of the fault-prevention and mitigation features including the protective relaying itself.

title: Advanced Smart Grids & Future Energy Cities
description: The world’s electricity systems face a number of challenges, including ageing infrastructure, continued growth in demand, the integration of increasing numbers of variable renewable energy sources and electric vehicles, the need to improve the security of supply and the need to lower carbon emissions. Smart grid technologies offer ways not just to meet these challenges but also to develop a cleaner energy supply that is more energy efficient, more affordable and more sustainable. These challenges must also be addressed with regard to each region’s unique technical, financial and commercial regulatory environment. Given the highly regulated nature of the electricity system, proponents of smart grids must ensure that they engage with all stakeholders, including equipment manufacturers, system operators, consumer advocates and consumers, to develop tailored technical, financial and regulatory solutions that enable the potential of smart grids. Making a city “smart” is emerging as a strategy to mitigate the problems generated by the urban population growth and rapid urbanization. More than half of the world’s population now lives in urban areas. This shift from a primarily rural to a primarily urban population is projected to continue. Cities, megacities, generate new kinds of problems. Difficulty in waste management, scarcity of resources, air pollution, human health concerns, traffic congestions, and inadequate, deteriorating and aging infrastructures are among the more basic technical, physical, and material problems. The urgency around these challenges is triggering many cities around the world to find smarter ways to manage them. These cities are increasingly described with the label ‘smart city’ which basically is a city that monitors and integrates conditions of all of its critical infrastructures, including roads, bridges, tunnels, rails, subways, airports, seaports, communications, water, power, even major buildings, to better optimize its resources, plan its preventive maintenance activities, and monitor all security aspects while maximizing services to its citizens.

description: This module provides in-depth exposure to analytic and simulation techniques appropriate for the representation, analysis and performance evaluation of communications systems and networks

title: Optical Transport & Networks Elective
description: Fibre optic networks in telecommunications systems.

title: Information Theory for Communications
description: This module covers fundamental concepts in information theory relevant to communication systems. It builds on students' existing knowledge in probability and statistical theory, as well as communication theory, to equip them with new knowledge and perspective to advance their study in the course of ICT.

title: 4th year English
description: Course required by all 4th year students, who do not show proof of current IELTS requirement overall 6.5 (with no sections less than 6.0).

title: Introduction to Electrical Circuits
description: This is the first course on electrical circuit theme and covers three distinct circuit aspects. The first part of the course deals with the circuit analysis techniques, circuit theorems, various combination on RLC circuits and their responses, and phase relationship for R, L, and C, Impedance and Admittance. The second part of the course deals with Semiconductor diode, Zener diode, Rectifier Circuits, Clipper and Clamper Circuits, and other wave shaping circuits. The third and final component of this course covers Magnetic circuits, mutually coupled circuits, Transformers, and equivalent circuits and their performance.
prerequisite: MATH 162 Calculus II (170) (C- and above) AND PHYS 162 Physics II for Scientists and Engineers with Laboratory (173) (C- and above)

title: Circuit Theory
description: The objective of this course is to build on the tools and techniques learnt in ELCE 200 Circuit Theory I course. A tentative list of topics includes: Review of Basic Circuit Analysis, Operational Amplifiers-based circuit analysis, Second-Order Circuits and Three-Phase Circuits, Frequency Response of Active Filters, Application of Laplace Transform for Circuit Analysis, Circuit Application using Fourier Analysis, Two-port Networks.
prerequisite: ELCE 200 Introduction to Electrical Circuits (4991) (C- and above)

title: Circuit Theory Laboratory
description: The objective of this course is to provide hands-on laboratory training in circuit theory, design and analysis methods to students taking the accompanying core ELCE 200 Circuit Theory I and ELCE 201 Circuit Theory II courses.
corequisite: ELCE 201 Circuit Theory (5507) (D and above)

title: Digital Logic Design
description: This course presents the introductory concepts that are needed in order to design digital systems including combinational and sequential digital logic, and state machines. Concepts of Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps, flip-flops, registers, and counters along with various logic families and comparison of their behavior and characteristics are covered. Additionally this course presents an introduction of the Hardware description language (VHDL) and introduce students to design combinational and sequential circuits using VHDL and simulators.
prerequisite: MATH 162 Calculus II (170) (C- and above) AND PHYS 162 Physics II for Scientists and Engineers with Laboratory (173) (C- and above) AND ENG 101 Programming for Engineers (4517) (C- and above)

title: Digital Logic Design Laboratory
description: A co-requisite laboratory course (accompanying ELCE 206 Digital Logic Design), covering practical aspects of digital system design. This course introduces basic wiring and hardware interfacing techniques, exposes students to state-of-the-art design applications and techniques using Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA), and covers design using hardware description languages (HDL).
corequisite: ELCE 202 Digital Logic Design (4992) (D and above)

title: Signals and Systems
description: The objective of this course is to introduce fundamental properties of linear systems and transform techniques to analyze the behavior of linear systems. Students are also expected to gain an appreciation for the importance of linear system theory in electrical engineering.
prerequisite: MATH 162 Calculus II (170) (C- and above) AND PHYS 162 Physics II for Scientists and Engineers with Laboratory (173) (C- and above)

title: Signals and Systems Laboratory
description: The objective of this course is to train students by providing comprehensive practical (laboratory) works on the fundamental properties of linear systems and transform techniques to analyze the behavior of linear systems. Students are also expected to gain an appreciation for the importance of linear system theory in electrical engineering.
corequisite: ELCE 203 Signals and Systems (4993) (D and above)

title: Solid State Devices
description: This course focuses on the semiconductor device physics for engineering students. The contents will cover the knowledge of semiconductor materials, semiconductor models, carrier actions, p-n junctions, ohmic & schottky contacts, diodes, solar cells, LEDs, MOS capacitors and transistors. The working mechanism of the semiconductor devices will be taught. Students will gain the knowledge from the lectures and consolidate the learned concepts by performing experiments in labs and solving problems in tutorials. The performance of the students will be assessed by exercises, quizzes, midterm, lab reports and the final exam.
prerequisite: ENG 103 Engineering Materials II (4818) (C- and above)

title: Solid State Devices Laboratory
description: This lab course complements the Solid-State Devices lectures. Students gain practical experience in emerging semiconductor material processing and characterization techniques. Thin film deposition methods like spin coating and various vacuum deposition will be taught. Equipment such as spin coaters, furnaces and various deposition systems will be used. Students fabricate and analyze devices such as diodes, LEDs and solar cells. Characterization includes material and device characterization techniques. In this lab course, students learn how material growth and their impact on device performance. This course prepares students for their careers in semiconductor research and engineering.
prerequisite: ENG 103 Engineering Materials II (4818) (C- and above)
corequisite: ELCE 204 Solid State Devices (5508) (D and above)

title: Discrete Mathematics
description: The aim of this course is to introduce students to a mathematical way of thinking that can serve them in variety of situations, particularly in expressing their mathematical ideas clearly, precisely, and unambiguously. The main themes of a first course in discrete mathematics are logic and proof, induction and recursion, discrete structures, combinatorics and discrete probability, algorithms and their analysis, and applications and modeling. The content is supported with examples from electrical and computer engineering practices such as digital circuit design, network analysis, encoding/decoding messages, cryptography etc.
prerequisite: MATH 162 Calculus II (170) (C- and above)

title: Microprocessor Systems
description: This course provides an overview of microcontrollers, as well as select topics in computer architecture and embedded systems. Students will develop an appreciation for the role of hardware in computer operations; an understanding of microcontrollers, microprocessors, and embedded systems; and will be able to design, write, and debug assembly language and C-language programs for microcontrollers using a state-of-the-art integrated development environment.
prerequisite: ELCE 202 Digital Logic Design (4992) (C- and above)

title: Microprocessor Systems Laboratory
description: This course provides students with hands on skills in programming and application development with microprocessors. In this course, students conduct experiments using microprocessor kits and experiment boards. The major subjects that are covered include assembly language programming, interfacing to external devices (serial/parallel as well as analog devices through DAC/ADC), interfacing memory and troubleshooting.
corequisite: ELCE 300 Microprocessor Systems (6183) (C- and above)

title: Electronic Circuits
description: The course focuses on building the ability to analyze and design electronic circuits. This course starts with an overview of semiconductor technology.
prerequisite: ELCE 201 Circuit Theory (5507) (C- and above)

title: Electronic Circuits Laboratory
description: The objective of this course is to provide hands-on laboratory training in analysis and electronic circuits design to students taking the accompanying core ELCE 301 Electronic Circuits course.
prerequisite: ELCE 201L Circuit Theory Laboratory (6179) (C- and above)
corequisite: ELCE 301 Electronic Circuits (5918) (C- and above)

title: Electric Machines
description: General purpose of the course is to have the students exposed to the fundamentals of magnetics and electromagnetic energy conversion and its applications to basic electrical machines and drives. Topics covered include: Electromagnetism and magnetic circuits, magnetic losses, self and mutual inductances, permanent magnet, and production of voltage and force. DC machines, Transformers, Three-phase induction machines, Synchronous machines and some special purpose machines.
prerequisite: ELCE 201 Circuit Theory (5507) (C- and above)

title: Electrical Machines Laboratory
description: Objective of this course is to provide hands-on laboratory training in the analysis and the characterization of electrical machines to students taking the accompanying core ELCE 302 Electrical Machines course.
prerequisite: ELCE 201 Circuit Theory (5507) (C- and above)
corequisite: ELCE 302 Electric Machines (5919) (C- and above)

title: Power System Analysis
description: Power system analysis is the core knowledge required for understanding, planning, and operating a power system. This unit introduces students to the core knowledge of power systems analysis and modelling.
prerequisite: ELCE 200 Introduction to Electrical Circuits (4991) (C- and above)

title: Power System Analysis Laboratory
description: The power system analysis laboratory course aims to bridge theory and application by training students on real networks using actual equipment. It enables hands-on experiments, issue troubleshooting, and application of lecture theories. This practical course enhances understanding of concepts, their real-world application, and addressing challenges like voltage instability and power losses. The course covers diverse power system analysis concepts, such as modeling, power factor correction, per-unit analysis, load flow, Gauss-Seidel, Newton-Raphson techniques, and software-based network modeling.
prerequisite: ELCE 200 Introduction to Electrical Circuits (4991) (C- and above)
corequisite: ELCE 303 Power System Analysis (6180) (D and above)

title: Computer Networks
description: Computer networking is a major field of study in computer engineering. This course aims to introduce students to the basic networking principles including protocols, architectures and layered network models with focus mainly on the OSI layers and the relevant protocols. In addition to theory, the students will gain hands-on experience in configuring and setting up small-scale networks, socket programming, proxies, firewalls, and exploiting wireless protocols in IoT which are skills highly valued in the market.
prerequisite: ENG 101 Programming for Engineers (4517) (C- and above)

title: Computer Networks Laboratory
description: This course provides students with hands on skills in design, modeling and evaluation of computer networks. In this course, students conduct experiments using modeling tools and learn about network design topics including multiple access protocols, switched LANs, IP addressing, routing protocols (RIP, OSPF, BGP), transport layer protocols (TCP/UDP) and others.
corequisite: ELCE 304 Computer Networks (5920) (D and above)

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: This undergraduate-level course introduces several highly efficient algorithms and data structures for fundamental computational problems across various engineering areas. This course should be of interest to students in computer engineering and related fields, especially those with a mathematical bent of mind. Familiarity with basic material in algorithms, programming, and probability theory is expected. The performance of the students will be assessed by lab reports and assignments, quizzes, midterm, and the final exam.
prerequisite: CSCI 151 Programming for Scientists and Engineers (192) (C- and above) OR ENG 101 Programming for Engineers (4517) (C- and above)

title: Linear Control Theory
description: This course covers basics of control system theory, analysis and design. The course covers topics such as Transfer functions; Stability; Dynamic and steady-state performance; Root locus diagrams; Bode plots; Cascade compensation using root locus and frequency response techniques, Introduction to state-space modelling and analysis, and Analysis and design of PID control systems.
prerequisite: ELCE 203 Signals and Systems (4993) (C- and above)

title: Linear Control Theory Lab
description: The course provides access to the basic design and analysis tools used in practical control systems.
prerequisite: ELCE 203L Signals and Systems Laboratory (6182) (C- and above)
corequisite: ELCE 306 Linear Control Theory (5949) (D and above)

title: Digital Signal Processing
description: This course provides a core grounding in the analysis of discrete-time signals and linear time-invariant (LTI) systems in both time and frequency domains. Furthermore, it aims to develop fundamental techniques in designing digital filter for practical applications. The performance of the students will be assessed by exercises, quizzes, midterm, lab reports and the final exam.
prerequisite: ELCE 203 Signals and Systems (4993) (C- and above)

title: Digital Signal Processing Laboratory
description: To train students by providing comprehensive practical (laboratory) works on DSP fundamentals and filter design techniques.
prerequisite: ELCE 203 Signals and Systems (4993) (C- and above) AND ELCE 203L Signals and Systems Laboratory (6182) (C- and above)
corequisite: ELCE 307 Digital Signal Processing (5921) (D and above)

title: Communication Systems
description: This course covers a wide range of topics in analog and digital communication systems including; amplitude modulation types and demodulation, angle modulation and demodulation, sampling and quantization, additive white Gaussian noise, and baseband and passband digital modulation techniques. Laboratory assignments train students in design aspects and performance analysis of different systems, techniques and methods in modern communication systems.
prerequisite: ELCE 203 Signals and Systems (4993) (C- and above)

title: Communication Systems Laboratory
description: This laboratory course offers a comprehensive investigation of communication system fundamentals. Through a series of hands-on labs, students will gain practical experience in signal analysis, modulation and demodulation techniques, and digital signal processing. The labs cover various topics including spectrum analysis, amplitude and frequency modulation, analog to digital conversion, and digital baseband modulations. By the end of the course, students will have a solid understanding of key concepts in communication systems and the ability to apply them in real-world scenarios.
prerequisite: ELCE 203 Signals and Systems (4993) (C- and above)
corequisite: ELCE 308 Communication Systems (5922) (D and above)

title: Individual Study
description: This course is designed to be a lead-in to the Year 4 capstone project of student studies, during which students will develop necessary skills that would make their capstone project successful. The course covers literature review, independent research, and methods of applying existing knowledge and skills to solving an engineering problem.

title: Electronics Instrumentation and Measurement
description: This course is designed for year 3 bachelor students. The students will learn the fundamentals of electronic instrumentation and measurements with the understanding of how to use basic circuit components to build electronic circuits and systems; and also conduct measurements. They would also learn how to operate basic measurement instruments such as power supplies, function generators, oscilloscopes, multimeters, network analyzers and spectrum analyzers. This course is a full hands-on laboratory course.
prerequisite: ELCE 201 Circuit Theory (5507) (C- and above)
corequisite: ELCE 301 Electronic Circuits (5918) (C- and above)

title: Interdisciplinary Design Project
description: This course prepares students for the Year 4 capstone project by honing skills in report writing, research, and LaTeX typesetting. It offers hands-on labs covering electrical circuits and PCB design. Students present findings and submit a final report, showcasing growth and insights. Graduates emerge as skilled electronics enthusiasts, researchers, and adept report writers, well-prepared for their Year 4 capstone projects.
antirequisite: ENG 400 Capstone Project (6385) (C- and above)

title: Electromagnetics I
description: The Electromagnetics course explores electromagnetic wave propagation in free space and guided structures, focusing on its practical engineering applications. Five key components are covered: Maxwell's equations, transmission line analysis via Smith-chart methodology, wave propagation in open space and within waveguides and dielectric media, and an introduction to antennas and radars. The course emphasizes real-world applications in telecommunications, data transmission, and sensor technologies.
prerequisite: PHYS 162 Physics II for Scientists and Engineers with Laboratory (173) (C- and above) AND ENG 200 Engineering Mathematics III (Differential Equations and Linear Algebra) (5009) (C- and above) AND ELCE 200 Introduction to Electrical Circuits (4991) (C- and above)

title: Applied Simulation Laboratory
description: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of MATLAB/SIMULINK for modeling, simulating, and analyzing electrical systems. From circuits to control systems, students gain practical skills through lab sessions and theoretical explanations, ensuring a thorough understanding of the subject matter.
prerequisite: ELCE 200 Introduction to Electrical Circuits (4991) (D+ and above)

title: Power Electronics
description: This course covers the fundamentals and applications of power electronics, focusing on AC-DC, DC-DC, and DC-AC converters. Students will learn to analyze and simulate converter performance, understand semiconductor devices, and develop hands-on skills through labs and simulation tools. The course prepares students for advanced study and careers in energy systems, electric vehicles, and industrial automation.
prerequisite: ELCE 201 Circuit Theory (5507) (D and above)

title: Power Systems Protection
description: This course introduces students to the fundamentals of power systems protection and relaying. It discusses the types of faults and their calculation using symmetrical components methods; electromechanical relay principles; relaying transducers - voltage and current transformers; transmission line protection - overcurrent, directional, distance, out-of-step protection; primary and backup protection zones, discrimination of relay time and current settings.
prerequisite: ELCE 303 Power System Analysis (6180) (D and above)

title: Internship
description: Students in the Electrical and Computer Engineering department have an opportunity to complete a credit-bearing internship from the third year onwards either with a company located in Kazakhstan or abroad, or at a research institution. The number of contact hours should be no less than 200.

title: Introduction to Adaptive Signal Processing
description: This course provides the mathematical framework for an understanding of adaptive statistical signal processing, introduces various types of adaptive filters and their properties, and basic tools of vector spaces, optimization theory, and discrete-time stochastic processes.
prerequisite: ELCE 307 Digital Signal Processing (5921) (C- and above)

title: Modern Characterizations for Semiconductor Industry
description: This course is designed for year 4 bachelor students. The students will learn the fundamentals of semiconductor material properties with understanding the material as well as device characterizations. Different state-of-the-art characterizations techniques including electrical, optical, chemical and physical methods will be introduced. This course is delivered by lecture and lab sessions.
corequisite: ELCE 204 Solid State Devices (5508) ( and above)

title: Electric Drives and Motion Control Systems
description: The aim of this course is to equip students with knowledge of variable-speed drives and motion control systems which are used in many industrial processes such as in conveyors, machine tools, pumps, compressors, mining drives, electric vehicles, ship propulsion, wind energy systems, air-craft actuators, servo drives and automation systems, to name a few.
prerequisite: ELCE 302 Electric Machines (5919) (C- and above) OR EEE 381 Electrical Machines and Drives (1952) (C- and above) OR ROBT 304 Electromechanical Systems with lab (1171) (C- and above)

title: Renewable Energy and Electric Vehicles
description: The course aims to provide the students with the fundamentals of energy conversion and renewable energy generation along with resources, and renewable energy sites and potential recognition. Solar, wind, photovoltaic, geothermal, wave, tidal, micro-hydro generation along with Electric Vehicles (EVs), battery energy storage systems and DC/AC conversion systems and equipment, design, fabrication, calculation and their operation would be discussed in this course.
prerequisite: ELCE 200 Introduction to Electrical Circuits (4991) (C- and above)

title: High Voltage, AC/DC, FACTS Devices
description: This course is designed to provide knowledge and understanding along with design proficiency for electrical and high voltage apparatus. It will cover large power systems in interconnected physical networks, different types of equipment and apparatus, synchronous generators, power transformers, overhead transmission lines design and structure and insulation coordination, underground cables, metering and control equipment, switchgear for connection or disconnection, high-voltage insulators, AC/DC devices, flexible alternating current transmission system (FACTS) as static equipment used for the AC transmission of electrical energy, and high voltage direct current transmission (HVDC) systems as well as high voltage power electronics-based devices.
prerequisite: ELCE 201 Circuit Theory (5507) (C- and above)

title: Power Transmission and Distribution Systems
description: The course is designed to provide the fundamental and key knowledge on generation, transmission and distribution in power systems as well as electrical industrial power systems: design, construction, maintenance, load calculation, management and operation. It will also provide essential knowledge on renewable energy and its calculations along with microgrid and distributed generation concept.
prerequisite: ELCE 201 Circuit Theory (5507) (C- and above)

title: Machine Learning with Python
description: This course introduces a hands-on approach to machine learning principles and techniques using Python.
prerequisite: ENG 101 Programming for Engineers (4517) (C- and above) OR CSCI 151 Programming for Scientists and Engineers (192) (C- and above)

title: Internet of Things
description: This course provides a core grounding in how science and technology have developed to enable the Internet of Things (IoT) – in a way appropriate for any learner. For those interested in developing further hands-on expertise in designing and developing for the Internet of Things, this course will provide a context to the discoveries and converging technologies that will springboard the next round of innovations.
prerequisite: ELCE 304 Computer Networks (5920) (C- and above) OR CSCI 333 Computer Networks (1145) (C- and above)

title: Introduction to Computer Vision
description: This course introduces the basic methodologies and theories of digital image processing and computer vision.
prerequisite: ENG 101 Programming for Engineers (4517) (C- and above) AND ENG 200 Engineering Mathematics III (Differential Equations and Linear Algebra) (5009) (C- and above)

title: Numerical Optimization Techniques and Computer Applications
description: This is an undergraduate-level course manly designed to introduce various optimization techniques that can serve as efficient tools in solving unconstrained and constrained problems in engineering domain. The course will include implementation assignments to help students nurture their understanding of the concepts taught and prepare them to identify and model problems that can be optimized in real-world scenarios.
prerequisite: ENG 200 Engineering Mathematics III (Differential Equations and Linear Algebra) (5009) (C- and above)

title: Design of Application Specific Electronic Circuits
description: This course trains the students in the design schemes and skills required for electronic circuits in broad range of industrial applications. Students will also learn standard software tools (such as ADS, CST, Cadence etc) used for Circuit Analysis.
prerequisite: ELCE 301 Electronic Circuits (5918) (C- and above)

title: Introduction to Computer Architecture
description: Introduction to computer architecture including examples of current approaches and the effect of technology and software. Computer performance evaluation, basic combinatorial and sequential digital components, different instruction set architectures with a focus on the RISC-V. Evolution of CPU microarchitecture from time-multiplexed to multi-cycle pipelines.
prerequisite: ELCE 300 Microprocessor Systems (6183) (C- and above)

title: Industrial Automation
description: This course provides fundamental concepts of the automation in industry and covers related programming languages. In this course students will learn about CODESYS environment as a universal compiler for many automation and PLC modules as well as Siemens platforms. This course will prepare students to find opportunities in industry and develop their career in future.
prerequisite: ELCE 202 Digital Logic Design (4992) (C- and above)

title: Industrial Automation Laboratory
description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of industrial automation and explores relevant programming languages. Students will learn how to apply the knowledge gained in industrial automation to PLCs and hardware. This course will equip students to pursue opportunities in the industry and advance their careers in the future.
corequisite: ELCE 461 Industrial Automation (7020) (D and above)

title: Wireless Networks
description: This course covers fundamental technologies of mobile information systems and wireless communication networks. It also provides a core grounding in how science and technology have developed to enable Wireless Networks. In addition, this course will provide a context to the discoveries and converging technologies that will springboard the next round of innovations.
prerequisite: ENG 201 Applied Probability and Statistics (5505) (C- and above) AND (ELCE 308 Communication Systems (5922) (C- and above) OR ELCE 304 Computer Networks (5920) (C- and above))

title: Network Science: Methods and Applications
description: Network science is a framework to analyze the complex systems of technological, biological, and societal networks. The purpose of this undergraduate senior-year course is to present the fundamentals of networks, and mathematical toolsets to study and characterize networked data, and develop skills for network thinking. Students will also be exposed to current research in the field, and they will be given an opportunity to explore a chosen topic through a semester project.
prerequisite: ENG 101 Programming for Engineers (4517) (C- and above) AND MATH 162 Calculus II (170) (C- and above) AND ENG 200 Engineering Mathematics III (Differential Equations and Linear Algebra) (5009) (C- and above)

title: PCB Design and Manufacturing
description: This course trains students in printed circuit board (PCB) design, covering digital electronics, analog circuits, schematic capture, and design for manufacturability. Students design and fabricate their own PCBs with industry-standard software and tools. They also learn 3D design to visualize electronic components and circuits. At the end of the course, students will have a good understanding of PCB design principles and practical experience designing and prototyping their own PCBs.

title: RF and Microwave Circuits
description: This course is designed to train the students in the domain of RF and Microwave circuits & systems design techniques for radio communications leading towards the advancements in the domain of advanced radio technology. The focus of the radio technology concepts treated in this course is on the consumer electronics (5G and beyond) and aerospace electronics segments. This course starts with the fundamentals of RF and Microwave Circuits and will equip the students with the requisite tools and techniques to analyze and design moderately complex building blocks operating at high frequencies. The project is essential component and will enable the student in learning a standard commercial CAD simulator used in industry.

title: Modern Wireless Communications
description: Modern wireless communications course offers a deep dive into wireless technology. Topics include history, core principles, spectrum regulations, transmission basics, and multiple access methods. Students explore wireless architectures, channel challenges, and communication quality metrics. The course also covers system optimization, advanced topics, emerging technology, and wireless protocols. It concludes with future trends (6G, security, edge/cloud computing). By the end of this course, students will be well-prepared to navigate the ever-evolving world of wireless communications, contribute to cutting-edge developments, and address the complex challenges in this dynamic field.
prerequisite: ELCE 350 Electromagnetics I (7464) (C- and above)

title: Robots For Rehabilitation
description: This course will cover software modelling of the human musculoskeletal system that will be used to design robotic exoskeletons to assist in the rehabilitation of neurological and sports injuries.

title: Microfluidics Fundamentals and Applications
description: The objective of this course is to introduce students to fundamentals and applications of microfluidics. The course will provide knowledge on physics and theory of microfluidic principles, micro-/nano-fabrication of polymer microfluidic devices, materials and microfluidic components, and a wide range of applications of microfluidics through lectures and research case studies.
prerequisite: PHYS 162 Physics II for Scientists and Engineers with Laboratory (173) (C- and above) AND MATH 162 Calculus II (170) (C- and above)

title: Optical Communications
description: The Optical Communications course provides an in-depth overview of fiber-optic communications for high bit-rate and high-throughput. The course provides a description of fiber-optic communication networks. Starting from an in-depth analysis of the devices that are fundamental part of the optical communication network, such as single mode optical fibers, fiber amplifiers, optical switches, filters, multiplexers, and photodetectors, the course aims to set the basis for assessment of network performance and for the consequent network design. The effect of attenuation, dispersion, and non-linearities will be quantified and standard methods of compensation of those effects will be discussed. Protocols for 10-100 Gbit/s data communication over long-haul links are discussed. New trends on signal modulations, applied to optical communication, will be exposed as an overview of future optical fibers networks.
prerequisite: ELCE 203 Signals and Systems (4993) (C- and above)

title: Photonics for Engineering
description: This course is designed to provide students with a complete overview of photonics, which represents an essential prerequisite for advanced courses like Optical Communication and Optical Sensors. During this course the fundamental laws of optics will be explained. A particular attention will be spent to describe the formalism of ray and wave optics. A deep explanation of guided optics will be delivered, focusing on guiding structures like dielectric slabs and optical fibers. Passive and active photonic components including couplers, circulators, interferometers, gratings, modulators, LEDs, lasers and photodetectors will be presented and fully described. Furthermore, for each of the previous topics, the attention will be focus both on theory and on applications. A CAD numerical laboratory will be included in the course.
prerequisite: MATH 162 Calculus II (170) (C- and above) AND PHYS 162 Physics II for Scientists and Engineers with Laboratory (173) (C- and above)

title: Thesis
description: This course provides EMBA students with an opportunity to apply concepts and tools learned during the program to improve their own companies. Through coursework and by engaging with various parties in their organizations, students identify a thesis topic. Faculty and staff work closely with students to provide coaching and subject matter expertise, as well as monitor progress until the final thesis is submitted.

title: Entrepreneurial Finance
description: This course is designed to introduce students to the ways in which entrepreneurs in western capital markets raise money to launch businesses.

title: International Finance
description: This course provides an introduction to international finance and multinational financial management practices. The course provides insights into the connections between the theoretical determinants of international finance and the realities of international financial management.

title: Pricing
description: This course covers fundamental analytic tools, theories, and conceptual tools for formulating pricing strategy. The course also covers pricing tactics, and some new economy pricing models.

title: Project Management
description: The project management course focuses on principles, tools and techniques required for successful management of projects. Using the framework of project life cycle, the course covers various aspects pertaining to (i) project valuation and selection, (ii) project planning and scheduling, (iii) project monitoring and control and (iv) risk management. Scheduling of projects with resource limitations, role of incentives in project management, and project contracting are also included. Moreover, an overview of Agile Project Management, Organization Structure and project management approaches are covered.
prerequisite: GSBM 647 Operations Management (4834) (P)

title: Power and Influence
description: The course aims to help you improve your ability to 1) identify sources of power in social contexts, 2) learn techniques for building power, and 3) develop skills for influencing others.
prerequisite: GSBM 640 Management and Organizations (430) (C- and above)

title: Market Intelligence
description: Students will learn about framing problems, evaluating data, and analyzing data for important marketing questions (target market selection, new product or service introduction, customer retention, pricing, etc.)
prerequisite: GSBE 630 Managerial Economics (428) (C- and above)

title: Project Finance
description: Project finance would be interpreted broadly in this course and would include energy finance, environmental finance, infrastructure finance, impact investing, public-private partnerships for large projects, Islamic finance, syndication of large projects, valuation of real options and climate finance.

title: Consumer behavior
description: The study of consumer behaviour uses concepts, theories, and principles from the social sciences to extend our understanding of factors influencing the acquisition, consumption, and disposition of goods, services, and ideas. You will learn how and why consumers behave by examining how we use products to define ourselves and how this self-concept affects our attention and perception, our motivation to buy, our memory for brands, product and advertising awareness, our brand attitudes, product judgment and choice, customer satisfaction and brand loyalty.

title: Mechanics of Materials
description: The main objective of the course is to give students a basic knowledge of the mechanical properties of materials and mechanical systems, methods of their calculation for strength, stiffness and buckling.

title: Fluid Mechanics I
description: Fluid Mechanics is the study of the interaction of energy and fluid flow.

title: Research Project
description: Research Project is a research-oriented course for the 3rd year students with the aim to publish a paper in leading journals.

title: Advanced Control Systems
prerequisite: BENG 219 Control Systems (728) (D and above)

title: Heat Transfer
prerequisite: BENG 226 Engineering Thermodynamics (1553) (D and above) AND EME 275 Fluid Mechanics I (1988) (D and above)

title: Mechanical Systems Design
description: This module is designed to teach students principals of designing mechanical systems.
prerequisite: EME 361 Machine Design (1051) (D and above)

title: Aerodynamics
description: This course aims to introduce the concepts, principles, techniques and theory for the analysis of air flow over moving objects including a review of the historical development of aerodynamics and aerospace engineering. The application of aerodynamics to the design of engineering components and systems is emphasized.
prerequisite: EME 357 Fluid Mechanics II (1280) (D and above)

title: Air Conditioning and Fire Engineering
description: This course is divided into two parts: 1) Air Conditioning and 2) Fire Engineering. 1) The Air Conditioning course aims to relate the scientific theory and principles which govern building air conditioning and, to select and design of the engineering systems to meet requirements. 2) The second half of the course aims to provide a general understanding of the principles of enclosure fire dynamics, its applications to building fires and smoke analysis as well as the basic design methods for fire-fighting systems.
prerequisite: BENG 226 Engineering Thermodynamics (1553) (D and above)

title: Computer Aided Geometric Design
description: CAGD – Computer Aided Geometric Design course presents in detail all the mathematical representations developed for modelling geometric entities in Computer Aided Design (CAD) software packages. The course is also covering the geometric transformations and all geometric operations required in modern CAD packages and concludes with the presentation of tools and methods that are used is accessing the quality of the generated models.
prerequisite: EME 253 Computer Aided Engineering (1050) (C- and above)

title: Fire Engineering
description: Fire engineering includes basics of fire science, compartment fire and fundamentals of fire suppression, fire-fighting systems in buildings, smoke control in buildings.
prerequisite: BENG 226 Engineering Thermodynamics (1553) (D and above)

title: Flight Mechanics
description: Introduction to Flight includes performance and design of airplane, astronautics, propulsion and hypersonic vehicles.

title: Machine Dynamics II
description: Machine Dynamics II is dedicated to study of different ME mechanisms and processes during their operations.

title: Vehicle Propulsion Systems
description: Fuel consumption and drivability models of the most important vehicle propulsion systems, which are IC engines, electric motors, short range energy storages, batteries and fuel cells, drive trains and vehicles, etc.

title: Materials and Manufacturing II
description: This module is designed to teach students principals of manufacturing and production of materials.

title: Capstone Project II
description: The objective of the module (it is first part of a yearlong final year project) is to give the student opportunity to create masterpiece using the knowledge obtained during their study in the university

title: Particulate Technology
description: na

title: Industrial Automation
description: na

title: Applied Statistics and Probability
description: This module covers applied statistical methods and probability for undergraduate students
prerequisite: EME 485 Applied Statistics and Probability (2236) (D and above)

title: Oscillation of Mechanical Systems
description: Oscillation of mechanical systems is studying theory of vibrations.

title: Mechatronics Systems Design
description: Topics coverage includes mechatronics design approach and tools, simulations, mechanical system and mechanism, motors, actuators, microcontroller, sensors, data acquisition, and communication.
prerequisite: BENG 219 Control Systems (728) (C- and above)

title: Structural Mechanics
description: In the course, the main problems of calculating rods, thick-walled vessels, plates, shells and rotating disks are considered.

title: Advanced Engineering Mathematics
description: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations and Complex Analysis with the help of special computer software.
prerequisite: BENG 228 Engineering Mathematics III (3154) (D and above)

title: Multiphase Systems
description: This course will identify the industrial occurrence of the simultaneous flow of more than one phase and highlight the implications for design. The course will cover the basic principles, engineering models and equations of multi-phase flows and selected multi-phase systems.
prerequisite: EME 275 Fluid Mechanics I (1988) (C- and above)

title: Decision Models
description: Successful management requires the ability to recognize a decision problem, understand its essential features, and make a smart choice.

title: Introduction to Optimization Methods
description: Optimization is the problem of making decisions to maximize or minimize an objective in the presence of complicating constraints.

title: Leading Engineering Teams
description: The goal of this course is to enhance your leadership skills. The course is designed to prepare you to lead high-performing, successful firms in the future and to effectively lead your own career.

title: Operations Management
description: This course explores issues related to planning and controlling the processes used to produce the goods and services provided by an organization

title: Probability and Statistics
description: This course provides the basic concepts in probability and statistics and gives the students introductory-level -practical ability to choose, generate, and properly interpret appropriate descriptive and inferential methods.

title: Project Management
description: The purpose of this module is to introduce theoretical and practical perspectives to project management and understanding of project management principles.

title: Risk Analysis and Management
description: This course help students to develop a working knowledge of risk terminology and reliability engineering, analytic tools and models used to analyze safety, environmental and technological risks, and social and psychological risk issues.

title: Systems Engineering
description: This course explores a framework encapsulating the entire systems engineering discipline and addresses the topics of systems engineering relevant to all professions associated with the complex human-made systems.

title: Managerial Accounting
description: The course is intended as an introduction for individuals who will make business decisions, evaluate business units, and evaluate others (or be evaluated) through the use of accounting systems.

title: Business Strategy
description: This course deals with the work and understanding of strategic management. The course adopts the perspective of managers within the corporation, business, division, plant, or other operating unit who must align their individual actions and responsibilities with the overall objectives of the firm.

title: Leading Change
description: The purpose of this course is to gain an understanding of the driving forces for organizational change.

title: Entrepreneurship
description: The focus of this course is the successful creation and early execution of a new venture.

title: Finance
description: This course is designed to introduce students to the economics of financial markets.

title: Management of Technology & Innovation
description: Technology Management is at the intersection of science, engineering, management and behavioral science.

title: Management of Organizations
description: This course introduces students to the practical and theoretical principles associated with managing organizations.

title: Marketing
description: This course will teach how to use the elements of marketing.

title: Engineering Ethics
description: This course is an introduction to engineering ethics, which stresses analytical reasoning regarding the application of professional ethical codes to specific cases.

title: Product Development
description: This course will provide students with an understanding of the key elements of effective new product development for commercial, industrial and service products.

title: Sustainable Development
description: The course focuses on the sustainability problems of managing growth, sustainability of production patterns, and population change.

title: Engineering Economy
description: This course gives the student an understanding of how the use of capital is perceived by individual stakeholders; why and how a financial feasibility assessment is performed and how financial assessments should be presented.

title: Quality Management
description: This course is designed to provide a comprehensive coverage of quality management theories and implementation including customer focus, continuous improvement, employee involvement, and process improvement.

title: Supply Chain Management
description: This course covers planning and controlling the processes used to produce the goods and services provided by an organization.

title: Big Data
description: This course covers advanced data-mining methods now possible in business and research; Introduction to software for data-visualization and pattern recognition in Big Data and Information Architecture of the Big Data Cloud.

title: Globalization and Engineering
description: The intent of this course is to view globalization as a fact of life and to give students the opportunity to analyze, contemplate, and discuss its impact on the professional lives and work of engineers.

title: Information Systems Mananegement
description: The purpose of this module is to provide a broad understanding of the role and importance of Information Systems (IS) in the modern corporate environment. This course will help students to realize the vital role of IS in the success of doing business. Topics to be covered include the followings: the fundamentals of IS management; IS strategy triangle; strategic uses of information resources (planning and resource management); architecture infrastructure; impact of IS in organizational structures; systems and applications to support business processes

title: Capstone Project
description: The Capstone project is designed to be reflection of a culminating set of personal, academic, and professional experiences. Students work in teams to apply synthesize knowledge and skills acquired during the course of their education to solve design, construction and operational problems with real world constraints and relevant to industry.

title: Technology Assessment
description: This sub-module deals with the techno-economic feasibility analysis of clean energy technologies. Additionally, environmental impact is assessed by the quantification on reduction in CO2 emissions obtained in proposed clean energy technologies when used instead of conventional technologies. This sub-module is accompanied by specialized software to prepare energy-emissions-economic models to support the assessments. The second part of the course will present notions and business cases for technology-to-market path, introducing technology readiness concept, intellectual property management, key performance indicators, and the cornerstones of entrepreneurship. This sub-module will be reinforced by business case discussions, based on real-case scenarios.

title: Engineering Management and Engineering Economy
description: This course is a combination of engineering management and engineering economy in which the basic principles and current practices in managing and analyzing engineering organizations will be focused.

title: Managing Product and Service Development
description: The ability to develop new products and services and bring them successfully to market is a critical capability for all companies. This course will provide students with an understanding of the key elements of effective new product development for commercial, industrial and service products. The manager of a new product or service development project must have the skills to manage a multi-disciplinary team from various disciplines such as engineering, manufacturing, marketing, purchasing, sales resources.

title: Engineering Decision Tools
description: This course will cover theories, methods and applications of linear programming, integer programming, nonlinear programming, network models, decision analysis and games. Students will learn optimization methods and their applications to problems in engineering and business.

title: Knowledge and Innovation Management
description: The course aims to deepen the understanding about the instruments and tools for knowledge and innovation management.

title: Big Data and Information Management
description: This course includes two modules: The Big Data module and the Information Management module. By the end of the course students will be expected, among others, to be able to: 1. apply a set of cross-functional techniques: (i) Computer Science: Databases and their technologies and Information Management, (ii) Statistical and (iii) Management Science/Operations Research optimization. 2. take decisions by handling big data in various companies such as: Banking, Insurance, Logistics/SCM, large supermarkets, and other industrial, computer and service firms. 3. gain the knowledge, skills, and abilities to manage information technology systems effectively. 4. formulate and execute IT policies, strategies, plans and procedures.

title: Production and Service Operations Management
description: This course explores issues related to planning and controlling the processes used to produce the goods and services provided by an organization.

title: Quality and Lean Management
description: This course is designed to provide a comprehensive coverage of quality management and lean production systems with their well-known principles, and how two systems can be integrated for sustainable process improvement in production and service organizations.

title: Lean Production
description: This course is designed to provide a comprehensive coverage of lean production with its principles including value, flow, pull, and perfection; and methods including value stream mapping, line balancing, 5S, Kanban and cellular systems for waste elimination, visual management, and continuous improvement.

title: Business Communication
description: This course establishes a foundation of competent communication in the business world, and provides an opportunity to assess and improve students’ verbal and written communication to be more effective, clear, appropriately assertive and based in foundations of personal integrity and leadership.

title: Applying Industry 4.0
description: This course aims at analysis of the industrial systems and development of the enhanced systems using Industry 4.0 architecture and technologies. The main focus will be on operations management and optimization of smart industrial production systems.

title: Understanding and Predicting Consumer Behavior
description: Consumer behaviour examines the impact of external environmental influences and internal psychological influences on consumer decision-making process. You will learn how and why consumers behave and how this self-concept affects our attention and perception, our motivation to buy, product and advertising awareness, customer satisfaction and brand loyalty.

title: Capstone Project I
description: The Capstone Project (CP) plays the role of the Master’s Thesis in the MEM Program. Students work in teams to apply knowledge and skills acquired during the course of their education to solve real industrial problems by combining both technical/engineering and managerial concepts and techniques. The CP is split into two parts: CP I, conducted in the 3rd Semester, and CP II, conducted in the last 4th Semester of the MEM Program. CP I consists mainly of two (2) concrete activities: 1. Identify a faculty advisor, an independent research-based project in collaboration with a local company or companies, and a liaison from the sponsoring companies. 2. Conduct a detailed literature review of the publications that are relevant to the CP proposal.

title: Capstone Project II
description: The Capstone Project (CP) plays the role of the Master’s Thesis in the MEM Program. Students work in teams to apply knowledge and skills acquired during the course of their education to solve real industrial problems by combining both technical/engineering and managerial concepts and techniques. The CP consists of two parts: CP I, conducted in the 3rd Semester, and CP II, conducted in the last Semester 4 of the MEM Program. CP II consists of the six (6) concrete activities: 1. Identify the research methodology to apply for solving the problem. 2. Gather and analyze the data from the collaborating companies. 3. Present the progress of the project, so far, with the initial results. 4. Complete the findings of the project with final results and recommendations to the Managers of the collaborating companies. 5. Submit their draft report to the supervisors and present the final results to the Panel Committee. 6. Finalize and submit the Final Report of the Capstone Project to the School.

title: Digital Transformation and Disruption
description: Digital Transformation Concepts is an immersive course meticulously designed to empower students with a comprehensive grasp of the principles and applications of digital transformation across diverse sectors. This course delves into the technological, managerial, and policy facets of digital transformation, with a specific emphasis on how technological advancements shape the landscape of firms, markets, supply chains, and regulatory frameworks.

title: Capstone Project Planning
description: Capstone Project Planning is the first phase of a two-part course where students apply engineering management principles to real-world problems. In teams, students collaborate with industry partners to address current challenges, conduct literature reviews, and develop project proposals. The course focuses on enhancing skills in problem-solving, teamwork, and effective communication. By the end of the semester, students present their project proposals, setting the foundation for Capstone Project Development.

title: Capstone Project Development
description: The Capstone Project Development (CPD) is designed to reflect a culminating set of personal, academic, and professional experiences.
prerequisite: EMEM 552 Capstone Project Planning (8510) (P)

title: Operations and Supply Chain Management
description: Operations and Supply Chain Management (OSCM) is a vital business function focused on the efficient production and delivery of goods and services. This graduate-level course explores both strategic and tactical aspects of managing resources, processes, and supply chains. Students will learn key topics such as demand forecasting, process optimization, inventory control, and project management, while examining global supply chain complexities. Through case studies and simulations, students will gain the skills to balance quality, cost, and logistics, and to mitigate risks in dynamic business environments, positioning firms for operational success.

title: AI Applications in Engineering Management
description: AI Applications in Engineering Management is a graduate course exploring advanced AI and ML methodologies for complex civil engineering systems. Topics include deep learning (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers), Explainable AI, NLP, and domain applications in structural health monitoring, environmental modeling, water quality and flood prediction. Students use Python, PyTorch, and GitHub, and complete an original research project with a written paper and conference-style presentation.

title: Advanced Materials Processing
description: This course will provide training in the engineering principles underlying the design and control of processes for the recovery and purification of materials.

title: Advanced Materials Structure
description: This course sets the foundation of materials, detailing the necessary principles governing the structure, composition and properties of materials. The aim is to give students an understanding of the fundamental principles of modern solid state chemistry structures, properties, syntheses and applications of solid materials.

title: In situ and Post Synthesis Materials Characterization I
description: This course will address the characterization of materials, especially for analyzing surface treatments and modifications and performance assessment.

title: Materials in Industry
description: This course will explore material behaviour as a result of processing techniques applied combining analytical techniques used in industry.

title: Introduction to Engineering
description: This course introduces students to the foundation and fundamental principles required to become analytical, detail-oriented, and productive engineers. The students will also gain an overview of what engineers do and of the various areas of specialization. Important topics for the engineering profession such as research in engineering, communications, and safety are also introduced. Additionally, students will work together in interdisciplinary groups to research, design, fabricate, test, and deploy a complete engineering project.

title: Programming for Engineers
description: Programming for Engineers is a comprehensive introductory course designed specifically for students with little or no prior programming experience. The course aims to equip students with fundamental programming skills and a solid understanding of the role computation can play in problem-solving.
