description: This course is designed to monitor progress and develop understandings, skills, and outlooks to conduct original, independent research at the PhD level. The student will develop (with the advisor’s guidance) a research plan at the beginning of the semester that will state a research problem/question/hypothesis, its background, outline a research strategy and experimental approach, method of data collection, interpretation and validation, and method of communication of the project results to others. The research plan is used as the basis for assessment of the student’s research progress.

title: Real Analysis
description: This course is an introduction to the modern theory of integration.

title: Functional Analysis with Applications
description: This advanced-level course will introduce PhD students to the important fields of function theory, operator theory, and spectral theory as well as their applications.

title: Abstract Algebra
description: This is an upper level course in abstract algebra.

title: Advanced Operations Research
description: Operations research helps in solving problems in different environments that needs decisions. This course covers topics that include: mathematical programming, stochastic optimization, fuzzy optimization, dynamic programming, deterministic and stochastic optimal control, multi-criteria decision aid, and application to engineering, finance, management.

title: Nonlinear Differential Equations with Applications
description: This advanced-level course will introduce PhD students to the qualitative theory of nonlinear differential equations and its applications.

title: Advanced Partial Differential Equations
description: This course is an introduction to the theory of linear and nonlinear partial differential equations.
prerequisite: MATH 701 Real Analysis (5489) (B and above)

title: Advanced Statistical Learning
description: The course covers theoretical foundations and applications of machine learning models. Topics include supervised methods for regression and classification (linear models, trees, neural networks, ensemble methods, instance-based methods), Bayesian parametric learning, density estimation and clustering, sequential models. Programming projects covering a variety of real-world applications are assigned.

title: Advanced statistical programming
description: The course introduces students to programming and algorithms in statistics and data analysis. It is intended for learners who have a basic programming background, and want to apply statistical, machine learning, information visualization, and text analysis techniques through popular toolkits such as pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn, and nltk to gain insight into their data.

title: Probability Theory
description: This course is a measure-theoretic probability with emphasis on rigorous mathematical theory.

title: Mathematical Finance
description: This advanced-level course will introduce PhD students to the advanced level concepts in stochastic calculus theory and its use in advanced mathematical finance.

title: Operations Research
description: This course will introduce PhD students to optimization theory and its use in applied sciences at the Ph.D. level.

title: Advanced numerical methods for partial differential equations
description: The course is a blend of conceptual and practical aspects of numerical solutions of partial differential equations. Topics include finite difference, volume, and element methods, and explicit/implicit methods for time integration, convergence, consistency, stability, Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy criteria, Lax equivalence theorem, error analysis, Fourier-von Neumann stability analysis. Applications include the Poisson equation, heat equation, wave equation, advection-diffusion equation, and Stokes equation.

title: Research Methods and Ethics
description: This course prepares students the fundamental skills and knowledge necessary for performing and managing their research works as well as training them to deliver high-quality technical presentations to communicate their findings.

title: Topics in Mathematics
description: This advanced-level course will introduce PhD students to the selected topics of mathematics.

title: Introduction to General Management Principles
description: This orientation course lays the foundation for success in the MBA program by providing students with the necessary skills and knowledge to navigate academic challenges, work collaboratively, and develop the mindset required for effective leadership in the business world.

title: Foundations of Financial and Managerial Accounting
description: The goal of this course is to equip students with knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary for detailed examination and evaluation of financial and managerial accounting information in order to make informed business decisions.

title: Leadership & Communication
description: This course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the critical role that effective leadership and communication play in modern organizational success.

title: Probability and Statistics
description: Management decisions are often made under conditions of uncertainty. This course introduces a framework for thinking about problems involving uncertainty and building on this framework, develops tools for interpreting data.

title: Principles of Finance
description: The course examines the theory of financial decision-making by firms and examines the behavior of the capital markets in which these decisions are taken.

title: Economics for Managers
description: This course aims to provide an analytical and conceptual basis to guide managerial decisions in complex business environments. To this end, the course introduces analytical tools that are frequently used in economics. The approach that we develop offers you a powerful framework to assess various problems businesses are confronted with on a daily basis and hence it provides a good framework of an optimal business strategy.

title: Management and Organizations
description: To be an effective manager and leader requires both a broad understanding of how organizations function as well as personal skills for managing people and relationships.

title: Managerial Economics
description: This course covers the fundamental concepts and tools of microeconomics: supply and demand analysis, market determination of prices and quantities, consumer choices, market demand, and production and cost theory.

title: Marketing Management
description: This course provides students with the necessary understanding of the basic marketing concepts and analytic skills.

title: Foundations of Strategy
description: The purpose of the course in strategy is to make participants familiar with the core concepts and techniques that function as foundations for formulating and implementing successful strategies.

title: Operations Management
description: Operations management involves planning and controlling the processes used to produce the goods and services provided by an organization. In essence, it is the management of all activities related to doing the actual work of the organization. Managing these processes can be quite challenging -they are often very complex, and can involve large numbers of people and facilities, huge volumes of materials and great distances.

title: Environmental, Social and Governance Factors (ESG) for Business
description: In this course students will learn the relevance of governance, social and environmental issues to their industry or function, and understand the interaction of business, government, and society in addressing society’s challenges

title: Macroeconomics
description: This course helps you understand the economics of financial markets and the global economic context in which managers make decisions.

title: Decision Models
description: Decision problems involving uncertainty or many variables are difficult to grasp intuitively.

title: Corporate Finance
description: This course takes the perspective of financial managers responsible for making significant investment and financing decisions.

title: Entrepreneurship
description: This course is intended to provide prospective entrepreneurs with information and tools.

title: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
description: This is a hands-on course that teaches a rigorous framework and provides a valuable experience to students so that they, upon completion, can be more successful in starting a new venture.

title: Negotiations
description: This course will help students understand the theory and processes of negotiation.

title: Financial Statement Analysis
description: The course provides a framework to analyze and interpret financial statements.

title: Distinguished Speaker Series
description: During this course, senior leaders from industry and government will be invited to engage with students on various business and policy topics.

title: Practicum Project
description: Research/consulting project and case study development

title: Internship
description: Internship is the final capstone course and project in the student's curriculum. The objective of which is to help students increase their knowledge of the complexities of organizations, and the role that the institutional environment plays in the conduct and performance of business. As such, this capstone project is intended to represent a synthesis and application of the program learning outcomes and demonstrate business competence, exceptional teamwork skills, knowledge of core business theory, and effective communication skills, all of which will be considered in the evaluation of deliverables: a paper and a presentation in which all students must participate.

title: Principles of Finance
description: The course examines the theory of financial decision-making by firms and examines the behavior of the capital markets in which these decisions are taken. The underlying concept is the concept of value and value creation. Upon the completion of the course the students will be able to build a spreadsheet model of a typical business project and analyze it from the financial perspective.

title: Corporate Finance
description: This course develops a theoretical framework for understanding and analyzing major financial challenges of a modern firm in the contemporary global market environment

title: Global Economics for Managers
description: This course will provide economic tools for students to analyze the challenges and opportunities of business that crosses borders.

title: Entrepreneurial Finance
description: The Entrepreneurial Finance course is designed primarily for students who plan to get involved with a new venture at some point in their career ―as a founder, early employee, advisor or investor

title: Investments
description: This course provides the principles of capital markets, investments, and asset pricing, including: fixed income and equity securities and markets, asset allocation, asset pricing models, active portfolio management, performance evaluation, the interaction between capital markets and the macro economy, as well as alternative investments such as hedge funds and private equity. Students learn how to appropriately create a portfolio based on an individual’s risk tolerance and securities’ expected returns and risk.

title: Data Analytics for Business
description: The course investigates how data can be used to directly impact business decisions. The large part of this course will be concentrated around basic methods for data analytics, such as multiple regression, ANOVA, contingency analysis and logistic regression.

title: Raising Capital
description: The course explains how venture capitalists arrange the financing for a company; what they look for in a business plan; how they value a business; and how they structure the terms of an agreement. Using informative case studies, and exercises, the course discusses the basic principles of the venture capital method, strategies for raising capital, methods of valuing the early-stage venture, and proven techniques for negotiating the deal.

title: Innovation Process
description: The topic of this course is the innovation process, particularly innovation within existing companies and organizations. The course will cover both the practice and theory of innovation. The main activity of the course will be to generate a meaningful innovation for an existing organization in Nur-Sultan city.

title: Advanced Corporate Finance
description: This course was designed to develop graduate students’ ability to make financial decisions and recommendations through the application of finance theory and concepts to a wide range of business cases representative of real world problems.

title: Project Management
description: The concepts and use of project management tools, techniques and methodologies are becoming all pervasive. The course addresses project management in a general context and not specifically focusing on any one type of project such as construction or software projects.

title: China Business Environment
description: This subject is designed to provide students with an introduction to the key issues facing business in China.

title: Consumer Behavior
description: The aim of this course is to develop a critical understanding of the behavioural aspects of marketing in both theory and practice in the national and international contexts.

title: Global Economics for Managers
description: This course will provide economic tools for students to analyze the challenges and opportunities of business that crosses borders.
prerequisite: MBA 08 Managerial Economics (1722) (C and above)

title: Emerging Markets Strategy
description: The course focuses on strategies that firms based in emerging market economies around the world are adopting in order to compete in their home markets and, increasingly, in regional and global markets beyond their boundaries.

title: Marketing Research
description: This course will provide a basic understanding of research methodology and implementation of marketing. Students will develop a comprehension of applying appropriate research methods (e.g., secondary data, qualitative methods, surveys, or experimentation) to marketing-related managerial problems.

title: Project Finance
description: Project finance would be interpreted broadly in this course and would include energy finance, environmental finance, infrastructure finance, impact investing, public-private partnerships for large projects, Islamic finance, syndication of large projects, valuation of real options and climate finance.

title: Business Law
description: This course is an introductory course in business law, with emphasis on real world applicability in the field of business. Theory combined with practice-oriented exercises to develop a foundation in intellectual property, environmental law and corporate law.

title: Valuation
description: The course is intended to provide students with a strong theoretical and applied understanding of the key equity valuation and stock selection approaches used by financial managers, securities analysts and investment/portfolio managers. Emphasis is placed on the role of financial statement data in equity valuation, using advanced problems and cases developed from and around actual financial statements.

title: Pricing
description: Profitable pricing is the harvest of firm's efforts to create value for its customers. Indeed, it is the only element of the marketing mix that produces revenue; all other elements represent costs. Consequently, setting prices is a critical managerial decision. For both strategic and tactical reasons, managers change prices more often than any other element of the marketing mix.

title: Competitive Analysis
description: The course explores how the strategic decisions of individual firms shape the structure of its industry, using concepts from Game Theory.

title: International Finance
description: This course provides an introduction to international finance and multinational financial management practices.

title: Supply Chain Management
description: A supply chain is a network of organizations that are involved in the different processes and activities that produce value in the form of products and services.

title: Leadership
description: Building on the concepts and skills introduced in its predecessor courses (Consequential Leadership) and Managerial Effectiveness, this course challenges students to sharpen and apply their leadership capabilities at the collective/community level, and building trust and community in a multi-cultural world through the practice of courageous leadership.

title: Marketing Strategy
description: The course is concerned with how to manage customers to maximize firm profits, i.e. how to select, acquire, retain, and profit from customers. The course builds on the core marketing class and the core strategy class.

title: Research Seminar
description: This course enables students to gain and apply basic research knowledge and skills to select their research projects in Biomedical Engineering.

title: Master Thesis I
description: This course intends to give students the opportunity to develop the research proposal in Biomedical Engineering.

title: Master Thesis II
description: Student will prepare MSc thesis and present research report in front of panel of faculty.
prerequisite: MBME 601 Master Thesis I (5953) (P)

title: Biomaterials Science & Engineering
description: The course “Biomaterials Science & Engineering” will present an overview of synthetic and natural materials, which are currently used in different areas of biomedical engineering. Structure and function of these materials will be discussed. Special emphasis will be laid on polymeric biomaterials and metals as well as their biocompatibility.

title: Biosensors
description: The Biosensors course will provide an interdisciplinary view of biosensors, focusing on the technological aspects, as well as on implementation and applications, with elements of electronics, photonics, surface chemistry, and biology. The course will present electronic biosensors, optical biosensors, biorecognition and functionalization, and applications of biosensors.

title: Advanced Tissue Engineering
description: This course is designed to cover the most recent advancements in different areas of applications of tissue engineering. The topics in this course will include tissue engineering strategies such as i) compositional, structural and functional analysis of different tissues in human body, ii) design, fabrication and utilization of scaffold biomaterials and iii) cellular engineering including cell therapy, drug delivery; as well as cell-biomaterial interactions. Recent advances and major problems relevant to tissue engineering will also be presented and discussed.

title: Anatomy and Physiology for Biomedical Engineers
description: This course is designed to cover the basics of human anatomy and physiology including anatomical terminology, cells and tissues, body parts, the musculoskeletal system, the nervous system, special senses, the cardiovascular system, ECG, the respiratory system, and urinary system. The course provides a foundation in human anatomy appropriate for biomedical engineering professionals. Learning objectives will be achieved through a combination of lecture and practical (on models) approaches, reinforced by clinical examples and analysis of how biomedical devices interface with anatomical structures.

title: Strategies for Controlled Topical Delivery of Drugs
description: The course will discuss the most important contemporary strategies and methods for controlled topical delivery of drugs in clinical practice. The course will focus on the use of advanced devices and biomaterials to achieve the aim of supplying drugs in adequate quantities to target tissues, during an extended time interval. Examples will be abstracted from oncology (e.g., local delivery of cytostatic and/or angiogenic agents to solid tumors), ophthalmology (e.g., delivery of drugs to anterior and posterior parts of the eye), pulmonary drug delivery and long-duration contraception, etc.

title: Infectious Diseases and Antimicrobial Strategies
description: This course will introduce the students to biofilm and its role in infectious diseases and outline the current antimicrobial strategies for biofilm control in health setting and biomedical devices.

title: Biomedical Imaging
description: This course will introduce the physical principles and applications of in vivo bioimaging modalities including X-ray computed tomography (CT), Single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), positron emission tomography (PET), clinical applications of nuclear medicine, ultrasonic imaging (US), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

title: Mechanics of Living Tissue
description: This course aims at introducing the basics and applications of biomechanics principals. The topics in this course will include skeletal muscle system, biomechanics of lower and upper extremity bones, spine biomechanics as well as cell biomechanics. More specifically, the students are expected to learn about biomechanics of tissues including bone, articular cartilage, tendons and ligaments, skeletal muscle, knee, hip, foot and ankle, shoulder, elbow, wrist and hand, fracture fixation, and gait.

title: Biophotonics
description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of how light interacts with biological materials. The primary focus rests on the deployment of photonics in domains such as optical bioimaging, phototherapy, optogenetics, and neurophotonics. Integral to the course content are fundamental concepts concerning biophotonic materials, elucidated through a variety of engaging case studies.

title: Basic Science Block
description: This Block provides strong fundamental scientific basis of human anatomy, genetics, cell pathology and microbiology, forming the basis of Medical practice and allowing students to apply the clinical knowledge and skills.

title: Medical Anatomy
description: The MEDICAL ANATOMY course provides the basic knowledge of structure and morphology of the human body, using the techniques of direct observation (anatomy virtual suites and cadavers) clinical imaging and scenarios oriented in developing observation and perception of abnormalities.

title: Human Genetics
description: The HUMAN GENETICS course gives a strong knowledge of genetic and genomic structure, putting in place the right basis for understanding topics like inheritance, mutation, genetic diseases management.

title: Immunology in Health and Disease
description: The IMMUNOLOGY course is focused on immunity, autoimmunity and immunodeficiency concepts, giving insight of the main immunologic diseases and treatments.

title: Medical Microbiology
description: The MEDICAL MICROBIOLOGY course introduces basic concepts of infectious disease, focusing on bacteriology, virology, parasitology, the mechanisms of disease transmission and treatment.

title: Pharmacology
description: In this course students will learn about the basic principles and mechanisms of commonly used drugs and how they exert their actions.

title: MSc Thesis in Civil Engineering
description: The key goal of the Master’s thesis is solving a problem relevant to the field of study based on existing scientific and engineering knowledge in compliance with the principles of responsible research conduct.

title: Sustainable Development
description: This course is an introduction to the field of sustainable development, based on the definition of the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED) in Our common future.

title: Advanced Project Management
description: This course is an advanced course for students who have completed Project Management. More advanced theories and practices will be introduced in this course and students are expected to have possessed basic project management concepts.

title: Environmental Impacts and Assessments
description: This course covers the process and techniques for assessing and managing the impacts on and risks to humans and the ecosystem associated with engineering processes and outputs such as facilities and infrastructure.

title: Contaminated Site Management and Soil Treatment Technologies
description: The course aims to give civil engineering M.Sc. students the fundamental notions of contaminated site management and of technology selection for soil treatment. It aims to make them capable to propose, based on a given specific case and characterization data, a site management plans a treatment technology including design.

title: Sustainable Transportation Systems
description: This course is to provide students with state of art analysis and design methods for transportation systems. It starts with development of transportation policies with sustainability and resiliency as main drivers and will include technical aspects in analysis and design of: (1) Highways; (2) Bridges; (3) Tunnels; (4) Rapid transportation systems for cities.

title: Sustainable Infrastructure Systems
description: This course is to provide students with analysis and design of infrastructure systems with consideration of economic, environmental and social impacts of infrastructures in communities. Technical aspects are include state of the art analysis and design methods for underground structural system; large span structural system; power plants; offshore structures; and control towers as part of integrated urban services.

title: Resilient Structural and Geotechnical Systems
description: This course is to provide students with understanding of the behavior and design of building structural systems including design load calculation and design procedures of structural systems as resilient systems in an urban setting.

title: Numerical Method in Geotechnical Engineering
description: Formulation and application of finite element and discrete element methods in solving geotechnical engineering problems related to seepage, diffusion, elasticity, plasticity and dynamic motion of soil masses, stability and convergence problems and utilization of industrial standard computer programs in real world engineering applications.

title: Applications of Geomatics in Civil Engineering
description: This course aims to lay foundation for the practical applications of the Geomatics for the Civil Engineering projects, to master Remote Sensing and GIS skills and to provide students opportunity to develop projects with applications of remote Sensing and GIS for Civil Engineering.

title: Research Seminar
description: This course enables students to gain and apply basic research knowledge and skills to select their research projects in Civil and Environmental Engineering.

title: Master Thesis I
description: This course intends to give students the opportunity to develop the research proposal.
prerequisite: MCEE 600 Research Seminar (4692) (P)

title: MSc Thesis II
description: This course intends to give students the opportunity to fully implement the research proposal and bring it to a conclusion.

title: Finite Element Methods
description: This course will provide students detailed theoretical backgrounds, formulations and implementations of the Finite Element Method and its application to solid and fluid mechanics.

title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
description: This course is designed to provide students a theoretical framework for the analysis of deformation and failure of soils with application to several practical problems. These include elasticity for linear deformation, plasticity models (including critical state model) for non-linear deformation and limit equilibrium analyses for important geotechnical problems.

title: Advanced Environmental Chemistry
description: This course will provide graduate students detailed theoretical backgrounds and their applications and computational implementations to estimate the fate of chemical species in the environmental systems.

title: Advanced Project Management
description: The aim of this module is to 1. Apply knowledge and skills in the solution of Engineering Management problems 2. Understand the importance of leadership in team development and operation. 3. Identify, formulate, and solve issues related to project implementation.

title: Structural Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering
description: This course will provide graduate students with an understanding of the vibration behavior and dynamic response of structural systems to periodic and arbitrary loadings; and with a discussion on earthquake engineering.

title: Advanced Concrete Technology
description: This course provides an overview of materials used to make portland cement concrete (PCC) and mechanisms of concrete durability. This course also identifies appropriate PCC material properties for PCC construction projects.

title: Structural Evaluation and Rehabilitation
description: This course introduces students structural evaluation techniques and determining remaining service life of structures.

title: Theory of Physico-Chemical Treatment Processes
description: This course will provide graduate students detailed theoretical background and their applications of physico-chemical processes for the treatment and remediation of contaminants in the environmental systems.

title: Contaminated Site Management and Soil Treatment Technologies
description: The course aims to give civil engineering M.Sc. students the fundamental notions of contaminated site management and of technology selection for soil treatment. It aims to make them capable to propose, based on a given specific case and characterization data, a site management plans a treatment technology including design.

title: Environmental Modeling Development
description: The course is intended to give advanced level of knowledge and real life applications of methods for environmental modelling and its purposes and to give fundamental knowledge and experience in model construction and evaluation.

title: Concrete Repair and Maintenance
description: This course introduces students different repair materials and strengthening techniques to carry out concrete repair and maintenance.

title: Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering
description: This course introduces students aspects of geotechnical engineering related to earthquakes and other dynamic effects.

title: Advanced Foundation Engineering
description: This course is designed so that students can better understand foundation engineering and learn from experts in geotechnical engineering on how to design a safe and sustainable foundation system in various site and loading conditions.

title: Building Information Modeling in Construction
description: This course introduces students the principles and practices of building information modeling (BIM) for architecture, engineering and construction. The course helps students develop proficiency with the methods and with the processes for delivering engineering solutions using BIM

title: Green Building - Concept, Design, Construction, and Operation
description: The objective of this course is to present key parts of green buildings, and provide a basis for further group project activities. Students will produce and generate ideas on green building projects' specific aspects. They will assess exiting projects by following a certification method (e.g., LEED, BREEAM, GreenStar, GSAS, etc.).

title: Soil Improvement and Stabilization
description: This course is designed so that students can not only understand the fundamentals of soil improvement/stabilization techniques and observational methods in geotechnical engineering, but also assess the suitability and design of improvement/stabilization techniques for difficult foundation soils including instrumentation and application of observational techniques.

title: Advanced Pavement Design, Analysis, and Rehabilitation
description: This course is designed to develop student’s knowledge further and enable them to plan, design, and analyze new and existing pavements. This course addresses the theory and practice in the fundamentals of pavement design and rehabilitation strategy such as pavement performance, structural design of pavement layers, types of materials used in pavement layers, characterization of pavement layer materials. Concepts of pavement management and pavement rehabilitation strategy will be introduced. Pavement design and evaluation computational tools will be introduced and applied.

title: Advanced Concrete Design
description: The objective of this course is to prepare students for advanced-level structural engineering employment by providing them with abilities to design and analyze reinforced concrete structures. This course provides students with advanced techniques, such as section analysis, yield line theory, 2nd order analysis, and Bresler’s reciprocal theory, for analysis and design of reinforced concrete structural members under the complicate loading conditions such as torsion, bi-axial bending, and buckling.

title: Advanced Wastewater Treatment
description: This course will provide graduate students detailed theoretical background and its applications to the design and development of advanced wastewater treatment systems.

title: Sustainable Construction and Development
description: This course covers sustainable construction concepts and techniques, including green building planning, design, delivery, operations, assessment systems, energy-efficient building systems, water conservation, and renewable energy sources. It equips students with the knowledge and skills to implement sustainable building projects that are environmentally responsible, economically viable, and socially beneficial.

title: Unsaturated Soil Mechanics for Engineering Practice
description: This course aims to acquaint students with the principles of unsaturated soil mechanics and its application to engineering practice under the effect of climatic conditions, such as: slope stability, retaining wall design, foundation design, soil-structure interaction.

title: Computational Modeling and Instrumentation in Geotechnical Engineering
description: This course aims to acquaint students with the knowledge of computational modeling and instrumentation for application in geotechnical engineering, such as slope stability, seepage analysis, deep excavation, and foundation.

title: MSc Thesis in Chemical Engineering
description: The Master’s thesis constitutes a piece of applied research and in this context, the primary goal is to provide students with the opportunity to analyze, solve and present their research findings for an existing problem relevant to their field of study.

title: Pipeline Engineering & Flow Assurance
description: The course will focuses on the reliable, continuous and simultaneous transport of liquid crude oil and gas from the formation to the processing facilities.

title: Process Engineering and Simulation
description: This course focuses on the development of process flowsheets, their implementation into commercial simulators and their use for process evaluation. Several case studies related to oil and gas industries will be discussed in this course.
prerequisite: MCHE 615 Advanced Unit Operations (3145) (D and above)

title: Crude Oil Processing
description: This course will present an overview of the modern, integrated crude oil refinery, its feedstocks, product, and the processes employed to convert crude oil and intermediate streams into finished products. Each refining process will be presented, covering operating description, feedstock and catalyst selection, unit performance, and product output and properties.

title: Natural Gas Processing
description: The course aims to cover the following: LNG production, Oil and Condensate Removal, Water Removal, Separation of Natural Gas Liquids, Hydrogen Sulfide and Carbon Dioxide Removal, Plant Design.

title: Petroleum Refining Water/Wastewater Use and Management
description: This course concerns best practices and strategies used in petroleum refineries to manage water, wastewater reclamation and ways to reduce water usage.

title: Physical Chemistry of Oil & Gas
description: Oil and gas reservoir fluids , mining , oil refining, natural gas utilization , pollution control and carbon sequestration is important for the chemical concepts . Oil and gas properties and fluid phase equilibria , thermodynamics of multiphase Oil and test methods ( laboratory )

title: Applied Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
description: This course covers advanced applied chemical engineering thermodynamics topics with focus on V-L multicomponent equilibrium.

title: Advanced Unit Operations
description: This course is designed to provide advanced knowledge in the current theory and practice of process systems engineering with the emphasis on petrochemical, oil and gas industries.

title: Advanced Chemical Reactor Engineering
description: Design for Multiple Reactors and Multiple Reactions Heterogeneous non-Catalytic and Catalytic Reaction Systems Isothermal and non-Isothermal Reactors Non-ideal Reactors Reactors Scale Up Biochemical Reactors
prerequisite: ECHE 481 Chemical Reaction Engineering (1985) (D and above)

title: Plant Economics and Planning
description: Economic concepts involved in project evaluation Value of investments as defined within a fiscal system Risks associated with economic decisions

title: Safety Engineering and Loss Prevention
description: The course aims to provide education and training in the area of Safety Engineering and Loss Prevention, including necessary aspects of Risk Management, in a unified approach. The course is tailored for Chemical Engineering needs and focuses on Chemical Process Safety and it covers principles and fundamentals of Risk Management and chemical-processes relevant hazards and mitigation including a number of in-depth case studies analyses.

title: Research Seminar
description: This course enables students to gain and apply basic research knowledge and skills to select their research projects in Chemical and Materials Engineering..

title: Master Thesis I
description: This course intends to give students the opportunity to develop the research proposal.

title: MSc Thesis II
description: This course intends to give students the opportunity to fully implement the research proposal and bring it to a conclusion.

title: Advanced Materials Processing
description: The main technologies for the production of high-value materials from polymers and ceramics and the theory which underlies materials processing operations will be covered in this course.

title: Advanced Materials Characterization Methods
description: Fundamentals, Operation, and Applications of Electron Microscopy, Spectroscopy, Diffraction, Calorimetry, and Thermogravimetric Analysis.

title: Advanced Chemical Reaction Engineering
description: The course is addressed to graduate students and aims at reinforcing and enhancing the knowledge they have on chemical reaction engineering, focusing on problem solving techniques and on connecting the principles presented with relevant applications, especially in the production of materials.

title: Advanced Heat and Mass Transfer
description: Advanced Heat and Mass Transfer focuses on the study and modeling of different types of heat and mass processes for various complex systems and apparatus in chemical engineering.

title: Advanced Chemical Thermodynamics
description: This course covers advanced applied chemical engineering thermodynamics topics with focus on V-L multicomponent equilibrium.

title: Advanced Safety, Reliability and Risk Engineering in Process Industries
description: This course enables students to understand dynamic risk assessment and accident modeling approach. It equips students with process safety analysis skills.

title: Food Engineering and Processing
description: The aim of this course is to introduce ChEM students the main principles of food engineering and their implementation in the food industry. The course covers the majors techniques used in food processing and preservation, including topics on food chemistry and microbiology.

title: Advanced Tissue Engineering
description: This course is designed to cover the most recent advancements in different areas of applications of tissue engineering. The topics in this course will include tissue engineering strategies such as i) compositional, structural and functional analysis of different tissues in human body, ii) design, fabrication and utilization of scaffold biomaterials and iii) cellular engineering including cell therapy, drug delivery; as well as cell-biomaterial interactions. Recent advances and major problems relevant to tissue engineering will also be presented and discussed.

title: Advanced Energy Materials and their Applications
description: This course covers the fundamentals, characterizations and preparation methods of advanced and currently used materials for energy applications. Generation, conversion and storage in solar cells, fuel cells and particularly Li-ion batteries are going to be presented. Additionally, special and unique properties of materials will be considered for designing of batteries for particular applications. Other advanced energy related technologies as fuel cell and photovoltaics will be introduced and the main applied materials will be discussed.

title: Computational Materials Engineering
description: This course introduces a variety of computational methods commonly used in Computational Materials Science and Engineering, ranging from atomistic methods, including first-principle calculations and all-atom molecular dynamics, to mesoscopic methods, such as coarse-grained molecular dynamics, Brownian dynamics, kinetic Monte Carlo, and to the continuum-level modeling methods.

title: Air Quality, Toxicity and Health
description: This course discusses chemical and thermodynamic processes in the atmosphere resulting in the nucleation of the airborne particles. The resulting health effects on the human will be discussed. This course explains how to identify sources of pollutants indoors and outdoor, their exposure routes, emission rate of the pollutants, and approaches to reduce the emissions

title: Cardiac Pathologies Clerkship
description: The course is designed to provide the student with the opportunity for in-depth study and performance of heart diseases.

title: Research Seminar
description: This course enables students to gain and apply basic research knowledge and skills to select their research projects in Electrical and Computer Engineering. The course develops the following knowledge and skills. Presentation of a seminar and being assessed by a panel.

title: Master Thesis I
description: This course intends to give students the opportunity to develop the research proposal.

title: Master Thesis II
description: This course serves as proof that the student obtainedunderstanding and knowledge in electrical and computer engineering field; the thesis should show the student's confident and awareness on the thesis topic, and should display original and meaningful thinking.

title: Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Growth of functions, sorting algorithms, hash tables, red-black trees, augmenting data structures, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, amortized analysis, B-trees, Binomial heaps, Fibonacci heaps, minimum spanning tree, shortest path algorithms, flow networks, sorting networks, linear programming, string matching, computational geometry, NP-completeness, approximation algorithms.

title: Statistics and Probability for Electrical and Computer Engineers
description: Goal of this course is to provide a mathematical introduction to the theory of stochastic processes. Topics covered in this module include: 1. Overview of Probability and Random Variables 2. Introduction of Stochastic Processes 3. Power Spectra and Orthogonal Expansions 4. Bandlimited and Discrete-time Processes 5. Introduction to Estimation Theory

title: Embedded Systems and Applications
description: An overview of select computer architecture and embedded systems topics, hardware, debugging and embedded program development using state-of-the-art tools. Interfacing with external hardware and software/hardware co-development principles are also covered.

title: Energy Systems Operations and Planning
description: Electrical energy system analysis is the core knowledge required for understanding, planning, and operating a power system. This unit introduces students to the core knowledge of electric energy systems analysis and modelling along with planning and reliability study. The course will cover the advanced concepts related to the operation electric energy systems and the regulations in energy industry.

title: Industrial and Commercial Power System
description: Industrial and commercial power systems are discussed in this course. Demand and load calculation along with power quality assessment in industrial power network as well as commercial power system network, regulations, demand and over load calculation, and its earthing system are discussed in this course.

title: Internet of Things
description: This course provides a core grounding in how science and technology have developed to enable the Internet of Things (IoT) – in a way appropriate for any learner. For those interested in developing further hands-on expertise in designing and developing for the Internet of Things, this course will provide a context to the discoveries and converging technologies that will springboard the next round of innovations.

title: Advanced Power Electronics
description: The general purpose of the module is to have the students exposed to modern DC-DC (Switched Capacitor and Flying Capacitor) and DC-AC (Neutral Point Clamped, Flying Capacitor, Cascade H-bridge) power converter topologies, their operation principles, methods of analysis and computer simulation.

title: Advanced Photonics
description: The course Advanced Photonics aims at giving students theoretical and applied concepts of photonic engineering. The course, having strong lab content, extends over 3 main areas: (1) Optical waveguides and optical fibers; (2) Optical sensors; (3) Microscopy and imaging.

title: Fundamentals of Signal Processing
description: This course is designed to familiarize the students with the fundamental topics in digital signal processing and it applications. The course starts from the basics of signals and systems and gradually develops to fundamentals in digital signals processing, random signal processing, and linear optimal filtering.

title: Advanced Mixed Signal Circuit Design
description: This course will provide graduate students detailed theoretical background and their applications of analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits through project based learning.

title: Advanced Electronic Circuits
description: The purpose of this graduate course is to first revisit the fundamentals circuit analysis concepts used in both low and frequency regime. Subsequently, some advanced circuits such as amplifier, filter, and instrumentation amplifiers will be investigated in depth. In the second part of this course, the students will learn fundamental principle of passive circuits such as impedance transformer, filter, power amplifier, and antenna. The project using one of the state-of-the-art EDA/CAD tools is the key aspect of this course.

title: Adaptive Signal Processing
description: This course provides foundational knowledge and practice required to understand adaptive filtering algorithms, and teaches how the adaptive filtering concepts are applied in practical applications.

title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
description: The aim of this module is to introduce fundamental concepts used in design and implementation of pattern recognition and machine learning.

title: Deep Learning for Internet of Things
description: This course will provide graduate students detailed theoretical background and their IoT applications of deep learning through project based learning.

title: Advanced Electromagnetics
description: This course presents advanced analytical techniques for formulating and solving problems in applied electromagnetics. Topics covered are basic electromagnetic theorems, boundary conditions, solutions to the wave equation, Green's functions, spectral domain representations, electric and magnetic field integral equations, and antennas and apertures. Applications of these methods are also presented in the areas of radiation, radiowave propagation in stratified media, scattering, electromagnetic compatibility, and metamaterials.

title: System Modelling and Control
description: This course introduces students to recently developed and advanced techniques for solving modeling and control problems. The course presents theory and methodology for analysis and modeling of systems and signals, and methods for design and synthesis of advanced feedback controllers. The emphasis of this course will be on mathematical foundations and numerical methods for system modeling from physical properties, identification, and advanced control of dynamical systems.

title: Smart Grids and Energy Systems
description: This is an advanced course which focuses on the state of the art developments in power systems and smart grids. The topics to be taught in course will give the students a great competency and in-depth knowledge to contribute to the future of the local power industry and to make it globally competitive. In specific, the course covers the topics such as power system planning and operation, power markets and their integration into the system operation, active distribution network management, Power system automation and control, distributed generation and microgrids, transactive energy systems, machine learning applications in power system, multi-area and tie-line control problems, automatic generation control, frequency-droop control, and power system stability, Availability Based Tariff (ABT) and Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI).
prerequisite: MECE 700 Industrial and Commercial Power System (4810) (D and above)

title: Modern Semiconductor Devices and Systems
description: This course focuses on recent topics of modern semiconductor devices including photodetectors and imaging; photovoltaics; solid-state lighting and laser diodes. Students will be introduced the fundamental knowledge of these semiconductors devices, state-of-the-art device engineering, processing technologies and practical applications in systems. After completion of this course, student will be equipped with consolidated knowledge in those popular topics of semiconductor devices and systems as well as their recent development progresses. The course is composed of lectures, tutorials and lab sessions. The performance of the students will be assessed by quizzes; midterm exam; assignments;summary of literature search and presentations; lab reports and final exam.

title: Biosensors
description: The Biosensors course will provide an interdisciplinary view of biosensors, focusing on the technological aspects, as well as on implementation and applications, with elements of electronics, photonics, surface chemistry, and biology. The course will present electronic biosensors, optical biosensors, biorecognition and functionalization, and applications of biosensors.

title: Renewable and Sustainable Energy
description: The course aims to provide the students with the fundamentals of energy conversion and renewable energy generation along with resources, and renewable energy sites and potential recognition. Solar, wind, photovoltaic, geothermal, wave, tidal, micro-hydro generation along with battery energy storage systems and DC/AC conversion systems and equipment, design, fabrication, calculation and their operation would be discussed in this course.

title: Convex Optimization
description: The objective of this course is to provide the fundamental mathematical knowledge needed to recognize and solve convex optimization problems that arise in engineering. The topics covered in this course include basics of convex analysis, such as convex sets, convex functions and convex optimization problems; convexity with respect to generalized inequality; least-squares; linear and quadratic programs; semi-definite programming; geometric programming; minimax; optimality conditions; Lagrange dual functions and problems; duality theory; theorems of alternative and applications; and algorithms for solving unconstrained and constrained optimization problems. Students complete hands-on exercises using high-level numerical software.

title: Microfluidic Devices
description: The objective of this course is to introduce students to fundamentals and applications of microfluidics. The course will provide knowledge on physics and theory of microfluidic principles, design and micro-/nano-fabrication of polymer microfluidic devices, materials and microfluidic components, and a wide range of applications of microfluidics through lectures and research case studies.

title: RF and Microwave Circuits
description: This course is designed to train the students in the domain of RF and Microwave circuits & systems design techniques for radio communications leading towards the advancements in the domain of advanced radio technology. The focus of the radio technology concepts treated in this course is on the consumer electronics (5G and beyond) and aerospace electronics segments. This course starts with the fundamentals of RF and Microwave Circuits and will equip the students with the requisite tools and techniques to analyze and design moderately complex building blocks operating at high frequencies. The project is essential component and will enable the student in learning a standard commercial CAD simulator used in industry.

title: Complex Networks: Modeling and Analysis
description: This course provides an accessible yet thorough introduction to network science, an interdisciplinary field for analyzing complex systems across technology, biology, and society. Students will learn the fundamentals of graph theory, network structure, community detection, and dynamic processes, with real-world applications in data-driven research and computational social science. Emphasis is placed on developing both theoretical insight and practical skills for modeling and interpreting networked data.

title: Automation, IIOT and Cybersecurity
description: This course offers an in-depth introduction to the integration of industrial automation, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and cybersecurity, with particular focus on secure remote communication in industrial systems. Students begin with learning core automation concepts, including factory automation, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), their hardware, programming languages, and human-machine interfaces (HMIs). The course then explores how IoT technologies are embedded in industrial environments, addressing data communication, device connectivity, and interoperability. A strong emphasis is placed on cybersecurity principles specifically tailored to protect IIoT networks from vulnerabilities and cyber threats.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Infectious Diseases
description: The goals of this elective are to introduce medical students to the principles of diagnosis and management of various infectious diseases by (1) evaluating patients with infections; (2) participating in clinical rounds; (3) reading current literature and to understand the pharmacology and appropriate use of antibiotics.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Pulmonary Medicine
description: This rotation is aimed at acquainting the student with the diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to the common pulmonary diseases, including lung cancer, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, interstitial lung disease, pulmonary vascular disease, sarcoidosis, and pulmonary infections (bacterial, fungal, viral and mycobacterial).

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Rheumatology and Immunology
description: This elective is an integrated program of patient care, and teaching which involves several UPMC affiliated hospitals. Emphasis is on evaluation and treatment of patients with various rheumatic and immunologic disorders on rheumatology consult service. Students perform initial examinations of patients under the supervision of a fellows and rotating residents and take an active role in teaching rounds with a member of the faculty specifically assigned to the service.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Geriatric Medicine
description: The physician of the future must possess the knowledge and ability to provide optimum care for growing numbers of older adults. The Division of Geriatric Medicine offers students the opportunity to develop these skills and to participate in the continuum of care of older adults across settings (from inpatient to outpatient to long-term care) with a faculty dedicated to teaching. Students will see patients in a variety of clinical settings, which are outpatient geriatric primary care and consultation interprofessional clinics where geriatricians, geriatric psychiatrists social workers, pharmacists, nurse practitioners, endocrinologists (specializing in osteoporosis), cardiologists and continence specialists, provide comprehensive and coordinated care to frail older adults.

title: MSc Thesis in Electrical and Electronics Engineering
description: The key goal of the Master’s thesis is solving a problem relevant to the field of study based on existing scientific and engineering knowledge in compliance with the principles of responsible research conduct. The nature of the thesis should not be underlined too much, since producing new knowledge is not expected for a Master’s thesis, but only for a doctoral thesis.

title: Industrial and Commercial Power System
description: The course aims to provide the student with the fundamentals of electrical, industrial and commercial power systems: design, demand calculation, maintenance, load calculation, management and operation.

title: Advanced Power Electronics
description: The aim of the course is to make a student familiar with the fundamentals of modern advanced power electronics - DC-DC converters including Switched Capacitor Converters with multiphase balanced switching; multilevel DC-DC and DC-AC converters - diode-clamped; flying capacitor; cascade H-bridge; modulation strategies - phase-shifted and level-shifted; analysis of natural voltage balancing dynamics; analysis of voltage and current quality for Pulse Width Modulation and synchronous low frequency switching.

title: Special Topics in Power Engineering
description: This course provides knowledge on alternative sources of energy and all the matters related to the development and usage of this type of energy.

title: Statistical Signal Processing
description: This module is to cover the advance level of Signal Processing course

title: Special Topics in Circuits Theory
description: This module is to cover the fundamentals of mixed-signal circuit design

title: Internet of Things
description: This course provides a core grounding in how science and technology have developed to enable the Internet of Things (IoT) – in a way appropriate for any learner. For those interested in developing further hands-on expertise in designing and developing for the Internet of Things, this course will provide a context to the discoveries and converging technologies that will springboard the next round of innovations.

title: Wireless Communications
description: This module is to cover the topics in Advanced Mobile Communications

title: Simulation and Modelling
description: This module is to cover the topics in modeling and simulation.

title: Optical Communication
description: This module is to cover the topics in Optical Communications

title: Photonics Technology
description: This module is to cover the topics in Photonics Technology.

title: RF and Microwave Communications Systems
description: This course will cover a wide range of topics from the antenna to the baseband level on the modern wireless systems. Focus will be placed on each components of the wireless systems such as antenna systems, filters, mixers, and amplifiers. The second aspect of the course will be on radar and sensor systems such as pulse radar, doppler radar, FMCW radar, and synthetic aperture radar.

title: Modern Control Theory
description: This course will focus on time response and steady state errors, system stability, Roouth-Hurwitz stability criterion, robust control systems, Bode plots, lead/lag compensators design, state space.

title: Random Processes
description: The course will focus on quantitative analysis of uncertainty and risk for engineering applications, design analysis, system reliability, estimation of distribution parameters (method of moments, maximum likelihood, Bayesian estimation) and regression, data mining, design of experiments.

title: Pattern Recognition
description: The aim of this module is to introduce fundamental concepts used in design and implementation of pattern recognition methods. After a brief review of probability theory, we will cover important and classical families of classification rules, error estimation, and dimensionality reduction techniques. Our discussion on classical methods is then followed by a set of modern shrinkage-based techniques for performing classification and regression on very large sparse data matrices.

title: Switched Capacitor Converters (Special Topics in Power Engineering)
description: The aim of the course is to make a student familiar with the fundamentals of Switched Capacitor Converters that can be used as DC-DC step-down and step-up converters. Discussed are conventional series-parallel, charge pump and relatively new reconfigurable Binary, Fibonacci, and Flying Capacitor converters with multiphase and balanced switching. Along with voltage conversion ratio analysis, the course focuses on voltage ripples and converter equivalent resistances. Dual-output Switched Capacitor Converters are considered as well. Analytical methods of Switched Capacitor Converters investigation are supported by computer simulations.

title: System Design for Wireless
description: This course will include: linear and nonlinear system analysis, Radio architectures (super-heterodyne, low-IF, direct conversion, sub-sampling), Receiver system analysis and design, Transmitter system analysis and design, advanced flexible architectures for software defined radio.

title: Elective Clerkship in Pediatric Cardiology
description: 4-week Pediatric Cardiovascular Acting Internship, taking place at Pediatric Cardiology Department at National Research Cardiac Surgery Center.

title: Elective Clerkship in Pediatric Nephrology
description: 4-week Pediatric Nephrology Elective Internship, taking place at UMC National Research Center for Maternal and Child Health.

title: Elective Clerkship in Pediatric Oncology
description: 4-week Pediatric Oncology Elective Internship, taking place in the Oncology-4 department at UMC National Research Center for Maternal and Child Health.

title: Gastroenterology and Hepatology
description: Clinical Elective for MD Year-4 students at NUSOM is offered to increase their interest in Internal Medicine subspecialties and to help them experience variety of clinical disciplines to choose from in the future. Gastroenterology & Hepatology course is chosen to be selected as a common diseases for future Medical Doctors to be seen in their practice. As a clinical sight for this Elective Course a Tertiary Care hospital National Research Oncology Center is chosen with a strong department of Gastroenterology & Hepatology. Students can be exposed to daily routine of the doctors in managing major diseases in this field and English speaking clinical preceptors will be able to give up-to-date knowledge in patient treatment & follow-up.

title: Extracorporeal Hemocorrection
description: The Elective course in extracorporeal hemocorrection is dedicated to get knowledge and practical skills in methods of extracorporeal blood purification such as hemodialysis, plasmapheresis, different modalities of renal replacement therapy in acute and chronic conditions. Students also will be acting in the team as interns: they will admit, manage, and discharge patients with end stage renal disease, chronic kidney disease and acute kidney injury and will be guided as they develop their diagnostic and management skills. This Elective course is offered in the Dialysis Departments of LLP B.B.Nura hospital group located in Str Alikhan Bokeikhan 19/1

title: Radiology
description: Elective Internship: Radiology will be a four week long course that 4-th year MD students can choose . During this course, students will be part of the medical staff and will work with one or more attending physicians. Therefore, the student will be exposed to a variety of radiologic modalities as well as different kinds of pathologies and anatomical variants of human body. Seminars, discussions and lectures will be provided by experienced specialists, with participation of radiology residents. The main aim of the course is to provide knowledge of currently existing radiologic modalities, understanding of their capabilities and application for evaluation of human organs and systems at the level of MD graduate.

title: Elective Clerkship in Pediatric Hematology
description: The Elective in Pediatric hematology will be a 3-week training, consisting of a rotation in the pediatric Pediatric Hematology Program of the UMC Clinical Academic Department. Student will work under a supervision of clinical supervisor, who will be one full-time Attending Physician or Program Lead. After the end of the course the student will be able to achieve the following learning outcomes: • Interviewing patients and parents/guardians, according to their age/development and cultural level, respectively. • Performing physical examination, according to patient’s age and clinical setting. • Organizing a complete and relevant clinical history (including present complaints, past medical history, review of systems, family history, social history and developmental history). • Developing problem-solving skills and critical clinical reasoning, in order to carry on the process of differential diagnosis. • Achieving the final diagnosis through a reasonable, evidence-based and cost-efficient diagnostic process. • Providing oral and written presentation of clinical cases in an organized and informative manner, according to the specific clinical context.
prerequisite: MPED 832 Pediatric Clerkship (5887) (P)

title: Family Medicine Elective
description: This 3-Week Family Medicine Elective course is tailored supporting the development of ambulatory care skills, the treatment of medical and psychosocial problems and preventive health. This course deepens clinical skills in the family practice healthcare Poliklinic n9 Mangilik El 16/1based in Astana .

title: Heart failure
description: Heart failure elective aims to train medical students in the etiology, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure in all stages, and to train on the indications for evidence-based management, including the need for surgical procedures and mechanical circulatory devices.

title: Elective Course Diabetes
description: The Elective course on Diabetes is focused on details in management of Diabetes. Students will be introduced with range of conditions commonly associated with type 1 and type 2 diabetes. The most challenging issues in glycemic control, comorbidities and end-stages of diabetic complications will be highlighted and students will be guided to develop their diagnostic and management skills. This Elective course is offered in the Republican Diagnostic center (UMC), in outpatient settings.

title: International Elective in Medicine
description: Students will be acting in the team as interns during the 3 weeks Rashid Hospital’s General Practice Department in Dubai. They will admit, manage, and discharge patients with general medicine specialties and will be guided as they develop their diagnostic and management skills. This Elective course is offered in Rashid Hospital’s General Practice Department in Dubai. At the end of the 3-week elective course Student will be able to understand the clinical aspects multi-subspecialty internal medicine diseases, will know and interpret the related laboratory analysis and their indications. In particular, the students will demonstrate clinical and practical skills in assessment, evaluation and management of chronic and acute illnesses.

title: International Elective in General Gynecology
description: The General Gynecology Elective Clerkship is oriented around key areas in gynecology that have been identified as essential for medical school graduates to know. This elective course will last for 3 weeks. The location for the O&G 4th year clerkship is the Latifa Women & Children Hospital, Dubai, UAE.

title: International Elective in Pediatrics
description: Pediatric elective aims to train medical students in the etiology, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and treatment of acute and chronic pediatric conditions.

title: International Elective in General Surgery
description: General Surgery aims to train medical students in the etiology, pathophysiology, diagnostics, and treatment of acute and chronic surgical diseases, and to train on the indications for evidence-based management, including the need for surgical procedures and mechanical circulatory devices.

title: ELECTIVE CLERKSHIP IN OPHTHALMOLOGY
description: This 3-week Ophthalmology Elective course is tailored to support the development of eye care skills, the treatment of eye health problems, and preventive health. The course deepens clinical skills within the Ophthalmology Department of the Republican Diagnostic Center.

title: ELECTIVE CLERKSHIP IN ORTHOPAEDICS AND TRAUMATOLOGY
description: This 3-week Orthopedics and Traumatology elective course is tailored to support the development of trauma care skills, the treatment of orthopedic problems, and preventive health. The course deepens clinical skills within the National Research Center of Traumatology and Orthopedics.

title: Family Medicine Clerkship
description: The clerkship in Family Medicine is oriented around key areas that have been identified as essential curriculum for medical school graduates to know. Clinical rotation will last for 4 weeks. The location for the clerkship is TBD.

title: Health, Physical Fitness, and Well Being
description: This is a 4-week hands-on, introductory short course in the principles of health and physical fitness. The course will expose the students to the basic concepts in health, wellbeing, sports and physical fitness.

title: Orientation
description: This module combines the essentials of effective team building with the essentials of effective time management, which is a critical component for personal and organizational success in today’s world of work.

title: Talent Management
description: The course examines talent philosophies, the best practices in strategies and tools to create and sustain the talent pipeline; issues in the area of building and maintaining a strong talent management life cycle.

title: Introduction to Statistics and Research Methods
description: The course teaches Statistics from the management perspective, though it also provides the needed theoretical background for a comprehensive understanding of the presented methods. The course also helps students familiarize themselves with the practice of these methods through the use of specialized software.

title: Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine Clerkship
description: This is a 4 week clerkship The clerkship is a mixture of hands-on patient care experience. Students are assigned to an intensive care unit where they become active members of the care team. They make daily teaching rounds, and follow, assess and treat critically ill patients.

title: Integrated Life Sciences
description: This course will revisit basic science after students have had clinical experience.

title: Mineral Processing
description: The course is aimed at introducing undergraduate mining engineers to the fundamentals of mineral processing so that they can understand the process of ore discovery to market to allow them understand the production chain to optimize the system when needed. This is relevant to the state of the art of mine to mill.
prerequisite: SMG 100 Introduction to Natural Resources Extraction (4773) ( and above) AND MATH 162 Calculus II (170) ( and above) AND CHEM 101 General Chemistry I (113) (C- and above) AND PHYS 162 Physics II for Scientists and Engineers with Laboratory (173) (C- and above)

title: Mine Surveying and Geographic Information Systems
description: This course introduces applications of topographic and geodetic surveying, geospatial and remote sensing technologies applied for mining. This course will present the principles of geospatial data collection using geodetic instruments (Total Stations, Levelling, and GPS etc.), space airborne and satellite technologies. GIS data will be developed in geospatial software for further storage, management, manipulations, quality assurance, spatial analytics, interpretations, cartographic design of maps, geovisualizations and dissemination of produced results.
prerequisite: SMG 100 Introduction to Natural Resources Extraction (4773) (C- and above)

title: Geomechanics
description: This core course is a pre-requisite for other courses covering the engineering applications of soil and rock mechanics including rock breakage, ground control, and surface mine design and underground mine design. Hence, the course aims to establish a framework for understanding the fundamental principles governing the response of geo-materials (soil and rock) to applied loads.

title: Mine Services and Materials Handling
description: This course covers the fundamentals of mine services and materials handling. Mine service part consists of mine power supply, mine maintenance and mine drainage. The other part encompasses the types and selection of equipment and materials handling methods. Continuous and cyclic loading and transportation systems for surface and underground mining operations will be analyzed including: shovel-truck systems, draglines, conveyors, rails, hoisting, and auxiliary equipment.
prerequisite: SMG 100 Introduction to Natural Resources Extraction (4773) (C- and above) AND PHYS 162 Physics II for Scientists and Engineers with Laboratory (173) (C- and above) AND ROBT 201 Mechanics: Statics and Dynamics (475) (C- and above)

title: Resource Estimation
description: This course familiarizes the students with the process of resource modeling.

title: Rock Breakage
description: The course covers the principal methods of rock breakage used in mining including mechanical mining, drilling and blasting. Mechanical mining includes the rock cutting principles, cutting with picks and discs, effect of tool wear, impact breakage and ripping, assessment of rock cuttability and boreability, also, includes machine rock interaction and influence of parameters on mechanical rock breakage. Drilling includes the methods of drilling used in mining application. Blasting includes the chemistry of explosives and mechanics of explosive-rock interaction, selection of explosives, explosive charging techniques; and initiation and delay systems, blast design principles for surface and underground mines.
prerequisite: MINE 302 Geomechanics (5878) (D and above)

title: Underground Mining Systems and Design
description: This course introduces students to high underground mining is conducted for orebodies of different geometries and mechanical properties.
prerequisite: MINE 302 Geomechanics (5878) (D and above)

title: Surface Mining System and Design
description: Analysis of elements of surface mine operation and design of surface mining system components with emphasis on minimization of adverse environmental impact and maximization of efficient use of mineral resources.
prerequisite: MINE 302 Geomechanics (5878) (D and above)

title: Sustainability and Mining Environment
description: This course addresses the sustainability of mining operations and the impact of mining operations on the environment through the introduction and analyzes of the effect of mining on sustainable development including economic, social, and policy aspects of sustainability, and the use of green techniques and technologies aimed at reducing the environmental impact of mining, increasing safety, and improving productivity towards sustainable mining operations.
prerequisite: SMG 100 Introduction to Natural Resources Extraction (4773) (D and above)

title: Mining Geotechnical Engineering
description: The course aims to cover the practical applications of the principles of geomechanics. The course contents include: stability of slopes formed in soil & rock, subsidence, rockbursts and seismicity, ground support, pillar mechanics and design, rock mass classifications and applications, excavation stability, caving mechanics, mine backfill, application of numerical methods, instrumentation and monitoring. The course will incorporate fieldwork (geotechnical mapping) as well as the use of geotechnical software such as Rock science to analyze and design a wide range of geotechnical structures.
prerequisite: MINE 302 Geomechanics (5878) (C- and above)

title: Mine Planning
description: This course is dealing with identifying the mine planning process, mine scheduling and production planning, and analysis of cut-off grades. This course will end up with mine optimization.

title: Coal Mining
description: This course is devoted to surface and underground coal mining systems and design

title: Health, Safety and Sustainability in Mining
description: Fundamentals of managing the occupational safety and health aspects of a mining operation. Includes tracking of accident and injury statistics, risk management and tools, developing a safety and health management plan, etc.

title: Mine Ventilation
description: This course covers the provision of a safe underground working environment through appropriate ventilation practice. Fundamentals of mine ventilation, including control of gas, dust, temperature, and humidity; ventilation network analysis and design of mine ventilation systems. Sustainable mining practices as well as governmental health and safety regulations will be discussed.

title: Mine Robotics and Automation
description: This course's general objective is to equip the students with the knowledge of the technological advances towards implementation of automation and autonomous operations in the mining industry.
prerequisite: SMG 100 Introduction to Natural Resources Extraction (4773) (C- and above)

title: Mining and Environment
description: This course covers studies of the interface between mining, mineral processing, metallurgical process engineering and environmental engineering areas.

title: Mine Risk Management
description: This course will teach students on fundamentals of mine risk management related with risk of injuries / fatalities, environmental, financial, operational and technological. Demonstrates systematic application of policies, processes and procedures to identify, analyze, assess, treat and monitor risk in mining. Introduces a basis of managing the occupational safety and health risks of a mining operation.

title: Mine Design Project
