description: Introduce students to the principles of mine feasibility studies for evaluation of mining projects to determine whether the mineral resource can be mined economically. Develop skills for optimal mine design based on the estimated geotechnical parameters and mining methods selection, mining equipment selection, mine production scheduling, mining costs estimation, mining project economical evaluation, and minable reserves estimation to determine definitively whether to proceed with the project.
prerequisite: MINE 307 Surface Mining System and Design (6150) (C- and above) OR MINE 306 Underground Mining Systems and Design (6151) (C- and above)

title: Mine Design Project I
description: The Mine Design I is intended to be a team final year project along with the Mine Design Project II.

title: Mine Design Project II
description: This course will be a continuation of Mine Design Project I by applying advanced knowledge to mining-related research and design problems to create efficient, safe, sustainable, and cost-effective solutions.
prerequisite: MINE 489 Mine Design Project I (6419) (P)

title: Foundations of Mining
description: This course aims to establish and review the foundation knowledge and insight into mining operations. The course will cover the various areas of mining engineering including open pit and underground mining methods, ventilation, rock mechanics, mine planning, geology, environmental management, mining unit operations, and mining economics.

title: Geology for Mining Engineers
description: This is an introductory course specifically designed for students in mining engineering to give them the necessary background in geology they will need in their future professional career. The course is a condensed version of several more in-depth courses proposed in the B. Sc. Geology program.

title: Applied Geostatistics
description: This course will cover: sampling methodology. Merits of various advanced resource estimation methods variogram, estimation variance, block variance, kriging, and geostatistical simulation. Application of simulation methods in resource estimation including mining and petroleum and how to manage uncertainty in resources estimation.

title: Mine Geomechanics
description: The objective of the course is for the students to develop an understanding of the fundamentals of soil and rock mass mechanical behavior including soil, intact rock and rock mass physical and mechanical properties.

title: Advanced Mine Ventilation
description: This course covers the provision of a safe underground working environment through appropriate ventilation practice.

title: Rock Excavation Methods
description: This course delivers the main rock breakage techniques used in mining including machine mining, drilling and blasting. Machine mining method comprises rock cutting principles, cutting with picks and discs, the design of cutter heads. Drilling covers drilling methods used in mining, selection and costing of drilling equipment. Blasting encompasses mechanics of explosive-rock interaction, selection of commercial explosives, the chemistry of explosives, blast design principles for surface and underground mines, safety, environmental and regulatory management and blast performance assessment and analysis

title: Advanced Rock Mechanics
description: Analytical and numerical modeling analysis of stresses and displacements induced around engineering excavations in rock. Rock deformation and failure criteria. Measurement and monitoring techniques in rock mechanics. Principles of design of excavation in rocks. Analytical, numerical modeling and empirical design methods. Probabilistic and deterministic approaches to rock engineering designs. Excavation design examples for shafts, tunnels, large chambers and mine pillars. Seismic loading of structures in rock.

title: Advanced Surface Mine Design
description: The process, technologies and methods for an optimal surface mine plan and design will be covered in this course.

title: Advanced Underground Mine Design
description: Selection, design, and development of most suitable underground mining methods based upon the physical and the geological properties of mineral deposits (metallic, nonmetallic and coal), conservation considerations, and associated environmental impacts.

title: Mineral Processing Plant Design
description: This course covers studies of importance of process mineralogy for process selection, overview of methods and equipments used for laboratory testwork, development of flowsheets for comminution circuits. Sizing and selection of comminution equipments; crushers, screens, grinding mills and cyclones within a practical exercise.

title: Advanced Tunnelling
description: The course covers the principles and application of tunneling in rock masses.

title: Mine Management and Sustainability
description: The course covers the management principles and practices vital to a mine manager's successful running of a mining enterprise including strategic minerals management; mining law, mine safety and risk management, mine valuation and operations management.

title: Mine Maintenance and Services
description: This course's general objective is to enable the students to develop skills in the analysis and decision making in relation to effective management practices in mine maintenance and mine services.
prerequisite: MINE 502 Geology for Mining Engineers (3691) (C- and above)

title: Multivariate Geostatistics
description: This course covers essential concepts in mineral resource estimation with complexity in formation of ore deposits.
prerequisite: MINE 503 Applied Geostatistics (3692) (C- and above)

title: Geology of Ore Deposits
description: This course is an introduction to the geology, mineralogy, and geochemistry of ore deposits. It is designed specifically for students in Mining Engineering with little or no background in geology. The different types of ore deposits (magmatic, hydrothermal, sedimentary and supergene) will be described in terms of their modes of formation and their petrological and mineralogical characteristics. Examples from Kazakhstan will be used whenever possible for the purpose of illustration.

title: Mechanized Excavation and Tunnelling
description: This course provides a solid background to students for tunnelling in rock masses. It is designed for students in mining, mechanical, civil, petroleum and electrical and electronical engineering with some background in rock mechanics and engineering.

title: Underground Hard Rock Geotechnical Engineering
description: This course provides students with advanced knowledge in underground hard rock mechanics as required for the safe and economic extraction of ore and tunnelling in hard rocks under high stress conditions.

title: Geometallurgy
description: This course provides a technical knowledge for application of geometallurgy in ore characterization. Geometallurgy is an important strategy for any mining project, where the prime objective is to improve the profitability of mines through the use of spatial models of rock properties that have a significant impact on value in a mining project, because it directly influences the revenue from saleable material.

title: Thesis I
description: The students will complete a full literature review for their research topic.

title: Thesis II
description: This course aims to train the students to identify relevant research problem, perform a literature review on a research problem, develop and implement an original methodology to investigate for possible solutions to this problem.
prerequisite: MINE 690 Thesis I (4531) (P)

title: Advanced Mine Geomechanics
description: This course provides students with a practical understanding of the application of the fundamental principles governing the behavior of geo-materials (soil, soft and hard rock) in surface and underground mining environments. It covers: firstly a review of some fundaments of geomechanics; then basic and more advanced applications of geomechanics and finally discusses the implementation of computational tools including numerical modeling, artificial intelligence and data analytics in geomechanics.

title: Current Research Literature
description: This course will help PhD students to become more familiar with the literature of the research direction and research topic they choose as their PhD thesis. This course will help students to prepare their research proposal.

title: Advanced Mining Systems
description: Advanced Mining Systems is a high level discussion of mining systems in a Systems Engineering context. The course is focused on facilitating critical thinking in how various mining systems should be applied to challenging orebodies for safe and profitable extraction of such orebodies. The course will be started with an introduction to Systems Engineering and why systems thinking in mining engineering is critical. Further discussions will include design of unconventional pillars in room-and pillar mining, innovative approaches to the extraction thick and low grade orebodies and coal seams, application of block caving mining to inclined orebodies and super caves, longwall top coal caving (LTCC), transition from open pit to underground mining strategies, super pits, complex orebodies, strategies for mining in burst-prone ground conditions and at ultra-depths and high temperatures, recovery of remnant pillars and multi-seam and multiple lenses, extraction of ultra-narrow orebodies.

title: Advanced Mechanized Excavation and Tunneling
description: Бұл курс студенттерге тау жыныстарының массивтерінде туннель жасауға жақсы негіз береді. Ол тау-кен, механикалық, азаматтық, мұнай-газ және электротехника, электроника және механика салаларында білімі бар студенттерге арналған.

title: Advanced Geometallurgy
description: This course provides a technical knowledge for application of geometallurgy in ore characterization. Geometallurgy is an important strategy for any mining project, where the prime objective is to improve the profitability of mines through the use of spatial models of rock properties that have a significant impact on value in a mining project, because it directly influences the revenue from saleable material.

title: Unconventional Mining Systems
description: This course is intended to educate advanced degrees seekers in mining engineering other sources of valuable minerals and how they could be mined for the benefit of society.
prerequisite: MINE 501 Foundations of Mining (3693) (C and above)

title: Mine Robotics and Automation
description: This course's general objective is to enable the students to develop skills in the analysis and decision making for effective, safe, profitable and sustainable management of automated and autonomous mining operations.

title: Advanced Numerical Methods
description: The objective of this course is to introduce the advanced numerical methods used in rock engineering with application within the mining industry. Fundamentals of continuum and discontinuum mechanics will be reviewed. Theories of continuum and discontinuum modelling techniques will be presented and discussed as appropriate to the development of numerical modelling tools. The governing boundary conditions associated with rock engineering problems and key issues to be considered in the modelling of complex geomechanical problems will be discussed. The application of advanced numerical methods to actual engineering will be demonstrated through case studies and modelling exercises.

title: Doctoral Thesis
description: The “Doctoral Thesis” course fulfills the four-year research/thesis work of the student. A research plan developed by the student in collaboration with the Program Advisor or Research Supervisor at the start of the studies should be accomplished by the end of the semester.

title: Thesis Research
description: A research plan is developed by the student in collaboration with the Program Advisor or Research Supervisor at the start of the semester outlining the research goals to be accomplished. At the end of the semester the student files a research report which is graded (P/F) by the Program Advisor or Research Mentor (when selected). The “in-progress” grade is submitted and maintained on the student’s transcript; credit is awarded on successful completion of thesis requirements.

title: Infectious Diseases Clerkship
description: 4- week inpatient rotation block in Infectious Diseases. Clerkship location is the City of Astana Adult Infectious Diseases Hospital.

title: Research Seminar
description: This course enables students to gain and apply basic research knowledge and skills to select their research projects in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering.

title: Master Thesis I
description: This course intends to give students the opportunity to develop the research proposal.
prerequisite: MMAE 600 Research Seminar (4703) (P)

title: Master Thesis II
description: This course intends to give students the opportunity to fully implement the research proposal and bring it to a conclusion.
prerequisite: MMAE 601 Master Thesis I (5014) (P)

title: Modern Control Engineering
description: The principal objectives of this course are to: 1. Provide a solid background for the understanding of modern control system concepts, analysis, and design techniques. 2. Provide advanced knowledge of control theory in manufacturing such as NC, CNC, etc. 3. Develop hardware and software packages.

title: Advanced Computational Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer in Mechanical Engineering
Advanced Manufacturing Processes and Strategies
description: This course will be covering principles and applications of advanced/ nontraditional machining and additive manufacturing processes. In addition to that, aspect of lean manufacturing and life cycle assessment will be included as well. Under this course, student will be performing, laboratory project and term paper presentation on relevant topic.

title: Research Methods
description: This course addresses the primary need for graduate students to undertake formal training that will help them in understanding how to conduct their research. The course will develop students’ understanding of research planning and engender skills enhancement for reading, interpreting, writing about and presenting key ideas. The course will also instill an understanding of a variety of research methods and ethics, as well as implementation of appropriate strategies in lecture and workshop settings..

title: Advanced Fluid Mechanics with Applications
description: This course aims to further enhance students understanding on the basic principles of fluid mechanics, alongside covering more advanced topics. These include turbulence modeling, microfluidics, fluid flow in porous media, multiphase flows, as well as fluid-structure interactions, and other developing fields of fluid dynamics. Students will study key and analytical concepts like boundary layer theory, order-of-magnitude analysis, time and volume averaging methods, modern fluid mechanics research computational methods, among others. Because of the diversity and scope of these topics, the course will focus one or two areas depending on students’ preferences and previous knowledge.

title: Advanced Statistics and Probability
description: This module is going to develop knowledge about advanced statistics and probability, which is very important for experimental research and results analysis. It will cover statistical methods and probability of events as well as planning of experiments

title: Numerical Techniques for Engineers
description: Ordinary and Partial differential equations, with and without non-linear terms are solved using a variety of numerical techniques.

title: Sustainable Vehicle Transportation Systems
description: The main concerns due to the increased use of transport energy and sustainability will be investigated. A review of current traditional vehicular transport technologies, with emphasis on the energy sources, and especially those of internal combustion engines (petrol and Diesel) and gas turbines will be given. An exploration of how the traditional technologies could be made more acceptable will be made. The course will then move on to a review of the increasingly extensive area of newer cleaner transport technologies and vehicular transport systems with a low carbon future in mind.

title: Advanced Engineering Design and Manufacturing
description: The module is delivered in a project-based format, involving case studies from machine design, space satellite design, aeronautical structures, wind turbines, ground vehicles etc, in the context of running design and research projects with industrial partners. The course makes use of a dedicated Concurrent Engineering Design environment (Machine Design Laboratory), training students in state-of-the-art workflows (CAD/ CAE/ PDM).

title: Design and Manufacturing with Environmental Concern
description: This course addresses fundamental aspects of sustainability in the development of engineering designs and manufacturing. Topics to be presented include: (a) sustainable development; (b) environmental impact of engineering designs; (c) legal aspects associated to mechanical engineering design and environmental impact; (d) Life-Cycle-Analysis (LCA); (e) ISO 14000 Environmental section; (f) integration of recycling in the design; (g) biology-inspired design; and (h) life-cycle cost analysis.

title: Design Optimization
description: The objective of this course is to present tools and methodologies for performing engineering optimization in a multidisciplinary design context. This module will cover all three aspects of the problem: (a) the multidisciplinary requirements of the problem, (b) the appropriate guidelines and methodologies applied in modelling for design optimization and (c) the employed tools and methodologies for optimization. However, focus will be given in the modelling requirements and the modern optimization methods that are used to address such problems.

title: Computational and Unsteady Aerodynamics
description: The course provides deeper knowledge of applied aerodynamics by focusing on computational methods and unsteady flows. During the course, students first review fundamentals of ideal aerodynamics and then extend the scope to include computation of aerodynamic forces for arbitrary streamlined bodies using different panel methods. The course also covers boundary layer corrections to account for viscous drag. Corrections for high speed are also discussed by introducing various compressibility corrections. Unsteady ideal aerodynamics is introduced to examine the effects of sudden plunging, periodic heave and pitching of airfoils.

title: Space Structures Design
description: The course aims to impart advanced competencies in the design of bleeding edge space technologies, such as gyroscopic systems, vibration damping systems, satellite structures, composites, honeycombs, truss-cores and nanomaterials.

title: Computational Fluid Structure Interaction
description: The course aims to introduce the students to an important and complicated topic in engineering: Fluid Structure interaction (FSI) and its analysis by computational simulation. The students will learn to understand the physics, methods and models available for the study of FSI and how to apply them in engineering applications.

title: Space Flight Dynamics
description: This course is designed to provide graduate students with fundamental knowledge and modeling techniques in the most important fields of space flight dynamics, namely, orbital mechanics, rocket vehicle dynamics, and spacecraft attitude dynamics. The whole course will be delivered through a mathematical software package capable of performing symbolical and numerical calculations. With a strong emphasis on scientific problem-solving using programming, this course equips students with the knowledge and skills necessary to become specialists in the field of space engineering.

title: Digital Transformation Concepts
description: This course focuses on developing a systematic understanding and knowledge of key concepts and principles for digital transformation and its current practices, tools and processes and future development. The course will also provide hands-on experience using digital transformation tools and methods to enhance product development and enterprises. The course topics include digital tools, methods to support continuous improvements, design for Industry 4.0, enterprise systems, smart product, virtual and augmented reality (VR&AR), digital twin for product development, model based definition/enterprise, lean digital workflow for product development, and digital transformation industrial case studies.

title: Advanced Materials and Composites
description: This course teaches the latest advances in engineered materials, with a particular focus on high-performance nanomaterials. Their applications in electronics, aerospace, automotive and human-machine interaction are being studied. The course discusses the properties and characteristics of nanomaterials, their integration with polymers, metals and fibre metal laminates and improving their mechanical performance and functional properties. It also teaches how to use machine learning tools and numerical modeling methods to predict mechanical behavior of composite materials.

title: Rocket Propulsion Fundamentals
description: This course is designed to introduce fundamental aspects of rocket propulsion to graduate students. The course builds on a basic knowledge of thermodynamics, including combustion and gas dynamics, all of which are initially reviewed. This is followed by the basic elements of rocket propulsion, introducing performance parameters and important components of a rocket propulsion system. Different types of propellants will be introduced and discussed, including the important non-chemical propellants. The performance of space flight for several flight regimes, namely atmospheric flight, near-space flight and deep-space flight are analysed.

title: Master Thesis in Mechanical Engineering
description: The key goal of the Master’s thesis is solving a problem relevant to the field of study based on existing scientific and engineering knowledge in compliance with the principles of responsible research conduct. The nature of the thesis should not be underlined too much, since producing new knowledge is not expected for a Master’s thesis, but only for a doctoral thesis.

title: Engineering Mathematics
description: This module provides specialized mathematics required for engineers to work and research into problems which require a combination of engineering insight together with rigorous mathematical analysis. The module is designed for students/engineers who have already completed a course in engineering, mathematics or physics.

title: Numerical Techniques for Engineers
description: The unit will assist students to achieve a high level in understanding, proper selection and programming fundamental numerical algorithms to solve practical mechanical engineering problems governed by ordinary and partial differential equations. Students will perform the simulations in personal computers and will explore the principles of validity, accuracy and computational cost of their numerical solution.

title: Advanced Control Systems
description: This course introduces the theories, techniques and computational tools in advanced control systems.

title: Advanced Design and Manufacturing
description: The module explores the couplings between design, manufacturing, operation/ performance, maintenance and end-of-life and equips students with core knowledge regarding the physical principles involved, constitutive models and applicable architectures and design methods.

title: Design and Manufacturing with Environmental Concern
description: This module addresses fundamental aspects of sustainability in the development of engineering designs and manufacturing. Topics to be presented include: (a) sustainable development; (b) environmental impact of engineering designs; (c) legal aspects associated to mechanical engineering design and environmental impact; (d) Life-Cycle-Analysis (LCA); (e) ISO 14000 Environmental section; (f) integration of recycling in the design; (g) biology-inspired design; and (h) life-cycle cost analysis.

title: Design Optimization
description: The objective of this module is to present tools and methodologies for performing engineering optimization in a multidisciplinary design context. This module will cover all three aspects of the problem: (a) the multidisciplinary requirements of the problem, (b) the appropriate guidelines and methodologies applied in modelling for design optimization and (c) the employed tools and methodologies for optimization. Focus will be given primarily in the modelling requirements and the modern optimization methods that are used to address such problems.

title: Advanced Computer Aided Engineering
description: This course aims at bringing the MSc students, who arrive with quite varying backgrounds in Computer Aided Engineering (CAE), up to the same advanced level.

title: Advanced Manufacturing Processes and Strategies
description: This course will be covering principles and applications of advanced/ nontraditional machining and additive manufacturing processes. In addition to that, aspect of lean manufacturing and life cycle assessment will be included as well. Under this course, student will be performing, laboratory project and term paper presentation on relevant topic.

title: Medicine Inpatient I Clerkship
description: 8-week inpatient rotation block in Adult Medicine across a 32-week period. Clerkship location is the National Research Center for Oncology and Transplantation, UMC.

title: Adult Internal Medicine Clerkship
description: This 8 week course in Adult Internal Medicine Clerkship incorporates Adult Inpatient and Outpatient diseases and review pathophysiology of common diseases and complications of hospitalized patients and ambulatory patients. Students will learn how to take an accurate and pertinent history, conduct a physical examination, recognize patterns of illness, and acquire approaches to disease management. All students participate in clinical based learning sessions, didactics and radiology sessions within the rotation. The students will expand their history and physical diagnosis skills, develop the ability to prioritize patient problems, generate a differential diagnosis, implement patient management strategies and to observe the outcome of those strategies. Inpatient clinic will be located at 4 different departments of City hospital N2. Ambulatory patients will be observed at UMC clinics with 5 different specialties.

title: Surgery II Clerkship
description: This 4-week course covers the disciplines of general surgery. The course is oriented around key areas that have been identified as essential for medical school graduates to know. Students should to become familiar with the clinical presentations and management of common surgical problems. The location for the Adult surgery course is City Hospital N2.

title: Medicine Inpatient II Clerkship
description: 4-week inpatient rotation in Medicine. Clerkship location is the Adult City Hospital 2, Astana.

title: Molecular Basis of Infection
description: Major infectious diseases will be taught by a team of experts. The course will cover the molecular mechanisms underlying disease pathogenesis and therapeutic intervention.

title: Bioethics in Research: Principles and Practice
description: Bioethics in Research will highlight the importance of bioethics knowledge for a successful career in science and will increase awareness of the risks related to scientific misconduct and conflict of interests.

title: Inferential Biostatistics
description: Inferential Biostatistics course introduces the major concepts of modern statistics as applied to problems in molecular medicine. The topic begins with an understanding of concepts of probability and distributions and concludes with inferential reasoning and simple regression. Evaluation is based on individual and group problem sets, quizzes and an examination.

title: Biocomputing
description: Biocomputing is an interdisciplinary field focusing on study, design, and implementation of information systems that allow students to perform in silico biomedical research. Students will acquire essential skills through hands-on coursework, essential for the development of the basic knowledge necessary to interrogate in silico systems.

title: Molecular Immunology
description: The Molecular Immunology course will cover the molecular and cellular interactions of the immune response to pathogens and tumor cells as well as mechanisms involved in immunological disorders. The immune system as a target for therapeutic intervention will also be explored.

title: From the Bench to the Bedside: Drug Development and Clinical Trials
description: Overview of the complex pathways that lie between hypothesis regarding pharmaceutical therapies, and the end goal, regulatory approval of a new chemical entity for therapeutic use, and beyond.

title: Natural Medicine
description: The Natural Medicine course will explore the therapeutic properties and mechanism of action of natural products and will consider natural products for prevention and treatment of disease using current scientific research information.

title: Research Methods in Molecular Biomedicine
description: Major methods in molecular biomedicine will be taught including; protein isolation, DNA cloning, PCR, histology, immunofluorescence, microscopy, cell culture etc.

title: Molecular Basis of Chronic Inflammation
description: In this course students will learn about the molecular causes of different chronic inflammations as well as the consequences of inflammation and new treatment possibilities.

title: Molecular Basis of Neurological Disorders
description: Several neurological disorders including the major ones will be discussed by a team of experts. The course will cover the molecular mechanisms underlying disease pathogenesis and therapeutic intervention.

title: Entrepreneurship
description: This course is designed to address the needs of students who hope to pursue startup opportunities, join a new venture as early employees, lead new ventures in established firms, or pursue careers where the ability to evaluate startups would be helpful (e.g., venture capital, mergers and acquisitions).

title: Nutrigenomics
description: Our diet interacts with our genome leading to changes that will impact our health. Various experts in the field will discuss the underlying genetic-nutrient interaction leading to the changes that have important consequences in health and diseases.

title: Basics and Applied Precision Medicine
description: This course provides for theoretical and applied aspects of precision medicine, which include genomics, genetics and epigenetics of disease, and bioinformatics. It also discusses applications of precision medicine in disease diagnosis and management, and analysis of big data. The legal and ethical issues relating to precision medicine and genomics will also be discussed.

title: Molecular Epigenetics in Health and Disease
description: The Molecular Epigenetics in Health and Disease Course investigates how cells deal with gene expression without changing the code encrypted in their DNA sequences. This rapidly developing field of biomedicine intersects molecular biology, genetics, biochemistry and cell biology and thus provides important clues to the molecular mechanisms of various diseases. Furthermore, effects of environmental factors and metabolism on epigenetic mechanisms will be discussed in the context of various genetic disorders with special emphasis on cancer. Finally, the students will be familiarized with general techniques that are used to study the epigenetic phenomena.

title: Natural Drugs
description: This course will provide information on the therapeutic properties of natural products and their mechanism of action. It will also consider the potential use of natural products for prevention and treatment of disease based on current scientific research information. Furthermore, research into the discovery of medicinal resources in natural products will be encouraged.

title: Obstetrics and Gynecology Clerkship
description: The clerkship in Obstetrics & Gynecology is oriented around key areas that have been identified as essential for medical school graduates to know. Clinical rotation will last for 4 weeks. The location for the O&G clerkship is the UMC.

title: Organ Systems Pathophysiology Block I
description: The Organ System Pathophysiology Block 1 covers Neuroscience, Introduction to Psychiatry, Fuel Metabolism, Cardiovascular System, Pulmonary System and Renal System. Anatomy, physiology pharmacology and pathology of the various systems are covered and these basic disciplines are integrated with the clinical presentation, physical examination, laboratory diagnosis and treatment of patients with various diseases.

title: Neuroscience
description: Main goal of NEUROSCIENCE course it to be familiar with the physiological basis of central nervous system and peripheral nervous system, responsible of innervation of muscles, identifying and describing the functional manifestation of neural disorders explaining the etiology.

title: Introduction to Psychiatry
description: In the INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHIATRY course students will familiarize with the main common psychiatric illnesses, identifying how neurobiological factors play out in behavior, and how treatment approaches derive from this understanding. This is the first part of the block (which is in progress) consisting in two courses that will be individually assessed.

title: Organ System Pathophysiology Block II
description: The Organ System Pathophysiology Block 1I covers Endocrine System, Digestion and Nutrition, Hematology and Oncology, Skin and Musculoskeletal System, and Reproductive System. Anatomy, physiology pharmacology and pathology of the various systems are covered and these basic disciplines are integrated with the clinical presentation, physical examination, laboratory diagnosis and treatment of patients with various diseases.

title: Endocrine System
description: Endocrine System course will allow the students to understand the contribution of the endocrine system to homeostasis, common endocrine disease presentations and their treatment.

title: Digestion and Nutrition
description: In the Digestion and Nutrition Course the students will learn the five major organs that constitute the gastrointestinal (GI) tract and their innervation, vascular supply, and sequence of activation during normal digestion; will understand the combination of physical, cellular and chemical events necessary for normal digestion and the physiologic regulation that coordinates these processes.

title: Hematology and Oncology
description: The Hematology and Oncology course is designed to give the students the necessary knowledge of medical hematology and oncology, surgical oncology, radiation oncology, gynecologic oncology, pathology, radiology, biostatistics and behavioral medicine. The students will familiarize with the etiology, pathogenesis and disorders of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, will understand the coagulopathies, anticoagulant and thrombolytic therapies, and will learn the diagnosis, evaluation, and management of hematologic malignancies and different laboratory techniques.

title: Skin and Musculoskeletal System
description: The Skin and Musculoskeletal course will focus on diseases and conditions of skin and musculoskeletal disorders, including connective tissues. The students will learn the etiology, pathophysiology and clinical presentation of common dermatologic and musculoskeletal conditions, will correlate clinical findings with specific disease patterns, and will explain the role of preventative measures in reducing serious skin conditions.

title: Reproductive and Developmental Biology
description: The Reproductive System course covers obstetrics, gynecology, pediatrics and male reproductive system and will focus on the basic principles underlying the normal processes of reproduction and development.

title: Clinical Problem Solving
description: The Clinical Problem Solving course serves as a bridge between pre-clinical coursework and clinical clerkships. Students employ their knowledge base and data-gathering skills gained during pre-clinical coursework. Applying and building upon this foundation, students pursue clinical management of virtual patient cases. The course utilizes a small student group setting with a clinical faculty facilitator emphasizing self-directed and peer group-based learning. Therefore in this course students develop key skills needed for upcoming clerkships, including data-acquisition, clinical decision making, and team-building/professionalism.

The Hematology and Oncology course is designed to give the students the necessary knowledge of medical hematology and oncology, surgical oncology, radiation oncology, gynecologic oncology, pathology, radiology, biostatistics and behavioral medicine. The students will familiarize with the etiology, pathogenesis and disorders of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, will understand the coagulopathies, anticoagulant and thrombolytic therapies, and will learn the diagnosis, evaluation, and management of hematologic malignancies and different laboratory techniques.

title: Public Administration in Theory and Practice
description: The course provides students with an understanding of the theories and practices of public administration in various contexts. Combining historical, contextual and theoretical perspectives, this course gives students a comprehensive overview of the discipline and focuses on the practical implications of public administration theory. Students will read and discuss literature that explores theory and practice of public administrative and governance. Students will also examine several cases that explore practical examples in public administration in various geographical and political contexts.

title: Economic Applications for Public Managers
description: This subject provides a public sector manager's guide to key economic principles, and their applications to public sector activity. Public policy issues are addressed within an economic paradigm. The aim is to help public sector managers make better decisions when allocating scarce resources, when pricing and delivering public sector goods and services and when designing regulations.

title: Public Policy and Management
description: This core MPA course introduces students to key concepts and practices in public management. The course will cover the roles and responsibilities of managers in the design, implementation and evaluation of public programs and policies.

title: Research Methods for Public Managers
description: This course aims to provide students increased understanding of the scientific research process and the tools they will need to read and conduct empirical research in organizational settings. Students should expect to read and analyze scientific literature, write briefs or reports, perform basic qualitative and quantitative analysis. Upon completion of this module, students will know the structure and components of an empirical research paper, the key elements of the scientific method, the different types of investigations developed by the public administration research community. The course will equip the students with the relevant tools to develop their final Master’s Project.

title: Data Models and Decisions
description: Data Models and Decisions introduces students to analytical techniques that establish the optimality of managerial decisions via empirical (“data models”) and logical (“decision modeling”) means.

title: Fiscal Management and Budgeting
description: This course is designed to allow the students to develop a thorough understanding of the theory and practice of public budgeting and financial management. It explores various dimensions of public budgeting and financial management and the significance of resource allocation and management decisions within the public sector in promoting macroeconomic stability, social equity and economic growth/development.

title: Human Resource Policy and Management
description: This course introduces GSPP and other graduate students to human resource management and development (HRM/D) in public and non-profit organizations. It focuses on HRM/D theory and practice as well as issues and challenges that HR managers and professional face today.

title: Program Evaluation
description: Public resources are limited, and decisions regarding how to use these scarce public resources must be informed by an understanding of how well public programs and policies produce their desired outcomes. This course will introduce you to the art and science of evaluation. You will learn methods of collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and communicating information used in evaluation studies.
prerequisite: MPA 602 Public Administration in Theory and Practice (2077) (C- and above) AND MPA 603 Economic Applications for Public Managers (2074) (C- and above) AND MPA 605 Research Methods for Public Managers (2108) (C- and above)

title: Macroeconomics and Public Policy - Focus on Central Asia
description: The course is structured on the premise that the participants have limited background in economics. The participants are introduced the basic principles of macroeconomics starting with foundations of microeconomics.

title: Economic and Social Policy
description: The course is about development, especially economic and social development.

title: Comparative Economic Development
description: The course aims to train students in comparative economic development, for them to draw lessons from other countries and reflect on their implications for KZ.

title: Law, institutions and development
description: This course will provide an analysis of the relationship between law, institutions and development with the core focus on the impact of legal and institutional frameworks in promoting development.

title: Development, Industrial and Finance Policies
description: This elective for the Master in Public Administration students at the Graduate School of Public Policy examines the intersection of development, industrial and finance policies. It begins with a detailed look at key macroeconomic concepts; the monetary, fiscal and external parts of the economy; and how these sectors relate with one another and the flow of funds at the macroeconomic level. The second part of the course is devoted to understanding the process of economic growth—not just various models of growth, but also cross-country experiences and developmental challenges such as the middle income trap, inequality, the politics of growth, and climate change The third part of the course takes a comparative approach, looking at how countries in East Asia have differed in their finance, development and industrial policies. It concludes with an analysis of the recent innovations in behavioral approaches to development. The module emphasizes that economic development is more than economic growth. Development is a complex process that involves coherent growth-enhancing policies, institutional improvements and a sensitivity to a country’s context and circumstances. The module also takes a critical look at the “standard”, universalistic prescriptions of Washington-based institutions—deregulation, privatization, capital account liberalization—and assesses these against the empirical experiences of countries that have succeeded in development. Note: Prior coursework in basic macroeconomics would be useful but not essential.

title: Current Issues in Macroeconomic Policy
description: This course covers current issues in macroeconomic theory and policy. We focus on the role of the financial system in the economy and the importance of financial stability. The topics include current issues in monetary, fiscal, and exchange rate policy in the world and for Kazakhstan and emerging market economies.

title: Contemporary Issues in Foreign Policy
description: The course teaches students how to study and explain foreign policies of states in different international settings as well as explores Kazakhstan external behavior model and national foreign policy decision-making processes and mechanisms.

title: Global Health Policies and Systems
description: This course gives an overview of global health policy and issues, with special focus on changing social, economic, technological and political conditions across diverse systems and populations. It examines the roles and relationships among major players at the global level, and different approaches taken by various international organizations and national governments in tackling health and related problems. Significant challenges in the organization of global health systems and the complexities involved in international cooperation will be analyzed through selected case-studies. Topics on current global health policy and systems issues will include:- population health and development, role of international health organizations, international aid and development assistance, emerging epidemics and disasters, cross-border health issues, health of migrants, migration of health human resources, international trade in health services, medical tourism and the future of global health.

title: Public Policy and Economics of Health Systems
description: This course is an introduction to public policy and health economics, with a special focus on health care systems. It examines the roles and relationships between public policy in planning, implementation and evaluation processes, and different approaches of national systems in providing, regulating and paying for health care. Regional innovations in the organization, delivery and financing of health care systems will be analyzed through selected country case-studies. Seminars and exercises on current topical issues include comparative health and economic policies, private-public participation in the health care industry, stakeholder analysis in health sector reforms and a final project to conduct a public policy and economic analysis of a health system in the country.

title: Public Enterprises for Development: Potential and Limitations
description: The objective of the course is to critically discuss the developmental potential of Public Enterprises (also known as State-Owned Enterprises or SOEs) within the broader historical, legal, economic, political, and managerial contexts.

title: Master’s Project with Overseas Component
description: The Master’s Project is a final requirement for students on the MPA program. It may be conducted as a public policy or management exercise. In both cases, it is expected to be an exercise in which students will be able to apply relevant knowledge and skills gained during the MPA program including: defining and structuring the problem; organizing data; defining and carrying out analysis of the issue; developing specific action recommendations; and defending their findings publicly.

title: Master’s Project with Overseas Component
description: The Master’s Project is a final requirement for students on the MPA program. It may be conducted as a public policy or management exercise. In both cases, it is expected to be an exercise in which students will be able to apply relevant knowledge and skills gained during the MPA program including: defining and structuring the problem; organizing data; defining and carrying out analysis of the issue; developing specific action recommendations; and defending their findings publicly.

title: Master’s Project with Overseas Component
description: The Master’s Project is a final requirement for students on the MPA program. It may be conducted as a public policy or management exercise. In both cases, it is expected to be an exercise in which students will be able to apply relevant knowledge and skills gained during the MPA program including: defining and structuring the problem; organizing data; defining and carrying out analysis of the issue; developing specific action recommendations; and defending their findings publicly.

title: Patient Care Block I
description: In the first year students explore the basis of the unique doctor-patient relationship, with a broad introduction to the profession, getting the techniques of medical interviewing and physical examination through the standardized patients program created and tailored to build strong clinical skills and real selected patients.cted patients.

title: Clinical Experiences I
description: In the CLINICAL EXPERIENCES I students are observers of medical practice in a range of settings, such as primary care ambulatories, clinics and physicians’ offices.

title: Patient Care Block II
description: In the second year students develop their clinical skills about doctor-patient relationship, improving the techniques of medical interviewing and physical examination through the standardized patients program, real selected patients within the UMC Hospitals and simulation devices.

title: Advanced Physical Examination II
description: In the Advanced Physical Examination II course students will apply their leaned skills with selected real patients within the UMC Hospitals, as a flawless continuation with what has been experienced in year 1. They will perform medical interview and physical examination on the patient’s bed, in Russian or Kazakh language, under faculty observation.

title: Clinical Experiences II
description: In the CLINICAL EXPERIENCES II students will live an authentic experience of doctor’s everyday life in the Hospital, primary care ambulatories, clinics and physicians’ offices.

title: Advanced Medical Interviewing
description: For the courses Advanced Medical Interviewing students will interview standardized patients in English language in a controlled environment, experiencing challenging situations and difficulties among patient-doctor relationship.

title: Clinical Procedures
description: Finally the CLINICAL PROCEDURES course introduce students to some of the basic diagnostic and therapeutic invasive and noninvasive procedures that they may perform on patients while on their clinical rotations. This course will be delivered thorugh the state of the art Simulation Centre, through electronic mannequin.

title: Pre-Clerkship
description: Five-days Pre-clerkship introductory program, designed to provide an opportunity to begin the transition from students’ preclinical courses to their clinical training.

title: Internship in Public Policy
description: The purpose of MPE 600 is to provide students with an opportunity to gain insights into the day-to-day operations of an organization in the public, NGO, or multilateral sector, thereby gaining practical experience and advancing their understanding of how policies and processes are shaped by context, institutions, and culture. Students take advantage of the internship to acquire policy-related professional experience, including knowledge and skills that will help them progress towards their long-term professional goals.
prerequisite: (MPP 601 Microeconomics and Public Policy (1449) (C- and above) AND MPP 602 Macroeconomics and Public Policy (1023) (C- and above) AND MPP 611 Statistics for Public Policy (1450) (C- and above) AND MPP 621 Public Policy and Analysis (1451) (C- and above) AND MPP 641 Public Management and Leadership (1907) (C- and above) AND MPP 603 Data Analytics in Public Policy (6618) (C- and above)) OR (MPA 602 Public Administration in Theory and Practice (2077) (C- and above) AND MPA 603 Economic Applications for Public Managers (2074) (C- and above) AND MPA 605 Research Methods for Public Managers (2108) (C- and above) AND MPE 608 Strategic Management and Leadership (2491) (C- and above) AND MPA 610 Program Evaluation (6617) (C- and above))

title: Strategic Management and Leadership
description: Today’s managers and leaders especially those in the public sector operate in an increasingly complex and challenging environment. The emerging socio-political, economic and technological developments demand that public managers reposition themselves, think and act strategically, and employ innovative methods in leading and managing organizations in order to meet the changing demands of various stakeholders. This module introduces the students with unique context within which public managers operate and challenges in leading and managing organizations in the public sector.

title: Organizational Behavior in the Public Sector
description: This course introduces GSPP and other graduate students to Organizational Behavior in the public sector. This course examines 1) the core functions of management and 2) the political socio-economic context in which today’s organizations operate. The course is designed to introduce accepted theories of management and real world applications. To achieve these goals, the course includes in-class group assignments, articles presentation, and final term paper. Lectures and class assignments given in the course are intended to help students understand the needs of modern public and private organizations, including emerging national and international trends. Students will read the assigned textbook as well as other readings posted on Moodle or distributed in-class.

title: National Identity and Public Policy
description: This elective course introduces students to key concepts, theories and practices in national identity and language policies. The course aims to develop understanding of different theories and perceptions of a nation, ethnicity, and nationality. We will also discuss national identity and language policies from public policy perspective.

title: Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Government intervention is commonplace in both developed and developing countries. All governments intervene in their agri-food, environment, health care, natural resources and other economic sectors. These interventions often take the form of projects/programs, policies or regulations and are introduced based on the premise that there is a ‘market failure’. The objective of this course is to provide a greater understanding of how economic concepts can facilitate the decision making process within both the private and public sector. The intent of this module is to equip the student with analytical, economic theory and supporting processes which can be used when facing government policy decisions in order to provide decision makers direction on what should be done.

title: Policy Tools for Addressing Inequality and Demographic Change
description: This course explores the interlinked domains of social policy, inequality, and demographic change through a public policy lens. Students will learn how to critically analyze income and non-income inequality, understand different welfare models, examine the design of family and labor policy, and assess the demographic challenges shaping future welfare systems. Using evidence-based tools and accessible data analysis (Stata, Python, Excel), students will be equipped to interpret key indicators and develop informed policy responses to inequality and social challenges in both developed and developing countries, including Kazakhstan.

title: Scientific Reasoning for Policy Research
description: This course explores the logic and limits of causal inference in the social sciences, confronting the foundational challenge that causal relationships cannot be directly observed or logically deduced from empirical regularities alone. We will critically examine the misuse of p-values, the problem of false positives, model overfitting, and post hoc hypothesis testing. Students will develop a clear understanding that research design, not statistical significance or p-hacking, determines the credibility of causal claims. We explore how data can both reveal and obscure the truth, depending on how it is collected, modeled, and interpreted. Rather than relying on abstract theoretical exposition, the course is grounded in applied case studies from economics, political science, and public policy.

title: Designing and Managing Public Private Collaboration
description: Collaborative arrangements are being adopted across sectors and are relevant for understanding contemporary approaches to solving society's problems. Collaboration is claimed to combine the best of government, market and civil society by bringing together key public and private actors in a policy sector constructively and inexpensively. This course introduces graduate students to collaborative arrangements in public service delivery. Given the wide variety of collaborative arrangements, the course uses a common analytical framework to understand the selection, design, and management of these arrangements. The course covers the design and management of three common varieties of collaborative governance- Contracting, Public Private Partnership, and Networks. Throughout the course, we cover five key questions- why and when to collaborate? What forms of collaborative arrangements are suitable given contextual conditions? How do we design and manage these arrangements? What are the common challenges and to what extent have these arrangements delivered public value?

title: Institutions and development policies
description: This course will provide an analysis of the relationship between institutions and development with the core focus on the impact of institutional frameworks in promoting development.

title: Quantitative Analysis for Managers
description: This class is designed for graduate students, especially public managers, to learn how to conduct data analysis and how to interpret the outputs and to draw policy implications from the results. Lectures in this course will demonstrate how to code and conduct analyses for specific research questions with data.

title: Circular Economy Strategy
description: This course is designed to introduce the circular economy (CE) to learners and provide insights and practice in applying CE strategy to a business context, be it in the private or public sector. Through a project-based learning approach, learners will work independently and in groups to apply CE strategies to organizational improvement.

title: Case Study Research Method
description: The course introduce the students to designing and conducting robust case studies that meet standards for public policy research and publication. The purpose of using a case study method is to develop an in-depth understanding of a phenomenon, based on intensive study of single or multiple units (small-n) representing that phenomenon in a in a real life context, from multiple theoretical perspectives, using multiple methods (survey, secondary data, observation, interviews) . It is a useful approach for both explorative, descriptive as well as analytical types of research. The case study method of research uses both qualitative and quantitative analysis to answer research questions like how and why?

title: Law and Development
description: This course will provide an analysis of the relationship between law and development. The impact of legal and institutional frameworks in promoting development is the course’s core concern.

title: Public Management Reforms in Transitional Countries
description: This module is aimed to improve students’ knowledge and understanding on various public management issues that are facing the governments across the world. These issues include, and are not limited to, the following topics: open government; impact of technologies; public service delivery; ethics and corruption; citizens participation; government-NGO-business collaboration; public management reforms in transitional countries; impact assessment; state-society relations; access to information and a free media; good governance measures; peer-to-peer learning and isomorphic mimicry; and civil service reform.

title: Ethical Challenges in Governance
description: This is an advanced course that centers on normative values and ethical dilemmas in public policy. The key purpose of this course is to prepare students to have a critical perspective on public policy and to be able to evaluate the moral dilemmas that policy makers, politicians, and citizens have to face in the policy-making process and beyond.

title: Open Governance
description: The course is intended as an introduction to the emerging concepts of open government and open data from both theoretical and practical perspectives.

title: Public Policy and Health Issues
description: This course is an introduction to public policy in health and social issues, with special focus on countries and systems experiencing rapid demographic and epidemiological transitions. It will cover population health and development aspects, and the different approaches and methods of public policy in comparing present and future health-related challenges. It will examine the roles and relationships between public policies in planning, implementation and evaluation processes and different approaches of national systems in providing, regulating and paying for health care.

title: Good Governance and Corruption
description: The purpose of this course is to give students an opportunity to familiarize with such concepts, to understand how corruption and good governance promote development, to learn about what international organizations do to promote good governance and contrast corruption, and how they track their progress in both respects.

title: Political Economy of State-Building
description: Reading some of the foundational texts on state-building, this course examines processes, institutions, and functions that make the modern state. This course will analyse processes of state formation and the classification of regimes types, the structure of political and economic institutions, the role of political and economic actors, and processes of governance performance.

title: Finance and Economic Development
description: The global financial crisis of 2007-2012 was the defining economic event of our times. Students of economics and public policy need to have a sound understanding of the causes and consequences of the crisis, the ideas that contributed to it, and how those ideas and their policy implications are debated. Most importantly, students in economics need to be able to understand what went wrong – not just in finance, but also in economics and in development policy, even more so in a pandemic-disrupted world. This is what the course aims to provide.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Governance
description: This course explores the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and governance, examining how AI technologies are transforming public administration, policy-making, and citizen engagement. Through case studies, theoretical readings, and practical tools, students will critically analyze the opportunities and challenges of AI adoption in the public sector.

title: Big Data Applications in Public Policy
description: This course explores how big data can be used to understand and solve policy challenges. Students will work with real datasets, including spatial data, to learn how to map patterns, analyze inequalities, and assess the impact of policies. The focus is on practical skills that combine spatial analysis and big data tools for evidence-based decision-making.

title: Foreign Policy Analysis
description: This module introduces key concepts and theories in foreign policy analysis and applies those concepts/theories to empirically examine foreign policy decision-making in various context, including in Kazakhstan and other Central Asian countries. The module follows a "levels of analysis" structure and begins with “systemic” sources of foreign policy, and then moves to “state” and “individual” level sources. By the end of the course, students will be expected to understand the fundamentals of foreign policy analysis and build a comprehensive knowledge of Kazakhstan’s foreign policy.

title: Innovation Management
description: This course provides students with the opportunity to understand how to create and manage innovation strategies, manage innovation teams and apply innovation strategies to organizational contexts and challenges. A key outcome objective of this course is to provide students with the skills necessary to lead innovation initiatives and produce financially-viable, impactful innovations.

title: Social Entrepreneurship
description: This course gives students an understanding of social entrepreneurship through a human-centered design process. The module takes students, stage-by-stage, through the process of conceptualizing, designing and creating a social enterprise that addresses a social problem facing a community.

title: Policy Lab
description: Policy Lab is a hands-on, project-based course that connects academic learning with real-world policymaking. Working in interdisciplinary teams, students collaborate with client organizations – government bodies, international institutions, NGOs, or private partners – to address real policy challenges. Through defining problems, analyzing data, designing and evaluating policy options, and presenting evidence-based recommendations, students gain practical experience in policy research and teamwork. The course promotes creativity, critical thinking, and an understanding of how policies are developed and implemented. Guided by faculty and client feedback, teams deliver final presentations showcasing their findings. By the end, students can translate complex issues into actionable research questions, conduct systematic analysis, and propose innovative, feasible solutions. Policy Lab equips future policymakers and analysts with practical skills, adaptability, and ethical awareness to become effective contributors to policy innovation and public problem-solving.

title: Contemporary Security Challenges in Central Asia and Beyond
description: This course examines security challenges in a contemporary context. We explore various security threats and issues including but not limited to human, food, and health security, immigration and border security, terrorism, and environmental security in the Central Asian region and beyond.

title: International Financial Policy
description: This course covers international finance and macroeconomic issues including the foreign exchange market, exchange rate determination, output determination under fixed and flexible exchange rates, current account balances, international capital movement, exchange rate regime choice, and the causes and consequences of speculative currency crises.

title: International Political Economy
description: This course aims to introduce students at an advanced level with the contemporary issues in international political economy, theoretical frameworks, and research approaches to analyze the issues of international political economy. The key issue around which the course develops its subject matter is international cooperation in various policy areas and the role of international institutions in facilitating global governance of global issues such as trade, finance, development, climate change, and other social and macroeconomic policies.

title: Globalisation and Public Policy
description: This course is designed for students working in public, private or non-profit sectors with some background in political economy and policy making. It introduces students to the analysis of globalization – widening and deepening of international interconnectedness –and its impacts on national policy making substance and processes. Some of the questions this course deals with include what are the major issues brought forward by globalization, how can we think about them analytically, and what kinds of policy options are available to policy makers under the opportunities and constraints placed by globalization.
antirequisite: MPE 640 International Political Economy (1307) (C- and above) OR DPE 623 International Political Economy (6338) (C- and above)

title: The Media and Public Policy
description: The course is intended as an introduction to the concept of media politics from both theoretical and practical perspectives.

title: Communications for Public Leadership
description: Public policy is not just made. It must be explained. To be effective in positions of authority, future public leaders in democratic societies need to be able to communicate succinctly and strategically, be that with their colleagues, or the wider public via an increasingly fast-moving digital media environment. This course provides practical techniques to improve student's spoken and written abilities, and helps them to practice these skills in challenging real-world situations, from winning over hostile audiences to writing punchy op-eds suitable for publication in global media outlets.

title: Macroeconomic Development and Human Capital
description: The goal of this course is to provide a framework for the analysis of macroeconomic development so that students will be able to analyze and understand the implications of macroeconomic policies for economic development through specific country-case and cross-country studies. The course explores the main drivers of economic growth, cross-national differences in growth, poverty and income inequality, the role of human capital, technology and institutions in economic development by overviewing and applying the major tools of macroeconomic policy and models of economic growth.

title: Environmental Economics and Public Policy
description: This course will provide a comprehensive overview of the interaction between economy and environment and its policy implications with focus on Kazakhstan.

title: Public Sector Innovation
description: This class is for students who are interested in public sector organizations and their innovation and reform, especially for the MPP, MPA, and PhD students in public policy. This course examines core functions of public sector innovation (PSI) and management and the political, socio-economic context within which organizations operate in different sectors, focusing on innovation.

title: Science and Technology Policy
description: The course is intended as an introduction to the concept of science and technology politics from both theoretical and practical perspectives.

title: Agricultural Policy Analysis
description: The course examines the design, implementation, and impact of agricultural policies. Students will examine the role of agriculture in economic development and food systems by applying economic principles to analyze key policy instruments, such as subsidies, price supports, and quotas. Through exercises and case studies, students will gain a practical understanding of how agricultural policies influence market outcomes and rural livelihoods. The course also covers trade policy, regional integration, and contemporary challenges in the agricultural and food sectors. Topics include agricultural trade, non-tariff barriers, the EAEU and EU’s CAP frameworks, food security, land governance, and environmental sustainability. Case studies and guest lectures from regional experts will provide practical insights. Students will be assessed based on their class participation, a midterm exam, group presentations, and case study analysis.

title: Health System and Policy
description: This is an introductory course on health, healthcare system and health policy. The course provides an overview and application of healthcare and health policy related key concepts needed for policy analyst and managers. During this course students will apply critical concepts from Public Health, Healthcare Economics, Policy Analysis, and Systems Thinking to health policy challenges facing middle income countries.

title: Applied Public Economics and Finance
description: Public economics examines government tax and spending policies: what does government do, what are the effects of these actions, and are these effects ‘good’ or ‘bad.’ This course applies economic theory to analysis of public policy using the microeconomic model of consumer behavior and studies empirical examples to evaluate theory, focusing on the casual effects of policy interventions on economic outcomes.
prerequisite: MPP 601 Microeconomics and Public Policy (1449) (B- and above) OR MPA 603 Economic Applications for Public Managers (2074) (B- and above)

title: Governance Through Networks: Theory and Practice
description: Network governance refers to inclusive and participatory approaches to policy-making, collective action, and implementation. This course is designed to addresses ways to work together across institutional, geographic, economic, and social boundaries in many different policy domains, such as natural resource management, public health, and community and economic development.

title: Behavioural Insights and Public Policy
description: Behavioral economics uses variants of traditional economic assumptions (often with a psychological motivation) to explain and predict behavior, and to provide policy prescriptions. Some examples include the cases when • people try to choose the best feasible option, but they sometimes don’t succeed; • people care (in part) about how their circumstances compare to reference points; • people have self-control problems; • people mostly care about our own material payoffs, but they also care about the actions, intentions, and payoffs of others, even people outside our family; • market exchange makes psychological factors cease to matter, but many psychological factors matter even in markets. This course is a brief introduction to the behavioral toolbox in public policy.

title: Game Theory and Public Policy
description: Game theory is a framework for analyzing strategic interactions between rational actors. The tools of game theory are employed widely to understand a variety of phenomena in politics, economics, business, and biology. This course will introduce the fundamentals of game theory and guide the student through some prominent applications of it, with special emphasis on applications in public policy. The course will also touch on basic social choice theory and bargaining.

title: The Third Sector: civil society, nonprofit organizations, and voluntary action
description: This course considers the Third Sector, a topic closely associated with civil society, characterized by voluntary behavior and nonprofit organizations, and that stands in contrast to the governmental and for-profit sectors. The course examines theories and concepts of civil society, with application across national contexts but with particular regard to Kazakhstan.

title: Development Assistance and Governance
description: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be equipped with knowledge of the foundations of and issues/challenges in development assistance and public administration reform. Topics will include an introduction to the key institutions of development assistance, the role of international organizations in promoting public administration reform, internal governance of international development organizations. The assessment strategy will include both open-book/takeaway assignments and in-class/controlled env. assessments in addition to class participation.

title: Urban Mobility Policy in the Age of the Smart City
description: This ‘applied public policy’ elective links public policy principles with key urban transport policy choices and the transport policy opportunities and challenges arising from recent technological change. While focusing on urban transport it also provides opportunities to apply concepts from other public policy courses. Although the course would provide an introduction for students hoping to go further on urban transport issues, the course is primarily aimed at policy generalists. Many policy-related professionals need to be discerning consumers of both urban transport policy analysis and of pitches from technology system and service vendors. This course will not make its participants urban transport experts but it will prepare them to engage in critical and constructive discussion with technical experts in urban transport and transport-related technology applications. The course draws on examples from a variety of places and situations around the world.

title: Natural Resource Management and Policy
description: Natural resources policy and management in the 21st century is guided by the paradigm of sustainability to balance human benefit and environmental protection. This balancing act presents critical challenges given the variety of resources, diversity of interests, and multitude of impacts on ecosystems, while interlinkages among these aspects further complicate decision making and elevate the risk of mismanagement. This course unravels the complexity through the prism of governance consisting of state, market and community as well as hybrid institutions, and assesses the effectiveness of their associated policy instruments.

title: Sustainable Development and Environmental Governance
description: This course will provide a comprehensive overview of the sustainable development concept, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and entailing public policies through an inter-disciplinary framework. Sustainable development is the most urgent challenge facing humanity. Its fundamental question is: How can the world economy continue to develop in a way that is socially inclusive and environmentally sustainable? This course provides a broad overview of the interactions between the economy and our environment and humanity, from the constraints of finite resources, to the activities that drive climate change, to equality for all.

title: Energy Systems and Climate Policy
description: This course examines the role played by various energy resources in fueling modern economic growth from early industrialization through present and provide a basic understanding of the technology, economics, social, and political aspects of various energy systems (non-renewable and renewable) for public policy analysis and the various energy options for climate change mitigation and adaptation. This course is organized into five broad sections: energy and economic development; non-renewable energy utilization and constraints; renewable energy policy and options; climate change science and policy; energy transition and sustainability. While the course is pitched in a larger international context, specific examples of energy policy issues relevant to Kazakhstan and the Central Asian region are covered in each lecture.

title: Global Energy Policy
description: This course applies the policy cycle to energy sector whereby a variety of approaches are analyzed at the stages of agenda setting, formulation, decision-making, implementation and evaluation. Drawing on cases from the Global North and South, including Central Asian region and Kazakhstan specifically, a mix of energy policies and associated instruments are critically examined. The perspective taken is that of a policy maker confronting decisions about the design and implementation of energy policy that is informed by the learning from practices in different contexts, while focusing on ways that public policy can affect social and environmental outcomes.

title: Water Resources Policy and Management
