description: Understand the concept of integrated water resources management (IWRM) through an inter-disciplinary approach, apply holistic models on IWRM for the development of better policy decisions and incorporate the complexities of transboundary water systems on policy frameworks.

title: New Technologies and Public Policy
description: This module will focus on TECH FOR GOOD or how new technologies can be used to improve the welfare of societies and how to minimize their harm. This course is also known as ABCD-EFGHIJ. ABCD refers to new, disruptive technologies (AI, Autonomous Systems, Blockchain, Cloud and Quantum Computing, Cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin/Ethereum, Libra, etc), Data Analytics, 3D, 5G, etc). We will examine the benefits, risks and problems associated with ABCD in terms of EFGHIJ (Education, Energy, Economic Development, Freedom/privacy, Finance/Banks, Government/Governance, Healthcare, Jobs and Inequality, Inclusion etc).

title: Data Analytics for Public Policy
description: This class is for graduate students studying public policy. The class is customized that students apply statistical knowledge to examining models explaining public policy and public administration issues. So, the main purpose of this class is to provide knowledge of statistics so that students can conduct regression analysis to address their research questions. During the first half of the class, students will learn probability distribution, hypothesis testing, and confidence interval. During the second half of the class, bivariate and multiple regression analysis, Difference in Difference Method, MNLM, etc. will be taught.

title: Pediatric Inpatient Medicine Clerkship
description: The Pediatric In-patient Medicine Clerkship is oriented around key areas that have been identified as essential for medical school graduates to know. Clinical rotations will last for 4 weeks in each department. The location for the PIMC is the UMC NRCMCH.

title: Microeconomics and Public Policy
description: MPP601 is a core module in the Master in Public Policy program and is a prerequisite for many of the other modules in the program. The main aim of the module is to provide you with a set of tools to model individual and firm behavior, the economic outcomes that result from this behavior, and their application in the formulation of public policy.

title: Macroeconomics and Public Policy
description: Macroeconomic developments are a central theme of policy debate around the globe. This course provides a sound understanding of macroeconomics for students wishing to become proficient civil servants, policy experts, or analysts in the field of public policy. This is a core course in the MPP program and is a prerequisite for many of the other modules in the program. This module assumes that you are comfortable with basic mathematical skills. We begin by reviewing the microeconomics content of MPP601 and extend the discussion on selected topics to an advanced level. We devote the remainder of the module to explore the study of macroeconomic policy analysis.

title: Data Analytics in Public Policy
description: This class is for graduate students studying public policy at the GSPP. The class is customized that students apply data analytical knowledge to examining models explaining public policy and public administration issues. So, the main purpose of this class is to provide knowledge of data analytics relating to various models with continuous or categorical dependent variable, in addition to including moderators or mediators as well as Big Data analysis, so as to address students’ own research questions. During the semester, students will learn and practice how to code mainly Stata or R and Python if necessary, so as to conduct empirical analysis on their own research questions in the end.
prerequisite: MPP 611 Statistics for Public Policy (1450) (C- and above) AND MPP 601 Microeconomics and Public Policy (1449) (C- and above) AND MPP 621 Public Policy and Analysis (1451) (C- and above) AND MPP 613 Policy Research Design and Methods (1301) (C- and above)

title: Statistics for Public Policy
description: The purpose of this course is to equip students with the necessary statistical tools and model building expertise that are related to the empirical analysis of public policy problems in a professional environment. Students can apply these tools for descriptive as well as inferential purposes: policy evaluation, and explaining bivariate and multivariate relationships in general. The course begins with an introduction to statistical and probability theory, probability distributions, types of data, inferential statistics, hypothesis testing, correlation analysis and ends with bivariate and multiple regression.

title: Public Policy Research and Evaluation
description: This module introduces students to the basic concepts and methods in social science research and their application in public policy analysis. It focuses on the development of students' professional skills in research design, data collection techniques, and analysis for the purposes of conducting policy research and evaluation.

title: Policy Research Design and Methods
description: MPP613 is a core module on the Masters in Public Policy Program and provides students with an early appreciation of the main elements of doing research in public policy. The module is delivered in three parts: Part 1 introduces what ‘research’ in Social Sciences is, what the main components of a research paper are, and how to write those components (abstract, introduction, literature review, and etc.); In Part 2, participants learn about the role of concepts and theories in doing social science research; Part 3 provides students with the basics of quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods approaches in conducting an empirical inquiry. At the end of the course, students come up with a research proposal that can be eventually used for their PAEs (Policy Analysis Exercises).

title: Public Policy and Analysis
description: Government officials are frequently confronted with decisions about whether or not to initiate, continue, modify, or terminate policies or programs, and the knowledge about public policy and skills in policy analysis is essential for them to make intelligent choices. The course will cover important considerations in conducting policy analysis and evaluation, such as identifying policy problems, establishing criteria, assessing policy alternatives, choosing among policies, and evaluating policy impacts.

title: Central Asian politics: Comparative Analysis
description: The course aims to analyze key developments in political, economic, and security dimensions in each of the five nations through the prism of a holistic perspective on Central Asia as a single and distinct world region.

title: International Political Economy of Energy and Climate Change
description: The module enables students to better understand and answer questions like: (a) why is there a lack of international cooperation on energy and climate change issues, (b) how does globalization and international institutions impact the energy policy choices of states, (c) how do national structural and political features mediate international pressures, (d) what are the trade-offs in choices between various energy resources (coal, oil, gas, nuclear, renewable), (e) what are the trade-offs between security, economic development, human rights, and the environment, and (f) how do states, markets, international institutions and other non-state actors interact the global energy regime complex.

title: Economic Growth in Developing Asia
description: This course is designed for students with substantial interest in economic development who may be involved in economic analysis and policy making in their future careers. The overall objective of this course is to provide students with a robust understanding of Asian economic growth experiences, the Asian economic growth models, and strategic policy frameworks for lower income countries to rapidly catch up with richer nations. The course also helps students examine the growth policies and experience of Kazakhstan and discuss how the country can learn from the successful Asian nations to achieve higher economic performance in the years to come.

title: Politics and Public Policy
description: This core course introduces MPP students to relationship and interplay between public policy and politics. This course covers key topics such as the role of government; public and private sector relations and dynamics; political-administrative relations; collaboration and networks; performance management; stakeholder management; and ethics and anti-corruption strategies. Case studies and class discussions throughout the course will ensure that students are able to link research insights and conceptual frameworks to practice.

title: Weapons of Mass Destruction Nonproliferation and Disarmament
description: In this course, students will learn about issues related to the Nonproliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD): nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons.

title: International Financial Policy
description: This course covers international finance and macroeconomic issues including the foreign exchange market, exchange rate determination, output determination under fixed and flexible exchange rates, current account balances, international capital movement, exchange rate regime choice, and the causes and consequences of speculative currency crises.

title: Public Management and Leadership
description: This core module aims to introduce MPP students to key theoretical concepts and practices of public management and leadership in a cross-institutional and cross-border manner. The effect of public management and leadership models and strategies on the performance on government institutions and implementation of public sector reforms all over the world is truly an important subject which the module addresses.

title: Personal Effectiveness for the Public Sector
Social Policy and Economic Development
description: Modern governments are extensively involved in ensuring the population's physical and economic well-being./Озық елдер тұрғындардың физикалық және экономикалық әл-ауқатын күшейтуге кеңінен ат салысуда./Современные государства широко вовлечены в обеспечение
antirequisite: MPP 622 Economics, Philosophy and Public Policy (1304) ( and above)

title: National Identity and Language Policies
description: This elective MPP course will examine policies of national identity, language and culture in different countries around the world, including transitional and/or multiethnic societies. Identity is crucial to public policy design and this is particularly evident when examining how identity issues in different countries have affected policies. Oftentimes, governments formulate and implement targeted public policies to address the needs of their population. During the course, students will read essential works of influential social theorists, including Gellner, Anderson, Smith, Foucault, Bourdieu, Geertz, and Brubaker. Students will also work on studying and designing practical public policy implications in ethnically diverse societies.

title: Public Project Evaluation and Analysis
description: The module is an introduction to the tools used in financial and economic evaluation of projects from the perspective of governments or development agencies.
prerequisite: MPP 601 Microeconomics and Public Policy (1449) (D and above)

title: Urban Planning and Public Policy
description: This course will introduce graduate students to the major themes in City and Regional Planning.

title: Science, Technology, and Public Policy
description: This course will examine the role of science and technology in public policy and decision-making. Topics covered in the course include foundations of science and technology policy, institutions and processes for science policy and scientific input for government and lawmakers in developed and developing countries, and the implications of digital revolution and disruption for society and government. Other relevant topics such public interest science, role of scientific academies and independent scientists in policymaking, and public science communication and engagement to support participatory governance and decision-making will also be covered.

title: Singapore Component
description: Students will have the unique opportunity to spend three weeks in Singapore./Студенттер үш апта бойы Сингапурда болудың бірегей мүмкіндігіне ие болады./Студенты получат уникальную возможность провести три недели в Сингапуре.

title: Policy Analysis Exercise with Overseas Component
description: The PAE is a public policy or management study, completed for a client or a target organization (where possible). It is, in essence, the applied version of the traditionally theoretical Master thesis. It requires each student to define and analyze an actual policy issue.
prerequisite: MPP 601 Microeconomics and Public Policy (1449) (C- and above) AND MPP 611 Statistics for Public Policy (1450) (C- and above) AND MPP 613 Policy Research Design and Methods (1301) (C- and above) AND MPP 621 Public Policy and Analysis (1451) (C- and above)

prerequisite: MPP 613 Policy Research Design and Methods (1301) (C- and above)

title: Patient Physician and Society Block
description: Longitudinal Courses Block that ensure the student to understand his role in society (ethics, law and professionalism) and to connect with different patients that may need special support (behavioral medicine) in terms of substance addiction and health promotion.

title: Medical Ethics and Professionalism
description: Medical Ethics and Professionalism is focused on understanding the role of doctor in the modern society, through the different concepts of ethics, professionalism and the law related to the medical healthcare profession.

title: Behavioral Medicine
description: The BEHAVIORAL MEDICINE course is oriented on some special skills of the modern doctor that has to face psychological topics like motivational interview, dealing with addicted patients and embracing the important role of health promoter.

title: English-Russian-Kazakh Medical Terminology
description: Aim of this course is to help students transition between the medical education given in English language and the Kazakh bilingual clinical setting in Russian and Kazakh languages.

title: Psychiatry Clerkship
description: The clerkship in Psychiatry Medicine is oriented around key areas that have been identified as essential curriculum for medical school graduates to know. Clinical rotation will last for 4 weeks. The location for the clerkship is Mental Hospital in Astana city.

title: Organ system and common diseases
description: This course describes the human body in healthy and diseased states.

title: Cellular Communications
description: This course will cover different aspects of cell signaling in health and disease states and include a short practical to familiarize students with some laboratory techniques used in signal transduction research.

title: Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology
description: In this course students will learn about the basic principles and mechanisms of commonly used drugs and how they exert their actions.
corequisite: MPTX 501 Organ system and common diseases (5841) (C and above)

title: Drug Discovery I
description: The course will introduce students to the drug discovery world, particularly the preclinical stage.
corequisite: MPTX 503 Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology (5843) (C and above)

title: Systemic Pharmacology II
description: The course aims to provide students with the core knowledge about the action of drugs on various systems of the human body.
prerequisite: MPTX 503 Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology (5843) (C- and above) AND MSBM 604 Systemic Pharmacology (5844) (C- and above)

title: Research Methods in Pharmacology
description: During this course students will learn fundamental concepts, methods, and tools and their applications in bio-medical research.
prerequisite: MPTX 502 Cellular Communications (5842) (C- and above) OR MPTX 503 Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology (5843) (C- and above)

title: Drug Discovery and Development II
description: Students will be able to outline and critically appraise the principal steps in drug discovery and explain the rationale for a complete development plan (clinical development) according to the proposed therapeutic indication.
prerequisite: MPTX 505 Drug Discovery I (5845) (C- and above)

title: Environmental Toxicology
description: Students will learn to apply theory, concepts, methods and approaches utilized in the investigation of environmental health problems in the fields of environmental toxicology, occupational health and environmental sciences.

title: Biostatistics and Critical Appraisal
description: The course aims to: 1. Provide students with the epidemiological and biostatistical skillsets to design and conduct studies to answer clinically important research questions associated with pharmaceuticals. 2. Provide students with the the epidemiological and biostatistical skillsets to critique clinical peer-reviewed journal pharmaceutical-related articles for validity and utility.
prerequisite: MPTX 503 Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology (5843) (C- and above) AND MPTX 505 Drug Discovery I (5845) (C- and above)

title: Current Topics in Pharmacology and Toxicology
description: The course aims to: 1. Provide students with up to date information and knowledge about current issues in the pharmaceutical industry. 2. Provide students with the necessary scientific knowledge to critique peer-reviewed journal pharmaceutical-related articles for validity and utility. 3. Provide students with the necessary scientific and regulatory knowledge to evaluate new drugs and review drug withdrawal.
prerequisite: MPTX 503 Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology (5843) (C- and above) AND MPTX 505 Drug Discovery I (5845) (C- and above)
corequisite: MSBM 504 Biostatistics and Critical Appraisal (8517) (C- and above)

title: Scientific Writing
description: This course will highlight the importance of scientific writing for a successful career in science.

title: Natural Therapeutics
description: This course will provide information on the therapeutic properties of natural products and their mechanism of action. It will also consider the potential use of natural products for prevention and treatment of disease based on current scientific research information. Furthermore, research into the discovery of medicinal resources in natural products will be encouraged.

title: Molecular Toxicology
description: Course will teach how different toxicants can disrupt physiological processes on a molecular and cellular levels leading to organ system dysfunction and possibly to a disease.

title: Research Project and Thesis
description: This is a research based course. Students will develop and test a hypothesis under the supervision of qualified researcher. They would have developed the required skills and knowledge to conduct their assigned research projects.
prerequisite: MPTX 601 Biostatistics and Critical Appraisal (6342) (C and above) AND MSBM 601 Introduction to Research Project (6344) (P)

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - General Anesthesiology
description: The fourth year elective is intended for future anesthesiologists or those physicians for whom acquiring the knowledge and skills utilized by anesthesiologists will be important (i.e. emergency medicine, critical care medicine, surgery). The student will be expected to perform as an acting intern and participate in all aspects of perioperative care.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Pain Medicine
description: This four-week rotation elective provides exposure to predominantly chronic and cancer pain patients.

title: Bioethics
description: The course is focused on theoretical concepts of Bioethics in Biomedical Research and the application of these concepts in research, innovations and future perspectives

title: Metabolism in Health and Disease
description: This course provides a comprehensive molecular-level introduction to human metabolism.

title: Research Methods in Molecular Biomedicine
description: Modern methods in molecular medicine and molecular biology play an instrumental role in understanding the major molecular mechanisms underlying a variety of biological processes in the state of health and disease

title: Nutrition Science
description: This course covers essential nutrients required for human health, the digestion and absorption of key nutrients.

title: Musculoskeletal System
description: This course introduces the human anatomy to the prospective sports medicine graduates.

title: Exercise and Biomechanics
description: This course will enable the students to understand how different muscles, bones, and tendons work together to produce motion. The course will cover how an understanding of Biomechanics can help in refining mobility techniques during sports and exercise.

title: Internship in Sports and Exercise Sciences
description: Internship in Sports and Exercise Sciences will enable students to acquire skills in comprehensive diagnosis, management and rehabilitation of athletes, people of all ages with injuries, neuromusculoskeletal disorders, associated illness and disabilities.

description: In this course students will learn about the basic principles and mechanisms of commonly used drugs and how they exert their actions.

title: Drug Discovery
description: The course will introduce students to the drug discovery world, particularly the preclinical stage.

title: Molecular Basis of Infection
description: Infectious diseases accompanied humans throughout evolution. From early days to modern times infection is tirelessly challenging our defense systems with old and new mechanisms, ultimately modifying our species by leaving traces in our genome and phenotype.

title: Molecular Basis of Neurological Disorders
description: Neurological disorders remain among the most devastating diseases affecting mankind for several reasons including the unavailability of effective treatment.

title: Molecular Immunology
description: The Molecular Immunology course explores the molecular and cellular interactions that occur during the immune response to microbes and tumor cells, as well as the irregular immunological responses that occur during allergy, autoimmunity, immune suppression and transplant rejection.

title: Introduction to Research Project
description: The course aims to: 1. Provide the students with scientific process of literature search 2. Allows students to appraise scientific literature 3. Provide students with scientific writing skills

title: Current topics in biomedical research
description: The course will train the students in critically analyzing research article in the areas of Molecular Medicine. The course will focus on the current concepts in these areas, covered through reading and critical discussion of selected scientific literature.

title: Advances in Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation
description: In this course, students will learn about the new developments, both in terms of concepts and technology, in the areas of Sports and Rehabilitation. In the newly established, cutting-edge Rehabilitation facility in NU Athletic Center, students will also learn about technological advances made recently in the assessment of movement/mobility, and its application in improving athletic performance and in injury rehabilitation.

title: Systemic Pharmacology
description: The course aims to provide students with the core knowledge about the action of drugs on various systems of the human body.
prerequisite: MSBM 512 Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology (8727) (C- and above)

title: Molecular Toxicology
description: The course aims to provide students with adequate knowledge of the biological basis and toxicological effects of drug of abuse and addiction.
prerequisite: MSBM 512 Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology (8727) (C- and above)

title: Molecular basis of Genetics and Epigenetics Disease
description: In this course we will examine the human genome architecture, discuss the role of coding and non coding DNA including the relevance of DNA repeats, copy number variation, ncRNA and miRNA to health and diseases. We will compare and contrast single gene disorders to multifactorial disorder using representative examples. Cellular gene expression regulation and mis-regulation and their importance to health and disease will be discussed. The interaction of genes and the environment and epigenetic modification and it’s impact on gene expression will also be examined. New strategies such cell and gene therapy including stem cell therapy and their effectiveness will be critically appraised.

title: Molecular Basis of Cancer
description: Molecular Pathology will be presented as a fast growing practical discipline developed to identify molecular changes in different cancers from the perspective of their routine laboratory analysis and their application in the clinic for prognostic classification and targeted drug therapy.

title: Robots for Rehabilitation
description: This course will cover how the human musculoskeletal system is modeled and simulated using computers to design robotic exoskeletons that can assist in the rehabilitation of neurological and sports injuries. Students will learn how to use robotic technology to rehabilitate patients in recovering their lost motions and strengths.

title: Recombinant and Natural Drugs
description: This course will cover the history and impact of genetic engineering on medicine and their regulatory aspects, with examples of recombinant proteins, recombinant vaccines and gene therapy applications that were approved for human medical intervention.

title: Developmental Biology
description: The course will teach the theory underlying, and the techniques used to understand, the molecular mechanisms of growth and development of animals. Developmental processes that go awry resulting in human fetal abnormalities will be described.

title: Adaptive Physical Activity
description: This course covers principles of adapted physical activity prescription for people with different age, physical capabilities and co-morbidities.

title: Research Method and Ethics
description: This course addresses the primary need for graduate students to undertake formal training that will help them in understanding how to conduct their research.

title: Technical Communication
description: This course provides the graduate students with skills to write their research reports and scientific articles in English with proper use of style and grammar, as required in international conferences and journals. This course also trains the graduate students to deliver effective and appealing professional and scientific presentations, with attention to best practices in the use of technical English and vocal-gestural communication.

title: Advanced Applied Mathematics
description: This course reviews and deepens the advanced analytical and numerical methods to solve ODEs and PDEs. The whole course, lectures, and tutorials will be delivered through a mathematical software package capable to perform symbolical calculations. The module is designed for graduate students to cover their research needs concerning mathematical modeling via analytical, semi-analytical or numerical techniques.

title: Advanced Statistics and Probability
description: This module covers applied statistical methods and probability for master students.

title: Research Methods
description: This course addresses the primary need for graduate students to undertake formal training that will help them in understanding how to conduct research and their master thesis.

title: Environmental Science & Technology
description: To give students an understanding of environmental science and management To provide students the engineering tools needed to solve environmental problems

title: Summer Research
description: Research in Summer.

title: Scholarly project
description: The scholarly project is a longitudinal block and will run from the 2nd year 2nd semester until the 4th year 2nd semester. During the course of the scholarly project the student will learn about the different aspects important to conduct good research and he/she will conduct her/his own independent research under the supervision of a faculty member. The student will start by writing a research proposal with the help of her/his supervisor.

title: Financial Modeling
description: In this course the students are introduced to the modelling of time value of money problems, investment decision problems, financial evaluation of projects, and the valuation models of securities that are commonly used by corporations (bonds and stocks).

title: Thesis Preparation Seminar
description: Students first learn the structure of a master thesis and its basic components, see examples of successful theses, and learn about the research process. The rest of the seminar is practical: students go through a mock empirical research process.

title: Advanced Econometrics
description: This is the second econometrics course in the Econometrics sequence of the MSF Program at NU. The course prepares students to conduct empirical work in finance and economics.

title: Private Equity
description: This course introduces students to private capital markets

title: Internship
description: This capstone project is intended to represent a synthesis and application of the program learning outcomes and demonstrate business competence, exceptional teamwork skills, knowledge of core business theory, and effective communication skills

title: Banking and Credit
description: "Credit Risk Modeling" course first examines the influence of credit risk on the structuring and pricing of fixed income – styled assets. In a second part, we consider the essentials of proper modeling of credit risk, the modeling of intensity and recovery of default, the estimation of defaults and transition matrices and the markets for asset- or mortgage backed securities, and credit default swaps. We also discuss specific asset and legal issues surrounding synthetic constructions and hybrids with distinctive fixed income components

title: Economic Policy in Global Markets
description: This course empowers students to evaluate national economic policy choices for emerging markets.

title: Microeconomics for Finance
description: This course provides rigorous training in microeconomic theory of relevance to finance

title: Corporate Governance
description: The course provides the information that allows organizations to take deliberate approach in designing governance systems.

title: Independent Research
description: This MSF elective course gives extra research time to students who are research-oriented and want to write a research-based thesis of high quality.There are two conditions under which the students can take the course: They opt for individual thesis (as opposed to group thesis), and they obtain written approval from a faculty member who is expected to serve as their thesis advisor.

title: FinTech
description: FinTech is the term for technology and innovation that targets frictions in the traditional financial industry. In this course you will learn how the FinTech industry creates value by lowering unit processing costs, resolves asymmetric information issues and discusses how network effects are introduced.

title: Financial Accounting
description: This course equips students with knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary for detailed examination and evaluation of financial accounting information in order to make informed financial and business decisions.

title: Industry Insights Initiative
description: The Industry Insights Initiative is designed to provide GSB students with exposure to various industries and job functions through direct interaction with industry leaders.

title: Industry Insights Initiative
description: The Industry Insights Initiative is designed to provide GSB students with exposure to various industries and job functions through direct interaction with industry leaders.

title: Advanced Empirical Methods
description: This course equips students with practical tools in empirical economic analysis, with a focus on methods and applications relevant to policy work in institutions such as the National Bank of Kazakhstan.

title: Musculoskeletal System
description: This course introduces the major concepts human musculoskeletal anatomy, structure and movements of joints, Neurovascular anatomy and a brief overview of thoracic and abdominal organs.

title: Nutrition in Sports and Exercise
description: Students completing the course will be able to identify basic terms and nutrition concepts in relation to sports performance and recovery. They will be able to apply the basic principles of dietary assessment in evaluating requirements for sports and fitness. The students should demonstrate the ability to analyze and apply current research findings to communicate appropriate dietary recommendations in the areas of sports nutrition. Assessments of the learning outcomes will be carried out by a combination of group reports and presentations.

title: Exercise Genetics, Physiology and Endocrinology
description: In this course, we will first look at the foundations of genetics starting with the human genome architecture, the role of coding and non-coding genes such as miRNA and ncRNA, we will examine the various types of mutations, discuss using examples, the differences between single gene and multifactorial disorders and the various modes of genetic inheritance.

title: Pharmacology in Sports and Rehabilitation
description: This course will provide a basic understanding of fundamental principles of pharmacology and toxicology. Students will learn general concepts of pharmacology and then learn to apply them to specific contexts of sports medicine.

title: Exercise and Biomechanics
description: This course will enable the students to understand how different muscles, bones, and tendons work together to produce motion. The course will cover how an understanding of Biomechanics can help in refining mobility techniques during sports and exercise. This course will consist of lectures designed to use the knowledge of biomechanics to physical activities such as locomotion, exercise, sports. In practical sessions, students will be familiar and capable with the biomechanical methods and tool for evaluation of human movement performance features with the following aims: preventing injuries, improving movement efficacy, and measuring rehabilitation progress.

title: Seminar in Sports Medicine
description: This course is an exercise in critical analysis of ongoing research in the areas of Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation. The course will focus on the current concepts in these areas, covered through reading and critical discussion of selected published scientific literature.

title: Management and Rehabilitation of Injury
description: This course will cover the rationales behind prevention and treatment of musculoskeletal injuries among athletes and non-athletes. Importance of maintaining proper form and physical habits in preventing injury will be discussed. Mechanisms and techniques of rehabilitation involved in relieving pain, achieving recovery as well as exercise protocols for musculoskeletal injuries will be covered. The course provides the knowledge and skills necessary to plan, implement, and supervise of progressive reconditioning and healing programs. Students will learn how to examine the process of recovery and identify precise stages of healing to be able to prepare evidence-based programs. Methods comprise progression and sequencing, examination and evaluation, and application of soft tissue and joint mobilization; flexibility and range of motion, muscle endurance and strength exercises; agility, coordination, and balance activities as well as function return to do normal physical activities and for a full return to sport participation.

title: Biostatistics and Epidemiology
description: This course introduces the major concepts of modern statistics as applied to problems in sports medicine. The topic begins with an understanding of concepts of probability and distributions and concludes with inferential reasoning and simple regression. Evaluation is based on individual and group problem sets, quizzes and an examination.

title: Introduction to Research Project
description: This course is an exercise in proposal writing for quantitative and qualitative research projects.

title: Internship in Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation
description: Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation (SMR) Internship will enable students to acquire skills in comprehensive diagnosis, management and rehabilitation of athletes, people of all ages with injuries, neuromusculoskeletal disorders, associated illness and disabilities.

title: Nutrition for Life
description: This course is an interactive course where students learn about nutrition and food components and the risk and benefits of each nutrient if they consume them in excess or insufficient amount. The students will learn about foods in different cultures as well as Kazakhstan, and they also study nutrition throughout different lifecycles. They can incorporate what they learn in order to plan a healthy diet and lifestyle based on their individual goals.

title: Clinical & Motivational Interviewing
description: This course will take an evidence-based approach that will help future MSMR practitioners incorporate effective communication skills and strategies into every consultation—from taking a medical history through to therapy and evaluation. The course is a combination of lectures, small group activities, standardized patient (SP) interviews, and self-directing learning.

title: Psychology of Sports and Rehabilitation
description: This course will enable the students to understand how psychology plays a role in achieving optimal level of performance in sports. Students will also learn about the skills required to maintain patient motivation throughout an injury rehabilitation process.

title: Advances in Sports and Rehabilitation
description: In this course, students will learn about the new developments, both in terms of concepts and technology, in the areas of Sports and Rehabilitation. In the newly established, cutting-edge Rehabilitation facility in NU Athletic Center, students will also learn about technological advances made recently in the assessment of movement/mobility, and its application in improving athletic performance and in injury rehabilitation. The course will cover technical approaches and concepts related to mental as well as physical aspects of sports and rehabilitation.

title: Master Research Project
description: This course will enable students to develop advanced research skills in the field of Sports Medicine and Rehabilitation. Students will utilize the fully functional and readily available laboratories at the School of Medicine and the Sports and Rehabilitation facilities at the NU Athletic Center to conduct their research under the guidance and supervision of qualified faculty from the School.

title: Ethics and Professionalism
description: This course will cover the aspects of Ethics and Professionalism from various angles. Students will learn about misconduct in athletic events, including the abuse of performance enhancing drugs. Additionally, professional misconduct in research and medical practice will be covered.

title: Master Research Project Thesis
description: Master Research Thesis will be culmination of the Master Research into a scientifically articulate finished project, ready to be presented and defended in front of a panel of experts. The students will apply their acquired critical thinking skills to carry out advanced scientific research.

title: Theoretical Foundations of Advanced Nursing
description: This course comprehensively explores and analyzes health behavior models and nursing theories as foundations for advanced nursing practice. Graduate students will deeply understand how various factors interconnect in behavior initiation and changes.

title: Advanced Physical and Health Assessment
description: The course emphasizes the practical use of advanced health assessment methods to conduct thorough and tailored health evaluations in diverse healthcare settings for patients of all ages.

title: Statistics for Nursing Research, Evidence-Based Practice, and Quality Improvement
description: This course introduces graduate students to statistical concepts, principles, and methods vital for Nursing Research, Evidence-Based Practice, and Quality Improvement projects.

title: Informatics and Healthcare Technologies
description: This course explores emerging technologies and healthcare information systems that manage clinical information and support safe patient care.

title: Health Policy and Advocacy
description: This course delves into the intricate world of healthcare policy, legislation, and advocacy.

title: Nursing Research, Evidence-Based Practice, and Quality Improvement
description: This course is meticulously designed to guide graduate students to the scientific core of nursing knowledge—research. It enables graduate students to employ the scientific method in exploring research phenomena in nursing, health, and healthcare.

title: Advanced Pathophysiology
description: This course critically examines normal physiology and pathological alterations, forming the cornerstone for clinical assessment, planning, nursing intervention, and precise patient condition evaluation.

title: Advanced Pharmacology
description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of pharmacological principles, drug classes, mechanisms of action, and therapeutic applications.

title: Learning and Teaching Strategies and Innovation in Nursing
description: This course focuses on innovative and evidence-based classroom and clinical teaching strategies helpful in delivering an effective and holistic teaching-learning process.

title: Population-Based Health Promotion and Clinical Prevention
description: This course provides graduate students with the concepts and practices of population health, underscoring health promotion, disease prevention, and healthcare disparities.

title: Nursing Leadership Development
description: This course focuses on applying leadership theory and cultivating critical leadership skills essential for success in today's dynamic healthcare landscape. The course emphasizes vital nursing leadership competencies, including professionalism, business skills and principles, knowledge of healthcare environments, communication and relationship management, situational and transformational leadership.

title: Organizational and Systems Management for Healthcare Leaders
description: Organizational and systems management and leadership skills are critical for healthcare and enhanced outcomes. This course delves into applying organizational, leadership, and management theories with a focus on transformational leadership, change theory, outcomes measurement, and data driven decision-making in both macro- and microsystems.

title: Financial, Business, and Economics Drivers in Healthcare Management
description: This course is designed to familiarize graduate students with the essential concepts of business, economics, and financial management in healthcare organizations and how they influence patient care. Students will learn key financial terms, the relevance of healthcare finances in today's complex healthcare environment, and the ability to develop and monitor budgets for practice initiatives.

title: Clinical Nurse Leader Practicum 1
description: Clinical Nurse Leader Practicum 1 provides graduate students a foundational experiential learning opportunity as a clinical nurse leader. Graduate students will have 150 hours of supervised clinical experience in diverse settings.

title: Thesis Planning
description: This course allows students to develop a nursing research proposal addressing a specific practice problem in the chosen area of practice or major. The students will synthesize and integrate the acquired knowledge and competence from the theoretical courses and practical experiences into a research proposal.

title: Surgical Specialty Clerkship
description: Clerkship of 4 - week inpatient rotation in Surgical specialties. Each rotation consists in one- week period for ENT, Ophthalmology, Orthopedic and Urology. Clerkship locations are UMC National Scientific Center of Oncology and Transplantation and Republic Diagnostic Center in Astana.

title: Scientific Reasoning Block I
description: This course provides an introduction to tools of analysis of particular relevant in clinical decision-making and in the reading of medical literature

title: Scientific Reasoning Block II
description: This longitudinal block is designed to give students foundation for using basic and clinical sciences in medical decision making. It will teach students to think critically about concepts relevant to medical decision making, including diagnostic reasoning, biostatistics and experimental design, etiology, prognosis and survival, therapies and studies of their effectiveness. The block consists of two courses.

title: Surgery I Clerkship
description: This 6-week clerkship overview covers the disciplines of general surgery. The course is oriented around key areas that have been identified as essential for medical school graduates to know. Students should to become familiar with the clinical presentations and management of common surgical problems. The location for the surgery clerkship is National scientific center for oncology and transplantation.

title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I and Lab
description: This course is designed to present students with a basic foundation in normal human anatomy and physiology. Topics covered are: cell physiology, histology, integumentary, skeletal, muscular, nervous and sensory systems. Emphasis is on the interaction of structure and function and the mechanisms which maintain homeostasis in the human body. The laboratory component is designed to provide students with hands-on experience related to the anatomy and physiology of the human body using preserved specimens, anatomic models and interactive 3D Anatomage Table technology (computer models of muscular, neural, bone, and organ systems). This complements the didactic component of NUR 101, with the same emphasis on structure and how it relates to function and the maintenance of homeostasis in the entire body.

title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II with Lab
description: This course is designed to present students with a basic foundation in normal human anatomy and physiology. Body systems covered include endocrine, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, and embryological development. Emphasis is on the interaction of structure and function and the mechanisms which maintain homeostasis in the human body. The laboratory component is designed to provide students with hands-on experience related to the anatomy and physiology of the human body using preserved specimens, anatomic models and interactive 3D Anatomage Table technology (computer models of muscular, neural, bone, and organ systems). This complements the didactic component of NUR 102, with the same emphasis on structure and how it relates to function and the maintenance of homeostasis in the entire body.

title: Microbiology for Nurses with Lab
description: This lecture course will introduce students to the basic properties of bacteria, archaea, eukaryotic microorganisms and viruses, with an emphasis on bacteria. The diversity within the microbial world will be emphasized, as well as their relevance to the health and diseases of humans. Approaches for controlling the growth of microbes in the environment and for preventing the spread of infectious diseases will also be discussed. In addition, students will also become familiar with host-microorganism interactions and host-immune responses. The laboratory component will provide students with hands-on experience in terms of the techniques used to detect, grow, isolate and identify microorganisms.

title: Introduction to Professional Nursing
description: This course provides a broad overview and synthesis of the issues and trends most relevant to the practice of professional nursing. Historical, contemporary and potential influences on professional nursing practice are reviewed. An emphasis on the unique and varied roles of nurses in today's interdisciplinary health care environment are examined within the context of individual, family, community, and global health. Characteristics and major changes in health care delivery systems (local and national) are discussed. Components of professional nursing values and core practice competencies are presented. The concept of an evidence-based approach to clinical practice is introduced. The nursing process is introduced and critical thinking strategies are outlined in the context of the nursing process.

title: Introduction to Basic Statistics for Evidence-Based Practice
description: This course introduces students to descriptive statistics and parametric and nonparametric statistical tests that are commonly used by researchers in the health sciences and appear in published research reports. Emphasis is place on student mastery of concepts and principles that are fundamental to descriptive and inferential statistics as well as interpretation and critical appraisal of their use in research studies. Students will also practice examining data to identify trends and identify problems in both the patient and on the clinical unit.

title: English-Russian-Kazakh Medical Terminology
description: The aim of this course is to enable medical and nursing students to switch fluently from English to Russian and Kazakh languages when they will be exposed to the local clinical settings with Kazakh doctors, healthcare professionals and above all patients. Students receive a thorough grounding in basic medical terminology through a study of root words, prefixes and suffixes for the different three languages. The study focuses on correct pronunciation, spelling and use of medical terms and abbreviations in English, Russian and Kazakh (ERK) language.

title: Pathophysiologic Foundations of Nursing Care
description: This course will examine mechanisms that produce disease and injury, the ways in which the body responds to these mechanisms, and the clinical manifestations produced by the body's response.

title: Introduction to Genetics and Molecular Therapeutics
description: This is an introductory course that focuses on the fundamentals of genetics. The course is designed to give the student a basic understanding of genetic concepts so that this knowledge can be utilized to understand current and future genetic theories and therapeutics.

title: Pharmacology and Therapeutics
description: This course provides an introduction for pharmacology that integrates the concepts of physiology, pathophysiology, chemistry, and nursing fundamentals to build a foundation for administering drug therapy to patients. Using a simple to complex approach, key content areas are presented to help conceptualize the important components related to pharmacology. The basic concepts of pharmacology, such as drug testing and approval, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, pharmaco-therapeutics and toxic effects, dosage calculations, and challenges related to drug therapy, provide the foundation from which drug therapy associated with specific body systems can be addressed. Discussion of the major drug groups focuses on therapeutic actions and indications, mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, contraindications and precautions, adverse effects, clinically important drug-drug interactions and nursing implications which emphasize the nursing process and focus on patient care and education. Prototypes of the major drug groups are emphasized. Lifespan considerations, evidence for best practice, patient safety, and critical thinking are integrated throughout the course.

title: Nutrition Essentials for Nursing Clinical Practice
description: This course focuses on nutrition for clinical practice for nursing students beginning their clinical practicum. Food for energy and the major nutrients are considered for the promotion of health and for medical nutrition therapy for selected disruptions of health. The most valuable contribution to clinical care in nursing is the ongoing assessment and monitoring of patient status. Emphasis in this course is placed on nutrition assessment and interventions in relation to current evidence-based practices and examines the influence of tradition and culture on nutrition.

title: Psychology for the Health Practitioner
description: Psychology is defined as the study of behavior or the study of mind and behavior. Health psychology is the study of psychological and behavioral processes in health, illness, and healthcare and is concerned with understanding how psychological, behavioral, and cultural factors contribute to physical health and illness. This course provides an overview of psychology as it pertains to health behavior and health care deliver. Foundational knowledge will be developed which can be applied to inform health care practice. Theories and research evidence of relevance to the health practitioner in the management of patient care are presented, including such areas as changing health behaviors, learning and motivation, and behavior and emotion in chronic disease.

title: Foundations of Nursing Practice I
description: This course focuses on the concepts of communication, therapeutic intervention, and decision-making as they relate to the nursing process. Techniques of assessment of the physical, psychological, and developmental dimensions of the individual are explored through a variety of learning strategies. Variations of expected findings based on influences such as age, social condition, and culture are discussed. Emphasis is placed on the therapeutic interventions of safety, hygiene and comfort, health assessment and health promotion. This lab component is designed to provide lab/clinical-like experiences related to the theory provided in Foundations of Nursing Practice 1. Techniques used in the assessment of the physical, psychological and development dimensions of the individual within an acute care setting are demonstrated.

title: Foundations of Nursing Practice II
description: The focus is on the cognitive basis, scientific principles, and manipulative component of psychomotor skills used when providing nursing care which promotes, restores and maintains the health of the patient. During laboratory sessions, students will have the opportunity to practice simulated clinical skills. Nursing process, critical thinking and decision-making serve as the framework for acquisition of clinical psychomotor skills. Through active laboratory participation, the student will demonstrate self-direction as a learner.

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing I: Clinical
description: This course focuses on the nursing care of adults, including older adults, with acute and/or chronic illnesses. Students will be guided in critical thinking exercises and the use of therapeutic interventions and research findings in the management of adults. Nursing process, critical thinking, and decision-making serve as the framework for acquisition of knowledge for the management of patients. Societal and cultural influences will be emphasized. During clinic, students will have the opportunity to practice clinical skills learned in the lab. The students’ ability to apply the nursing process, critical thinking, and decision-making serve as the framework for acquisition of clinical psychomotor skills. Common concepts of care will be emphasized, including societal and cultural influences.

title: Nursing Research: Introduction to Critical Appraisal and Evidence-Based Practice
description: This course is designed to provide the opportunity for students to become intelligent consumers of research and to provide the basis for evidence-based practice and the provision of culturally-congruent care. Students gain an understanding of the application of quantitative and qualitative research processes to the development of nursing knowledge and the contributions or research to the evidence base of nursing practice. Students are expected to critically appraise research articles, distinguish between useful, valid research and that which cannot or should not be applied to nursing practice. Completion of CITI (Collaborative Institutional Training Initiative) training will be required.

title: Nutrition for Clinical Practice
description: The course focuses on nutrition for clinical nursing practice where nurses’ assessment and intervention is applied.

title: Physical Assessment Across the Lifespan
description: The course focuses on the nursing performance of a comprehensive physical assessment, and psycho-socio-spiritual assessment among patients of all ages.

title: Nursing Care of Older Adults
description: The course focuses on the concepts, principles, and evidence-based nursing care for older adults and their families.

title: Introduction to Basic Statistics for Evidence Based Practice
description: The course assists students to develop an understanding and mastery of the concepts and principles of descriptive and inferential statistics.

title: Research Methods for Nursing
description: The course builds on NUR 304 Introduction to Basic Statistics for Evidence Based Practice and introduces students to the concepts and principles of quantitative and qualitative research design. The focus is application of the phases of the research process, including the methods of data collection, sampling technique, and ethics in research. Students will evaluate frameworks for formulating evidence based questions. The students will also learn to search the literature, read, and evaluate evidence-based research studies.

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Complex Medical Management for Acute and Chronic Patient
description: The course focuses on the nursing care of adults, including older adults, with acute and chronic illnesses. Students will be guided in critical thinking exercises and the use of therapeutic interventions and research findings in the management of adults. Nursing process, critical thinking, and decision-making serve as the framework for the acquisition of knowledge for the patient management. Societal and cultural influences will be emphasized.

title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention in Culturally Diverse Populations
description: Health promotion and disease prevention are examined from theoretical foundations to clinical applications. The course focuses on individual and community health promotion assessment, screening, and interventions in diverse populations. Epidemiological principles and real clinical examples are discussed as a basis for focusing on health promotion assessment and interventions. Course topics are delineated according to factors related to health care disparities among vulnerable populations. Current research in health promotion and disease prevention is the basis for identifying appropriate interventions in diverse populations and settings. World Health Organization global health initiatives to reduce premature mortality will be discussed. United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals will be integrated throughout the course.

title: Enhanced Communication in Professional Nursing
description: The course is designed to provide information about basic principles of effective communication in the practice of professional nursing. Units of content and learning activities focus on writing skills, presentation skills, communication as an image builder, barriers to effective communication in the workplace, and strategies for enhancing communication in the healthcare environment and among the healthcare team. Frequent opportunities for skill development and practice are provided. The goal is to enhance the proficiency of the professional nurse in a variety of situations that require effective communication.

title: Obstetric Nursing + Clinical
description: This course provides an introduction for the process of childbirth and the dynamics of the childbearing family. It explores the areas of health promotion, physiologic changes associated with pregnancy, high risk conditions associated with pregnancy and the development of the fetus and newborn. Emphasis is on adaptation to the biopsychosocial needs of the childbearing family with sensitivity to the cultural needs and ethical issues of a diverse population. Critical thinking, problem solving, stress adaptation, role, family and nursing theories provide a major focus for understanding childbearing. Clinical experiences reflect a diversity of settings including outpatient, inpatient, and community programs that provide services to the childbearing family. The students’ ability to apply the nursing process, using critical thinking skills, is expanded through clinical activities. The clinical setting will provide collaboration opportunities with interdisciplinary health professionals to foster health promotion and restoration.

title: Pediatric Nursing + Clinical: Care of Children and Families
description: This course focuses on the unique health and developmental needs of infants, children and adolescents with an emphasis on family-centered care. The course incorporates principles of assessment, planning and implementation of nursing interventions appropriate for health promotion, wellness, health restoration and various complex health problems. Nursing approaches are based on the use of best evidence, developmental perspectives, and cultural competence with a focus on critical thinking. For the clinical component, nursing care approaches are based on the use of best evidence, developmental perspectives, and cultural competence. The nursing process is applied to the child and family to minimize the effects of stressors which have resulted in a disruption of health. There is an emphasis on critical thinking and decision making as the student applies theory to nursing care.

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing II: Complex Surgical Management and Clinical
description: The most valuable contribution to clinical care in nursing is the ongoing assessment and monitoring of patient status. Research on patient outcomes states that advanced nursing care is more likely to prevent failure to rescue and other poor outcomes. This course is designed to provide the nurse with in depth competencies in the care of adults and older adults undergoing complex surgical procedures. Students will be guided in critical thinking exercises and the use of therapeutic interventions and research findings in the management of adults with acute and chronic illnesses that have received surgical intervention as part of their treatment plan. Emphasis is placed on using the nursing process for the prioritization and decision making processes of nursing care and the nursing responsibilities associated with translating, integrating and applying surgical management; evaluation of outcomes; and support for patients and families experiencing complex surgical problems. The clinical nursing responsibilities include interpretation of diagnostic studies, medical/surgical patient management, evaluation of outcomes, health promotion, and support for individuals and families experiencing acute and complex health problems. This course includes application of cultural diversity awareness training to the nursing process. Clinical learning is focused on developing and refining the knowledge and skills to manage patient care as part of inter-professional teams. Clinical experiences are offered in acute care, critical care, and monitored units.

title: Psychiatric Nursing and Clinical
description: This course is designed to teach basic psychiatric mental health nursing concepts and their application to clinical practice. Classroom learning is focused on developmental, psychological, and biological theories in order to enhance understanding of psychiatric illness. Major psychiatric illnesses throughout the lifespan as well as contemporary methods of treatment are addressed. Emphasis is placed on understanding the unique contributions of social and cultural factors to mental health.

title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
description: Chronic diseases continue to be among the leading causes of death. Global health initiatives discussed by the World Health Organization to reduce premature mortality will be discussed. This course focuses on individual and community health promotion assessment, screening, and interventions in diverse populations.

title: Ethics in Healthcare
description: This course introduces students to the domain of clinical ethics as a foundation for developing ethical expertise in nursing and medical practice. The course focuses on contemporary nursing and health care issues that raise personal and professional ethical concerns. Emphasis is placed on cultural differences, current legislation, political and religious controversy, economic constraints, and professional commitment related to the resolution of the identified ethical dilemmas. The process of ethical analysis and reasoning is used to resolve representative patient and health care situations.

title: Education: Principles and Practice for Teaching in Nursing
description: The course is designed to develop a theoretical, practical, and evidence-based foundation for students in the education of clients/patient/families, nurse colleagues, and other health care providers.

title: Capstone I: Evidence-Based Clinical/Quality Improvement Research Project Development
description: The course explores concepts related to data analysis within the healthcare environment and will focus on healthcare practice outcomes for quality improvement.

title: Community and Home Health Nursing
description: The overall objective of this course is to provide the student with a broad introduction to community and home health and the role of nursing within this context.

title: Medical-Surgical Nursing: Complex Surgical Management
description: The course focuses on the nursing care of hospitalized adults with acute and/or chronic illnesses requiring surgery.

title: Clinical Transitions
description: This course is designed to facilitate the transition into professional practice through preceptorship with a registered nurse in a variety of settings. During this course, the student will also complete their Capstone Project (nursing research or quality improvement).

title: Capstone I: Developing a Project Proposal in Nursing
description: This course synthesizes and applies the knowledge and skills students acquired in the theoretical and practical courses in the program through a capstone project focused on nursing, health, or health care.

title: Capstone II: Evidence-Based Quality Improvement/Research Project Completion
description: The final culminating course and the subsequent Capstone project will integrate content from the previous courses. Students will undertake a systematic investigation of a quality improvement need that is either a clinically-based or administration-based problem selected by the student and supported by faculty.

title: Introduction to Medicine
description: Introduction to Medicine is a one-semester introductory course that gives an overview of the Medical Sciences (Pre-Medicine) program and provides students with insight into various aspects of a physician profession.

title: Biology for Medical students I with Lab
description: Biology for Medical Students I with Lab course focuses on the fundamental principles of molecular biology, cell biology, biochemistry and evolution. These principles are introduced at the molecular level: the structure and function of biological macromolecules, how these molecules integrated into the cell, the basics of cellular metabolism, gene replication, expression and evolution. The course provides students with foundation that is essential to understand the basic mechanisms of life on cellular level with further implications for health/disease and biotechnology and includes research laboratory part.

title: Biology for Medical students II with Lab
description: Biology for Medical Students II with Lab builds on NUSM102 to deepen understanding of the molecular logic of life. It integrates molecular and cellular biology, genetics, and biochemistry to explain how cells organize, communicate, proliferate, and die. Topics include membrane dynamics, vesicular trafficking, energy transduction, signaling networks, cytoskeletal organization, cell-cycle regulation, meiosis, apoptosis, and cellular interactions. The course emphasizes clinical and biotechnological relevance to health, disease, and therapy. A required laboratory component provides hands-on experience with modern biochemical, molecular, and cell-biological techniques, reinforcing theoretical concepts and developing experimental and analytical skills.
prerequisite: NUSM 102 Biology for Medical students I with Lab (8491) (D and above)

title: Capstone Project
description: The Capstone Project is a one semester course for third-year Bachelor of Medical Sciences students. The project will help students develop their research skills by designing a research study in the area of biomedical sciences, where students will conduct experiments and collect, interpret, statistically analyze and present the obtained data.
prerequisite: NUSM 301 Introduction to Immunology, Microbiology and Genetics (6958) (C- and above) OR NUSM 302 Introduction to Statistics for Evidence-Based Practice (6959) (C- and above) OR NUSM 303 Introduction to Anatomy and Histology (6957) (C- and above)

title: Introduction to Being a Physician
description: The purpose of this course is to introduce incoming students to what it means to be a physician, with an emphasis on the patient’s experience with chronic disease and the health care system.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C and above)

title: Medical Anatomy
description: Anatomical knowledge remains one of the cornerstones of modern medical practice. This course represents a nine-week program designed to provide an introduction to anatomical and medical terminology and comprehensive coverage of all aspects of human functional and gross anatomy.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C and above)

title: Human Genetics
description: Human Genetics and Molecular Therapeutics course is designed to provide students with general knowledge related to the organization of human genome, structure and function of DNA and RNA, inheritance mechanisms of simple and complex traits.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C and above)

title: Cellular and Pathological Basis of Disease
description: This course is focused on structural and functional properties of cells and tissues in both normal and disease states.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: Fuel Metabolism
description: The Fuel Metabolism course provides the foundation for understanding metabolic processes taking place in the body under various circumstances.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C and above)

title: Immunology in Health and Disease
description: This course will allow students to better understand the functions of the immune system in health and disease and the pathogenetic mechanisms underlying the development of a wide range of diseases associated with the immune system.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: Medical Microbiology
description: The Medical Microbiology course introduces basic concepts of infectious disease, focusing on bacteriology, virology, parasitology, the mechanisms of disease transmission and treatment.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: Pharmacology
description: In this course students will learn about the basic principles and mechanisms of commonly used drugs and how they exert their actions.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C and above)

title: Basics of Medical Interviewing
description: Purpose of this course is to provide a life-like learning environment in which medical students will be able to develop and practice effective medical interviewing skills.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: Basics of Physical Examination
description: This course is dedicated to teaching students to perform a physical examination.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: Basics of Physical Examination
description: This course is dedicated to teaching students to perform a physical examination.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: Evidence-based Medicine I and Biostatistics
description: In the course Evidence Based Medicine 1 students will learn the basic statistical methods and analytical epidemiological reasoning tools to be able to critically interpret and utilize the peer-reviewed medical research literature for medical practice.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: English-Russian-Kazakh Medical Terminology
description: The aim of this course is to make medical students able to switch fluently from English to Russian and Kazakh languages when they will be exposed to the local clinical settings with Kazakh doctors, healthcare professionals and above all patients.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: Medical Ethics and Professionalism
description: This course is designed to begin the exploration of the ethical, and professional issues that define the practice of medicine.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C- and above)

title: Behavioral Medicine
description: In this course, we will introduce part of the philosophical grounding for this claim-the biopsychosocial model-and then we will look at models and methods of behavior change that can help us in the future as we work with patients.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C and above)

title: Evidence-based Medicine II and Biostatistics
description: In this course you will directly apply your knowledge on how to conduct statistical analysis using the statistical software STATA.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C and above)

title: Clinical Experiences
description: In the Clinical Experiences students are observers of medical practice in a range of settings, such as primary care ambulatories, clinics and physicians’ offices.
prerequisite: NUSM 310 Capstone Project (7138) (C and above)

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - High Risk Obstetrics
description: Three Options for the Obstetrical Subinternship will be available. LABOR & DELIVERY SERVICE: This elective will focus on the technical aspects of obstetrics. COMPLICATED PREGNANCY SERVICE: This elective will focus on management of women with complications of pregnancy. PRENATAL DIAGNOSIS SERVICE: This elective will focus on reproductive genetics and obstetrical ultrasound.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Benign Gynecology
description: The student will function similar to an intern on the gynecological service. He/she will spend time on the ward and/or private gynecology services. The subintern will work up patients following admission, examine these patients and establish a differential diagnosis. He/she will assist in the surgical procedures and postoperative care of these patients.

title: Operations Management
description: This course provides an introduction to the field of Operations Management (OM), emphasizing the role of operations in creating and delivering value in both manufacturing and service organizations
prerequisite: BUS 101 Core Course in Business (5889) (C- and above)

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Pediatric Cardiology
description: This four-week elective involves intensive exposure to the diagnosis and management of infants, children, adolescents, and adults with congenital and acquired heart disease (rheumatic fever, myocarditis, etc). Daily evaluation of outpatients challenge the student to make accurate cardiac diagnoses by physical examination and with the help of electrocardiograms, echocardiograms and chest roentgenograms.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Pediatric Endocrinology, Metabolism and Diabetes
description: This four-week elective experience focuses upon (1) the outpatient evaluation of children referred for possible endocrine or metabolic disease, (2) follow-up of children initially evaluated by endocrinology in an in-patient setting and (3) chronic ambulatory therapy of children with endocrine disorders including a significant proportion of pediatric diabetes. Each clinic is supervised by one or more of the full-time faculty members. Students work closely with the pediatric endocrine clinical and research fellows, pediatric residents rotating on the service, endocrine physician assistants and endocrine nurse practitioners.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Pediatrics Infectious Diseases
description: This four-week elective will consist of consultation experience with the main emphasis on infectious disease problems in hospitalized pediatric patients at the Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh. There will be daily rounds with one of the faculty preceptors, as well as participation in departmental and divisional lectures, conferences, rounds and seminars. Ample time is provided for literature review and discussion of representative topics.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Pediatric Nephrology
description: During the four-week elective, emphasis will be placed on independently evaluating patients to learn the clinical-pathological relations of renal diseases and therapeutic principles. Students will interact with patients and families directly with supervision of pediatric nephrology faculty and fellows and have active roles in patient discussion and counseling.

title: University of Pittsburgh Component - Pediatric Gastroenterology
description: Students participate in supervised direct patient contact, and formal didactic instruction. Students on the in-patient service have a chance to see all in-patient consults, follow all hospitalized gastroenterology patients in daily rounds, and follow discharged patients in the Gastroenterology Clinics at Children's. In addition, a close relationship will be maintained with the nutrition team. Students are likely to see patients with intractable diarrhea, inflammatory bowel disease, gastroesophageal reflux disease, biliary atresia, neonatal hepatitis, celiac syndrome, Hirschsprung disease, gastrointestinal bleeding and other rarer disorders of the liver, pancreas and gastrointestinal tract.

title: Beginning Persian I
description: The course is designed for those who have little or no prior knowledge of the Persian language and, therefore, aims to introduce students to the basic grammar, vocabulary, and fundamental structures of written and oral Persian.

title: Intermediate Persian 1
